name: The DigDeep Right to Water Project
mission: DigDeep is a non-profit organization working to ensure that every American has clean, running water forever.

programs.name: The Navajo Water Project
programs.description:
The Navajo Water Project is a community-managed utility alternative that brings hot and cold running water to homes without access to water or sewer lines on the Navajo Nation. 

It's the first system of its kind in the United States.

programs.name: Appalachia Water Project
programs.description:
A hundred years ago, McDowell County, WV was one of the wealthiest communities in the nation. Today, many folks here don’t have access to clean, running water.

The reasons are complicated: 100-year-old water pipes failing, contamination from local mines, the collapse of the local economy. Water access is a critical first step toward protecting the health of our neighbors and putting them back on a road to prosperity.

DigDeep is bringing clean, running water to hundreds of families right now—some for the first time ever—and we’re doing it from within the local community. Residents guide our efforts; our local staff serve their neighbors; and we work in partnership with local government and water utilities, with capacity-building in mind.

programs.name: Colonias Water Project
programs.description:
More than 500,000 people live along the Texas-Mexico border in colonias—neighborhoods without basic services like running water, sewer, electricity, or roads.

Families drive for miles to haul water or buy it at the store. They carefully ration water for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and bathing. But despite their struggle for water, these families still go to work, take their children to school, and lead their communities.

Running water changes everything. DigDeep is on a mission to get the water flowing in colonias across Texas.

leader.name: Mr. George McGraw
leader.profile:
George McGraw is a human rights advocate specializing in the human right to water and sanitation in the US. He currently serves as founder and CEO of DigDeep, the only WASH organization serving disadvantaged communities in the US.
Under George's leadership, DigDeep won the 2018 US Water Prize for its Navajo Water Project, which has brought clean, running water to hundreds of Navajo families. Now George is leading an effort with Michigan State University, the US Water Alliance and the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation to study the root causes of domestic water poverty, which still afflicts some 1.6 million Americans without access to running water or basic sanitation.
George has written on water for The New York Times, The LA Times and The Nation, and spoken at events hosted by the Clinton Foundation, the Atlantic, and Ford. name: CLIMATE ACTION RESERVE
mission: To develop, promote and support innovative, credible market-based climate change solutions that benefit economies, ecosystems and society. The Climate Action Reserve was approved by the California Air Resources Board (ARB) in 2012 to serve as an Offset Project Registry in accordance with the regulations implementing the California cap-and-trade program. The Reserve has had many of the offset projects in its system recognized by the ARB for rewarding early actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and six Reserve offset protocols have been adopted by ARB for use in the compliance offset system under the cap-and-trade program.
ntee_code: C99 - Environmental Quality, Protection, and Beautification N.E.C.

programs.name: Compliance Offset Program under California’s Cap-and-Trade Program
programs.description:
The Climate Action Reserve is approved to serve as an Offset Project Registry (OPR) for the Compliance Offset Program under California’s Cap-and-Trade Program.  As an Offset Project Registry, the Reserve lists offset projects, collects project reporting documentation, facilitates verification, and issues Registry Offset Credits (ROCs) for offset projects being implemented using an Air Resources Board (ARB) Compliance Offset Protocol.  Registry Offset Credits are offset credits issued by an Offset Project Registry under the ARB Compliance Offset Program, which may later be transitioned to ARB Offset Credits.  

The Reserve has also been approved to serve as an Early Action Offset Program. In this role, the Reserve can issue Early Action Offset Credits for greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions and removal enhancements that meet the requirements of the Cap-and-Trade Regulation.  These credits have been issued under ARB-approved voluntary offset protocols and help create an initial supply of offset credits for the Cap-and-Trade Program.  Early Action Offset Credits may not be used to meet a compliance obligation in the Cap-and-Trade Program; however, they may be eligible for transition to ARB Offset Credits to be used for compliance in the Cap-and-Trade Program.

programs.name: Voluntary Offset Project Registry
programs.description: The Climate Action Reserve is a national offsets program focused on ensuring environmental integrity of GHG emissions reduction projects to create and support financial and environmental value in the U.S. carbon market. It does this by establishing high-quality standards for quantifying and verifying GHG emissions reduction projects, overseeing independent third party verification bodies, issuing carbon credits generated from such projects and tracking the credits over time on a transparent, publicly-accessible system. These standards not only ensure the environmental integrity of using offsets, but they also bring credibility and efficiencies to the carbon market by creating a trusted and valuable commodity.

programs.name: Climate Impact Score
programs.description:
Climate Impact Score TM is a pioneering program and decision-making tool that brings transparency and confidence to investments that claim a positive climate impact.

By providing the finance community with easily understood data supported by a rigorous methodology, Climate Impact Score allows stakeholders to assess the greenhouse gas reduction potential of investment products across asset classes. It is the first and only tool that quantifies the greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions from the projects funded by an investment over their lifetime.

name: COALITION TO ABOLISH SLAVERY AND TRAFFICKING
mission: Cast's mission is ending human trafficking through education, advocacy and empowering survivors.

programs.name: Training and Technical Assistance Program
programs.description: CAST’s Comprehensive Training and Technical Assistance (TTA) program is designed to provide expertise and training for service advocates on the full spectrum of legal remedies available to human trafficking victims through individualized technical assistance, in-person training and regular working group calls. CAST TTA is now offering free support to attorneys and social service providers assisting trafficking survivors with legal needs in the following areas of law: immigration, criminal re-entry, reporting to law enforcement, ethics, criminal victim witness advocacy, program support, referrals, civil and more. Through this program, CAST's TTA team established a toll-free hotline and dedicated email to respond to breaking requests for technical assistance from both legal and social service providers. For case specific questions or individualized technical assistance for attorneys and social service providers, contact TTA (email preferred) weekdays between 9 AM – 5 PM PST. Please allow for 48 hours turn-around time.

programs.name: Survivor Leadership Program
programs.description: CAST’s work is directly informed by the real experiences of the clients it serves. The survivor leadership programs, Survivor Advisory Caucus (launched in 2003) and National Survivor Network (launched in 2011), bring together a community of survivors of human trafficking for peer-to-peer mentorship and survivor-led advocacy. Their voices on policy and public awareness have led to the development of stronger protections for victims in both California and federal anti-trafficking laws. By connecting survivors across the country, CAST supports and encourages survivors to realize their own leadership qualities and to value their insight, not just as survivors, but as experts in the field. The accomplishments of the members of the Caucus and NSN, both individually and collectively, over the past year are tremendous. In 2016, nine members were appointed by President Obama to the newly established U.S. Advisory Council on Human Trafficking. The 11-member council advises the President’s Interagency Task Force to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons (PITF) and offers survivor-centered policy recommendations to both the White House and U.S. Congress on federal efforts to combat and prevent human trafficking. Members also participated in policy advocacy efforts at the federal, state and local levels, including: Congressional hearings on the long-term impact of criminalization of human trafficking survivors, state Senate hearings on behalf of CAST-sponsored criminal justice reform legislation and government oversight board meetings on lost income compensation. In addition, CAST's staff and survivor leaders were invited by the Office for Victims of Crime (OVC) to develop the "Survivor Professional Development Training Curriculum," which aims to strengthen the impact survivor advocates across the country can have in the anti-trafficking movement. Equally impressive is the group's media advocacy. Members have shared their unique experiences, impressive accomplishments and remarkable expertise through opinion editorials for CNN, expert commentary on MSNBC and featured profiles by the BBC.

programs.name: Youth Program
programs.description: CAST recognizes the specialized needs of minor and transition age youth (TAY) survivors of human trafficking and developed specific youth-focused programming. Youth services include monthly group activities focused on empowerment, positive experiences and education; comprehensive case management with interventions geared towards youth; and individual assistance navigating various systems, including the Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services and Probation Department, when necessary. In addition, the program offers internships for Transition-Aged Youth (TAY), which seek to build job skills and professional development through direct work experience and mentorship.

programs.name: Shelter Program
programs.description: CAST’s shelters provide physically and psychologically safe housing for trafficking survivors. Through a host of supportive programs and services, they are designed to provide emergency response, and to then help clients establish independence and self-sufficiency, to build community and to expand their own supportive networks. The shelters offer 12+ months of transitional housing, case management, a financial savings program, social and cultural activities, group therapy, supportive counseling and more. Shelter residents are also taught skills in conflict resolution, job training, independent living and financial planning. The shelter is also home to an outdoor sanctuary filled with fruit trees and a garden where residents can plant herbs and spices to use in their cooking and provide a taste of home. Admission is based on safety, current needs and the availability.

programs.name: Social Services
programs.description: Clients come to CAST in a variety of ways, including community- and faith-based organizations (CBOs/FBOs), law enforcement agencies (LEAs), Good Samaritans, and self referrals. Upon intake, the CAST staff assesses for emergency needs, such as housing, clothing, food, and safety, followed by a comprehensive assessment and legal interview that also address safety. Attorneys then evaluate the legal needs and provide each client with the necessary education and information to make an informed choice about how to proceed with their case. Combined social, shelter, and legal services are what continue to set CAST apart. To date, we remain the only organization in the country that offers all three branches of services in-house. We know that victims cannot become survivors without all three—a social service advocate to ensure access to benefits and services and to provide supportive counseling, validation, and normalization; a shelter or housing program to ensure basic necessities are provided; and finally, critical legal services that assist victims in navigating complex criminal, civil, immigration, and other legal proceedings that ultimately deliver the person to full status and work authorization.

programs.name: Legal Services
programs.description: CAST attorneys empower survivors to assert their legal rights and choose appropriate remedies to rebuild their lives. The legal services program works collaboratively with survivors, community-based organizations, public-interest attorneys and numerous government agencies to ensure survivors of human trafficking are provided culturally-sensitive, victim-centered legal representation. Along with its in-house legal team, CAST's pro bono attorneys dedicate their time and talent assisting with immigration advocacy, criminal victim-witness advocacy, civil litigation, family law and cutting edge policy initiatives.

leader.name: Kay Buck
leader.profile: Fueled by her passion for justice, Kay has over 25 years of experience leading anti-trafficking initiatives in the United States and abroad. Joining the Coalition to Abolish Slavery & Trafficking (CAST) in 2003, Kay leads one of the longest-running anti-slavery organizations in the United States, serving thousands of survivors and their families with comprehensive care to rebuild their lives and impact systemic change to prevent human trafficking.  Kay is responsible for opening the first shelter for trafficked women in the country and creating CAST’s one-of-a-kind survivor leadership program, which empowers and trains survivors to use their voices collectively to inform public policy and social change, resulting in better laws to combat trafficking.

name: Climate Resolve
mission:
Our purpose is a just and resilient future.

Climate Resolve builds collaborations to champion equitable climate solutions. We connect communities, organizations and policymakers to address a global problem with local action. We inclusively develop practical initiatives that reduce climate pollution and prepare for climate impacts. Using our collective power to tackle climate change, we are creating a thriving California and inspiring others to act.

programs.name: EnviroMetro
programs.description:
Climate Resolve leads EnviroMetro, an ad-hoc coalition working to realize green transportation policy outcomes in Los Angeles — advocating for green and equitable transit in Southern California. Additionally, Climate Resolve staff sit on Policy and Sustainability Councils at Metro, to ensure the public's access to opportunity and engage in advocacy to make cleaner, more equitable transportation options better for Angelenos. 

At Metro, Climate Resolve led an effort that reformed how street investments are made to align with climate goals and strategies for reducing car dependence. Our budget advocacy bolstered plans to provide high frequency (every 5 to 10 minutes) bus service for 83 percent of trips across LA County. Climate Resolve also pushed the City of LA to adopt targets for providing bus shelters in an equitable way that considers heat exposure and transit ridership above ad revenue potential.

programs.name: Climate Smart Schools
programs.description:
Climate Resolve is leading the Climate Smart Schools (CSS) initiative to help Southern California schools with energy efficiency and water conservation efforts — so schools save money and help California meet its climate targets. CSS enables Southern California school districts and Local Education Agencies (LEAs)  to work together to obtain the maximum dollar savings with allocations of their California Clean Energy Jobs Act (“Proposition 39”) funds. We provide Prop. 39 program assistance, acting as an energy manager for districts; ensuring school districts and LEAs get maximum savings from their Proposition 39 allocations; and making compliance easier.

With our guidance and consultation, Los Angeles and Orange County schools have saved 1.7 million kWh of electricity and 149,000 therms of natural gas through the replacement of old HVAC units with high efficiency units, installation of LED lighting, cool roofs, and energy management systems, as well as redirect stormwater underground.

programs.name: Affordable Housing, Sustainable Communities
programs.description: Providing workshops and technical assistance to applicants for transit-proximal affordable housing development in Southern California.

programs.name: Urban Cooling Strategies for Neighborhoods Serviced by the Orange Line
programs.description: Climate Resolve is producing climate adaptation strategies for the L.A. Bureau of Street Services, which include cool pavements, shade structures, landscaping, and stormwater retention. Climate Resolve is also managing community engagement for the project, including preparing the engagement strategy, creating surveys to collect community input, and holding workshops to encourage community participation and feedback.

programs.name: South El Monte’s Merced Avenue Greenway Project
programs.description: Climate Resolve is collaborating on an environmental services approach to manage stormwater runoff at its source in order to meet regulatory compliance, improve water quality, and enhance watershed health. Climate Resolve provides technical expertise on reducing the urban heat island effect and the project’s carbon footprint, creating new safe bike and pedestrian connections, enhancing public health, and beautifying the neighborhood. Climate Resolve also designs and leads community engagement events to invite public input on greenway components.

programs.name: Ready for Tomorrow
programs.description:
Climate Resolve’s “Ready for Tomorrow” program focuses on helping municipalities face the challenge of climate preparedness in Southern California. Our report and extensive online Excel matrix assess how 200+ municipalities are adopting plans and policies to protect their jurisdictions against climatic threats such as extreme heat, poor air quality, sea level rise, drought, flood, and wildfire. 

Moreover, our Ready for Tomorrow grant writing assistance program has helped disadvantaged vulnerable communities access funding resources to help prepare for climate change. In 2020, we assisted the municipalities of Compton ($50,000), Commerce ($3,240,000), and South El Monte ($205,100) pursue $3.5 million for planning and projects in their neighborhoods. 

Climate Resolve staff are also engaged in continuing efforts to provide supplemental technical assistance to local municipalities who are awarded these funds.

programs.name: Greenhouse Gas Mitigation
programs.description:
California has committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions to 40% below 1990 levels by 2030 and 80% by 2050, and Climate Resolve is committed to finding more ways for Los Angeles to lead California in meeting these targets. This includes work on local mitigation projects to benefit communities, especially low-income communities most affected by climate change.

Climate Resolve offers technical assistance and manages mitigation projects at public buildings, schools, businesses, and homes, including: Energy efficiency retrofits; Zero net energy (ZNE) implementation; Water conservation efforts; Cool roofs and surface implementation

programs.name: Resilience Hubs
programs.description:
Resilience Hubs are multifaceted centers that enhance a community’s capacity to adapt to multiple-climate perils including extreme heat waves, wildfires, floods and more. These spaces democratize sustainable solutions by acknowledging the existing community's resources and expertise, and provide infrastructure to enhance those efforts. 

Hubs are able to respond to the racial and socioeconomic disparities in disaster response by focusing on resilience before disaster. They connect trusted community spaces with resilience resources to promote social cohesion and meet community identified needs at the same time. Climate Resolve staff have been successfully advocating for Resilience Hubs funding at the state level, raising awareness, and helping with the implementation of new hubs throughout LA, including the first-ever resource of this kind in the historic neighborhood of Boyle Heights.

programs.name: California Regional Climate Adaptation
programs.description:
Climate Resolve, in partnership with the California Community Economic Development Association (CCEDA), has developed fact sheets summarizing relevant climate impacts and adaptation strategies for each of California’s nine regions. These fact sheets are intended to assist state and regional governments by highlighting each region’s existing climate action and identify policies and initiatives that can be implemented by each region to further defend climate progress.

Climate Resolve has also assisted the California’s Office of Emergency Services (Cal OES) and the Governor’s Office of Planning and Research (OPR) in putting together the State’s Adaptation Planning Guide (APG). Climate Resolve uses its knowledge of best practices in equity and engagement to influence this statewide resource. The APG is primarily meant to support local governments in their efforts to work with the community to prepare for climate change impacts such as extreme heat, drought, flooding, and wildfires.

programs.name: Community Outreach, Conservation, and Greening
programs.description:
Climate Resolve is working with City Plants and Koreatown Youth + Community Center to manage a tree ambassador program to expand the urban tree canopy in frontline communities that typically face the brunt of climate impacts. The program seeks to improve energy efficiency, increase access to trees, and mitigate the impacts of extreme heat via the cooling effects of a larger tree canopy. This project provides multiple co-benefits including but not limited to: improved water capture locally; increased sequestration of atmospheric carbon; improved air quality; and greater protection from heat-related illness.

We also meet with local LA residents to educate the public about issues relating to climate change. We know that climate change is already here and communities are feeling the environmental, health, and financial impacts. We promote awareness of the dangers of climate change and provide actionable information on strategies to conserve natural resources, save money, and live well.

leader.name: Jonathan Parfrey
leader.profile:
Before founding Climate Resolve, Jonathan Parfrey served as a commissioner at the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power.  is also the immediate past-president of the Los Angeles League of Conservation Voters a founder and Vice Chair of CicLAvia, LARC, and the statewide Alliance of Regional Collaboratives for Climate Adaptation.

Jonathan received the Paul S. Delp Award for Outstanding Service, Peace and Social Justice (1992), and was awarded a Durfee Foundation Fellowship (2002), a Stanton Fellowship (2010), and was appointed a Senior Fellow at the USC Marshall School of Business (2011). He is currently a fellow at the Los Angeles Institute for the Humanities; a member of the State of California Climate Adaptation Technical Advisory Committee (2016); a member of the steering committee for the US Climate and Health Alliance (2016). In April 2016, he was received the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors Chair's Green Leadership Award.

name: Entertainment Industry Foundation
mission: Founded in 1942, the Entertainment Industry Foundation (EIF) is a multifaceted organization that occupies a unique place in the world of philanthropy. By mobilizing and leveraging the powerful voice and creative talents of the entertainment industry, as well as cultivating the support of organizations (public and private) and philanthropists committed to social responsibility, EIF builds awareness and raises funds, developing and enhancing programs on the local, national and global level that facilitate positive social change.
ntee_code: E12 - Fund Raising and/or Fund Distribution

programs.name: Community Grants Program
programs.description: The foundation funds charitable organizations in the greater Los Angeles area, and targets dollars to the areas of greatest need in the greater Los Angeles community

programs.name: Stand Up To Cancer
programs.description: Stand Up To Cancer (SU2C) funds research to develop the newest and most promising cancer treatments to help patients today. A division of EIF, SU2C dramatically accelerates the rate of new discoveries by connecting top scientists in unprecedented collaborations to create breakthroughs. SU2C innovations lead to better cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment, which means that we can help more people diagnosed with cancer become long-term survivors.

programs.name: Know Your Rights Camp
programs.description: Know Your Rights Camp (KYRC), founded by Colin Kaepernick, is advancing the liberation and well-being of Black and Brown communities through education, self-empowerment, mass-mobilization, and the creation of new systems that elevate the next generation of change leaders. Kaepernick leveraged KYRC to house a Legal Defense Initiative for those who have been arrested or are victims of police brutality while fighting injustice across the nation, in addition to providing COVID-19 relief to those disproportionately affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

programs.name: People's Fund of Maui
programs.description: People's Fund of Maui is providing direct financial assistance to Maui community members experiencing devastating losses from the fires in Lahaina and Kula.

programs.name: Olivia Rodrigo Fund 4 Good
programs.description: Olivia Rodrigo’s Fund 4 Good is a global initiative committed to building an equitable and just future for women and girls through direct support of community-based non-profits that champion girls’ education, support reproductive rights, and prevent gender-based violence.

programs.name: DEFY:DISASTER
programs.description: DEFY:DISASTER is the entertainment community’s collective and immediate response to natural disasters. Building on the Entertainment Industry Foundation’s historic commitment to furthering the philanthropic efforts of the entertainment community, the program aims to support immediate and long-term relief with a primary goal of making a powerful and sustainable impact in highly affected areas. In October 2020, EIF reintroduced the full breadth of its disaster relief efforts under the program name Defy:Disaster. The program, which previously operated under the name Music for Relief, is dedicated to providing aid to survivors and communities affected by natural disasters to help them recover and rebuild. Supported by the entertainment community and the public, EIF’s disaster relief program has responded to more than 40 natural disasters, including the COVID-19 pandemic and hurricane and wildfire relief.

programs.name: EIF Careers Program
programs.description: The EIF Careers Program (EIFCP) is creating a more diverse talent pipeline into film and television production careers. The program is led by a collaboration of studios, networks, and career pathway providers and focuses on entry-level, below-the-line opportunities in its first phase. Future efforts will focus on entry-level administrative support.

programs.name: Kevin Love Fund
programs.description: The Kevin Love Fund strives to inspire people to live their healthiest lives while providing the tools to achieve physical and emotional well being. After publicly sharing his own battle with anxiety and depression, Kevin became committed to normalizing the conversation around mental health, opening up the public discussion and empowering people to pursue mental wellness with the same vigor as they do physical health.

programs.name: Social Change Fund United
programs.description: The Social Change Fund United (SCFU) was created by philanthropists, entrepreneurs, and NBA superstars Carmelo Anthony, Chris Paul, and Dwyane Wade to support critical and timely issues impacting the Black community. SCFU focuses on public safety and criminal justice reform, empowering communities of color by expanding access to voting and civic engagement, increasing Black representation in leadership, and building economic equity for Black people through investment in education, employment, wages, and housing. The fund welcomes other individual changemakers and corporate sponsors committed to dismantling systemic racism and helping organizations build critical momentum to create equitable treatment and legislation that fosters justice and equality for all.

programs.name: The Charlize Theron Africa Outreach Project
programs.description: The Charlize Theron Africa Outreach Project (CTAOP) envisions a future where all youth are empowered to live healthy, productive, HIV-free lives around the world. CTAOP was created in 2007 by Charlize Theron, Academy Award winning actor and UN Messenger of Peace, with the hope of making a difference in fighting HIV in her home country of South Africa. Although the geographic scope of CTAOP is Sub-Saharan Africa, South Africa has remained the primary area of focus with the highest number of people living with HIV in the world. CTAOP connects community-based, African organizations to funding, capacity building, and broader resources. This allows these organizations to reach more young people with innovative programs and tools to help keep themselves and their peer safe from the disease. CTAOP supports Program Partners that use community-specific programming to educate, empower, and invest in young people between the ages of 10-20 years old.

name: OutCare Health, Inc
mission: OutCare Health, a 501c3 nonprofit, is leading the charge for LGBTQ+ health equity worldwide, empowering millions of LGBTQ+ individuals with comprehensive resources, support, and education. Our initiatives range from the OutList directory of affirming healthcare providers to mentorship, health equity training, community building, support groups, consulting services, and more. Our vision is to create a world where every LGBTQ+ person has access to quality healthcare and feels empowered to live their healthiest, most authentic life.

programs.name: Provider Health Equity Training
programs.description: OutCare Health’s Health Equity CEU Training equips healthcare professionals, health plans, and organizations with the tools and knowledge needed to deliver affirming care to LGBTQ+ individuals. Covering foundational and advanced topics like trauma-informed care, inclusive communication, and gender-affirming processes, these accredited programs bridge knowledge gaps, reduce disparities, and foster equitable healthcare environments.

programs.name: OutList
programs.description: The OutList is a national directory of LGBTQ+ affirming healthcare providers dedicated to improving access to inclusive and affirming care. By connecting LGBTQ+ individuals with compassionate providers who understand their unique needs, the OutList fosters trust, reduces care disparities, and enhances healthcare experiences. Searchable by location, specialty, and keywords, this robust resource helps LGBTQ+ individuals find affirming professionals who prioritize equitable care.

programs.name: Community Resource Directory
programs.description: OutCare's Community Resource Directory offers a comprehensive database of affirming services across all 50 states. From mental health support and shelters to youth programs and healthcare clinics, this tool connects LGBTQ+ individuals with vital resources tailored to their needs. By centralizing affirming programs and services, the directory simplifies the search for community support and helps individuals access life-changing resources.

programs.name: Mentorship Program
programs.description: OutCare’s Mentorship Program connects LGBTQ+ individuals with affirming mentors who provide support and guidance in education, careers, and personal development. Designed to create safe, welcoming environments, this program fosters personal growth, builds leadership skills, and helps participants achieve their goals through meaningful, one-on-one relationships with experienced mentors.

programs.name: Peer Support
programs.description: OutCare’s Peer Support program offers personalized, one-on-one connections between LGBTQ+ individuals and affirming peer support specialists. These sessions provide emotional support, resources, and guidance for navigating challenges like healthcare access, identity exploration, and personal well-being. Peer Support fosters community, belonging, and empowerment through shared experiences.

programs.name: Care Navigation
programs.description: OutCare’s Care Navigation program provides individualized guidance to LGBTQ+ individuals navigating the complex healthcare landscape. Care navigators offer support in accessing gender-affirming care, connecting with affirming providers, and overcoming systemic barriers. This personalized service ensures LGBTQ+ individuals receive the inclusive and compassionate care they deserve.

programs.name: OutTalk
programs.description: OutTalk is a community-driven webinar series that brings together experts, healthcare leaders, and community members to discuss critical LGBTQ+ health equity topics. From intersectionality to navigating care systems, OutTalk creates a platform for education, dialogue, and advocacy, empowering participants with tools to improve outcomes and advance equity.

programs.name: Research
programs.description: OutCare Health prioritizes research as a cornerstone of its mission to advance LGBTQ+ health equity. By conducting and publishing studies that explore disparities, experiences, and best practices in LGBTQ+ care, OutCare informs healthcare systems, providers, and policymakers to drive evidence-based solutions that improve health outcomes.

programs.name: Prescription Savings Program
programs.description: The Prescription Savings Program helps LGBTQ+ individuals access affordable medications by reducing financial barriers to care. Partnering with national organizations, this initiative ensures that vital prescriptions, including gender-affirming medications, remain accessible to those who need them, supporting better health and well-being.

programs.name: Health Equity Consulting
programs.description: OutCare’s Health Equity Consulting provides tailored solutions to healthcare organizations, health plans, and systems seeking to enhance LGBTQ+ inclusivity. By evaluating processes, delivering customized training, and offering actionable strategies, OutCare equips partners to meet regulatory requirements, embed affirming practices, and promote systemic change.

leader.name: Dustin Nowaskie
leader.profile: Dr. Dustin Nowaskie is a queer, nonbinary psychiatrist who is making waves in the world of LGBTQ+ healthcare. With a deep personal identification and a strong civic commitment, they have dedicated their career to improving the lives of LGBTQ+ individuals. As the President & Chief Medical Officer of OutCare Health, a national nonprofit LGBTQ+ health equity organization, Dr. Nowaskie is at the forefront of providing access to vital LGBTQ+ information, resources, programming, mentorship, education, training, research, and providers for millions across the country.

co_leader.name: Jordan Nowaskie
co_leader.profile: Jordan Nowaskie brings a wealth of experience in strategic integrated marketing, creative concept design, brand strategy, demand generation, marketing analytics, and account-based marketing. With a background in both the healthcare and nonprofit sectors, Jordan's expertise in marketing strategy and analytics drives member activation and engagement. His extensive healthcare experience and passion for solving health equity challenges and making a difference in people's lives shines through his dedication to measuring the impact of initiatives and constantly improving strategies for greater effectiveness.

name: International Institute of Los Angeles
mission: International Institute of Los Angeles (IILA) provides transformative services to refugees, immigrants, and working families by promoting self-sufficiency, strengthening resiliency, and honoring cultural identities. We strive to cultivate an inclusive IILA community where a powerful sense of belonging emboldens each person to foster their well-being. Initially founded in 1914 to assist newly arrived immigrants adjust to life in Los Angeles, we expanded our services over the decades to include a wide array of immigration legal assistance, resettlement of refugees, case management for survivors of human trafficking, free to low-cost child care, nutrition services, transportation subsidies, utility bill assistance and debt resolution, and more.

programs.name: Immigration Legal Services Division
programs.description: ADULT REMOVAL DEFENSE Full representation for immigrants facing a removal hearing in Immigration Court for those seeking asylum, cancellation of removal, or other remedies UNACCOMPANIED MINORS Representation for unaccompanied minors seeking asylum before the USCIS, or in Immigration Court and those same clients seeking Special Immigrant Juvenile (SIJS) orders in either Family Court or Probate Court IMMIGRATION DETENTION Free assistance with bond and detention cases AFGHAN LEGAL REPRESENTATION PROJECT Assistance with asylum applications, family petitions, assistance with SIV applications, TPS applications and other forms of immigration relief for Afghan humanitarian parolees, SIV applicants, asylum seekers and asylees IILA provides a full range of other immigration services. We represent a limited number of these cases free-of-charge and may charge low-cost community prices for applicants who do not qualify for our free services.

programs.name: Child Nutrition Division
programs.description: IILA's Nutrition Division provides child care programs across Los Angeles with healthy meals for children to set them up for a lifetime of health and success. By instilling healthy eating habits from an early age, we can significantly increase children’s chances of avoiding many health issues later in life. Furthermore, optimal health and nutrition can help low-income and underserved children close the achievement gap through better performance at school and in life. We serve meals “family style,” an approach affirmed by experts as the ideal way to help young ones develop social skills that will assist them throughout their lives. IILA serves hot meals that we cook from scratch. Our on-site state-of-the-art commercial kitchen prepares one million freshly-cooked breakfasts, lunches, and snacks each year to child care programs across L.A. By modeling healthy practices and making mealtimes enjoyable and social, we can lay the groundwork for a lifetime of healthy habits.

Before joining IILA in May 2021, she previously worked as the Parish Life Director at Holy Family Church in South Pasadena for 13 years, where she was the first lay person to lead the parish. programs.name: Emergency Response
programs.description: CORE (formerly J/P HRO) acts both quickly and strategically in the face of crisis in order to address immediate needs on the ground, working collaboratively to save lives and empower communities. Amid the COVID-19 pandemic, CORE responded by working throughout the United States, Haiti, Brazil and India to increase testing and access to vaccines. In partnership with local governments and community-based organizations, CORE provided free drive-through COVID-19 testing to vulnerable populations, first responders, and essential workers. Originally founded in response to the devastating 2010 earthquake in Haiti, CORE continues its work in there today and has also responded to hurricanes and floods in the Caribbean, U.S., Pakistan and Puerto Rico; the conflict in Ukraine; the earthquake in Turkey; and the climate and migrant crisis in Brazil.

programs.name: Disaster Preparedness
programs.description: Crisis mitigation means understanding the vulnerabilities that exist before emergency efforts are needed. We build systems that equip at-risk communities with the ability to fight back when faced with disaster. Haiti: In both our rubble removal and construction projects, CORE works with engineers, architects, and builders from the local communities in order to give agency to those we serve. By training individuals in earthquake-safe design and construction, we are able to better prepare and empower communities. Savannah, GA & Gulf States: In response to Hurricanes Florence and Michael in 2018, CORE created a disaster preparedness training program, Savannah Youth Disaster Preparedness Training Program, to address the most urgent community needs in the US gulf states region. Today, we continue to empower young adults from economically challenged neighborhoods and marginalized communities along the hurricane belt so they are able to respond to disaster and support their local communities.

programs.name: Environmental Resilience
programs.description: From hurricanes to wildfires, it’s impossible to ignore climate change’s role in causing natural disasters. We are committed to a future where our environment is no longer at the root of the crisis, but rather a system of support. Haiti Takes Root: Haiti Takes Root (HTR) is an innovative program addressing Haiti’s environmental crisis that targets the broader impact of climate change. In partnership with the World Bank, the governments of Haiti and France, and the Parker Foundation, HTR has developed a 30 year plan to overcome the environmental and economic consequences of climate change in Haiti by focusing on reforestation and supporting local farmers. Puerto Rico: We are collaborating with the Caribbean Climate Smart Action Coalition, a group of experts working to provide an in-depth analysis of food systems and landscapes to build back a stronger, greener, and disaster resilient country.

programs.name: Community Building
programs.description: CORE supports one of the largest municipalities in Port au Prince through education, vocational training, community health, programs targeting women, and a dynamic community space. Building Back Better Neighborhoods: In addition to the immediate relief efforts in Haiti after the 2010 earthquake and 2016’s Hurricane Matthew, CORE has also implemented long term development programs, community planning, and housing and infrastructure rehabilitation projects in the most devastated communities. The University of Haiti Faculty of Sciences Department: Funded by the Qatar Haiti Fund and the Inter-American Development Bank, CORE is rebuilding the previously destroyed classrooms and laboratory buildings, which will benefit 2,215 students, professors, and administrative staff. This effort is comprised of female-led planning, construction, and engineer teams. The School of Hope: CORE founded The School of Hope to provide quality education for children residing in the 60,000-person displacement camp following the devastating 2010 earthquake. As the first school in Haiti to serve children with disabilities, The School of Hope continues to provide equal access to education for children from the most marginalized communities. Integrated Music and Arts Education: Founded on the belief that music is a transformational tool that brings about change in the lives of young people, our program trains teachers and provides technical support on instruments, music and art classes, and working with special needs children. Community Development Campus: The campus serves as a focal point for community members to gather: youth can partake in extracurricular activities, while adults benefit from vocational training to build their careers. Dental Clinic: The dental clinic offers a selection of services for the greater community of Port-au-Prince, from basic teeth cleanings to one of Haiti’s only orthodontic clinics. Women’s Entrepreneurship: Entrepreneurs make significant contributions to their economies by providing jobs and livelihood opportunities; our program has become a critical voice for women’s inclusion in the labor market, empowering local businesswomen and equipping them with the skills to succeed.

leader.name: Mr. Sean Penn
leader.profile:
American actor, activist. Two-time Academy Award winner. 

Original founder of J/P HRO in 2010. Led the charge in mobilizing a powerful network of doctors, emergency workers, and government officials to take immediate action in relief efforts following the devastating earthquake in Haiti.

co_leader.name: Ann Lee

As CEO of CORE, she has overseen the organization’s successful transition into an international response and resilience-building NGO, responding to crises in Ukraine, Turkey, India, Pakistan, Brazil, Puerto Rico and the continental United States.

name: Immigrant Defenders Law Center
mission:
We are a next-generation social justice law firm that defends our immigrant communities against injustices in the immigration system.


ImmDef is fighting against the immigration system's campaign of cruelty against migrants at the border with a focus on assisting children and families.  Access to an attorney for all immigrants involved in deportation proceedings is the first step that we must take to ensure fairness in U.S. immigration courts. Our model of universal representation is built on this principle. It is our long‐term goal to ensure that no immigrant is forced to face an unjust immigration system alone.

programs.name: Children's Representation Project (CRP)
programs.description: Our team provides full‐scale deportation defense, legal representation, legal education, and connections to social services to approximately 3,000 detained or non-detained adults and children in Southern California annually. Unaccompanied minors, are uniquely disadvantaged if unrepresented because they are unlikely to fully understand the deportation process and do not have the skills necessary to defend themselves. Without ImmDef's intervention, children would be forced to appear alone before an immigration judge and defend themselves against a highly-trained Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) attorney.

programs.name: Community Defense Project
programs.description: ImmDef launched the Community Defense Project with the support of the City and County of Los Angeles the City of Santa Ana, and the City of Long Beach in support of immigrant communities facing deportation and ICE imprisonment. Generally, people facing deportation do not get appointed an attorney even if they are detained. Many people in deportation proceedings have valid claims to remain in the United States but find it nearly impossible to present these claims without proper legal representation. ImmDef believes everyone deserves representation, and the Community Defense Project takes a step closer to that reality.

programs.name: National Qualified Representative Program
programs.description: ImmDef’s National Qualified Representative Program represents immigrants in ICE detention who are entitled to court-appointed counsel because of serious mental disorders that render them unable to represent themselves. This model of court-appointed counsel in immigration court is possible thanks to Franco-Gonzalez v. Holder, a class action lawsuit and settlement. This settlement was the first time any U.S. court ruled that a group of immigrants is entitled to government-funded legal representation.  This team advocates on behalf of its clients while they are imprisoned in remote federal facilities and continues to represent them once they are released to their families or guardians in their local communities.

programs.name: Litigation & Advocacy Program
programs.description: ImmDef launched its Litigation and Advocacy Program in 2019 with the goal of creating systemic change to dismantle the systems that seek to deport our clients and separate families. The project specifically focuses on issues related to access to counsel, detention conditions & ending immigration detention, violation of rights of unaccompanied minors, cruel & inhumane treatment of asylum seekers, and systemic violations of due process rights.  This team has developed a robust impact litigation and legal advocacy strategy on select cases in immigration and federal court, both at the initial and appellate level.

programs.name: Cross-Border Initiative
programs.description: Under the Trump Administration and Biden Administration more than 70,000 asylum-seeking human beings were forced back into Mexico under the Migrant Protection Protocols (MPP). This cruel policy forced thousands into the streets of notoriously dangerous border towns and overcrowded shelters with unsanitary conditions while they awaited their asylum hearings. The Cross Border Initiative team represents MPP respondents before Customs and Border Protection and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, seeking their removal from the program and in immigration court. The team works tirelessly to advocate for an end to the MPP program.

programs.name: Post-Conviction Relief Program
programs.description: ImmDef is one of the only nonprofits in California with dedicated staff focused on representation in post-conviction relief. Post-conviction relief gives immigrants the chance to challenge unlawful criminal convictions that are the basis of their removal proceedings in immigration court or otherwise impacting their ability to obtain or maintain lawful immigration status.

programs.name: Deported Veterans Program
programs.description: ImmDef’s Deported Veterans Project represents Veterans of the United States Military seeking to be lawfully repatriated to the United States, the country they served. By serving honorably in the military, immigrants are entitled under the law to expedited naturalization, but it does not happen as often as it should. There are hundreds of thousands foreign born Veterans in the United States and only a minority have been naturalized. The Biden Administration has made the repatriation of deported Veterans a priority through the development of the Immigrant and Military Members and Veterans Initiative. ImmDef is working closely with the initiative to repatriate as many of those who served this country back during this window of opportunity.

name: Farm2People Inc
mission: Farm2People secures local harvests and fights hunger in Greater Los Angeles. We support independent California farmers within 400 miles of Los Angeles -- regionally and locally -- who practice various styles of regenerative agriculture. We prioritize purchasing surplus from underserved, small- and mid-sized farmers. We collaborate along the value chain to delivery these harvests to underserved food seekers in Greater Los Angeles. Farm2People's vision is for a food secure and climate stable Southern California that values dignity on both ends of the food supply chain, starting with the grower.
ntee_code: K99 - Other Food, Agriculture, and Nutrition N.E.C.

programs.name: General Farm2People Sourcing and Delivery Program
programs.description: This action based program is F2P’s fundamental programmatic offering. F2P sources from local, regenerative farms and delivers fresh produce along the cold chain to food insecure communities at no cost to the end recipient. As part of this program, we seek out regenerative practicing farmers who self-report various regenerative and climate-mitigating farming practices. We prioritize farmers in the margins, which is to say priority is given to farm owners who are BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, new to farming (farm established within 5 years) and operating independent farms (non-commodity, non-industrial) within 400 miles of Los Angeles. We pay our farm partners a wholesale market rate for their unsold surplus. Through 3rd party partnerships, we deliver fresh produce to hunger relief partner orgs in LA who distribute, for free, to food insecure individuals in Los Angeles and Orange County.

leader.name: Anna Hopkins
leader.profile: Anna R Hopkins (she/her) is an LA-based chef, food designer and the executive director of Farm2People.org –  a values-driven, nonprofit food hub. On the procurement side, Farm2People provides pathways to sales for farms that are regenerative-practicing, small- and mid-sized, and historically underserved. On the distribution side, Farm2People increases healthy food access in the densely populated area of Greater Los Angeles. Hopkins co-founded Farm2People in 2020 to positively affect Los Angeles foodways.

name: Project:Camp

What this looks like: strong, resilient, interconnected communities where children and parents are no longer traumatized by disaster, but are able to have safety, wellness, and positive memories. We pop up free, trauma-informed day camps to support children and their families in the wake of disasters. We also organize and prepare communities to provide childcare when their communities in impacted by disasters.

programs.description: Project:Camp launches pop-up day camps to provide impactful childcare for families affected by disasters. Our camps provide a space for kids to be kids and process through play. We also help organize communities both before and during disasters to provide critical social-emotional support for children, families, and communities. Our pop-up day camps: Provide free, full-day camp for kids aged 6-16 Run from a dozen kids up to 100+ Incorporate volunteer childcare professionals (teachers, counselors, etc.) All volunteers and camp staff are background checked, vetted, and vaccinated Provide critical social-emotional support with trauma-informed programming Immediately after disasters - Project:Camp Pop-up Day Camps Replicable, adaptable model to give kids tools and resources to process, and gives parents the t

programs.name: Community Disaster Preparation and Organzinging
programs.description: Before disasters strikes - Community Organizing and Preparedness Gather together the right organizations and people, so connections and plans are already ma Natural disasters are increasingly frequent and severe due to the effects of climate change, but emergency response infrastructure isn’t designed to support children. During emergencies, access to free, quality child care is important to support children's mental wellbeing and provides parents with time to process and make necessary plans. But too often this critical component of community recovery is missing. Children process extreme events very differently than adults, and require spaces and solutions unique to them Schools, daycare and other forms of childcare often shut down in the immediate aftermath of large disasters, leaving parents to provide 24-hour care. The National Risk Index shows historically disadvantaged communities are often the hardest hit by disasters, and have high rates of Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs)

leader.name: Mikey Latner
leader.profile: Project:Camp was founded by Mikey Latner, a camp director with decades of experience in youth education, and Ozzie Baron, a strategy and operations expert who has helped organizations start, grow and scale. Mikey and Ozzie are old friends who both had impactful, transformative experiences as campers and counselors at summer camp. In starting Project:Camp, their goal is to provide the same mentorship, humor and sense of belonging that they associate with camp for kids who need it most. The goal isn’t simply to provide a safe space for kids whose lives have been disrupted, but to help them learn, grow and thrive as a result.

name: IT GETS BETTER
mission: It Gets Better exists to uplift, empower and connect LGBTQ+ youth around the globe.

programs.name: Storytelling and Media
programs.description: Storytelling is at the heart of our effort to empower LGBTQ+ youth around the globe. We share stories that inspire hope, stories that nnspark conversations, and stories that can inform and positively influence a sexual orientation and/or gender identity journey. The It Gets Better Project strives to connect daily more than 2.1 million followers across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, TikTok, YouTube, Tumblr, Twitch, LinkedIn, Reddit, and ItGetsBetter.org. Our work has been translated into an award-winning MTV special, a NY Times bestselling book, museum exhibits, and live performances and in 2012 was awarded the Governors Award for use of media to educate and inspire.

programs.name: Global
programs.description: It Gets Better is the world's largest storytelling effort to empower LGBTQ+ youth. Investing in local, like-minded organizations outside the US, It Gets Better brings storytelling and other life-affirming support to communities of LGBTQ+ youth around the globe. Global Affiliates: International affiliates are independent organizations with licenses to do business as It Gets Better in their country. Our team works to provide them with resources including content translations, fundraising opportunities, continuing education, and more. Grants: We have awarded more than $350K in support of storytelling initiatives and/or capacity building efforts to international organizations working to create a better world for LGBTQ+ young people. Summits: We host annual multi-day summits packed with workshops, panels, networking opportunities, and more to support the continuing education of LGBTQ+ activists championing the needs of LGBTQ+ young people everywhere.

programs.name: It Gets Better EDU
programs.description: It Gets Better EDU exists to ensure that our uplifting and informative stories reach LGBTQ+ youth and their peers wherever learning takes place. With an impactful youth ambassador program, student-driven grantmaking initiatives, and a growing library of free educational resources for educators and student leaders, thousands of middle and high school students engage with It Gets Better EDU programming every year.

leader.name: Brian Wenke
leader.profile:
Brian Wenke is the Executive Director of the It Gets Better Project and has led the global storytelling effort to empower LGBTQ+ youth since 2016. He has successfully leveraged corporate and institutional partnerships to expand the It Gets Better Project’s reach, which now spans 18 countries and six major languages. His expertise has been featured in major publications including Ad Age, ELLE, Vanity Fair, and Forbes and he has spearheaded multi-national campaigns to connect and engage with LGBTQ+ youth where they live, work, and socialize.

Prior to the It Gets Better Project, Brian raised more than $25 million to tackle issues associated with healthcare disparities (American Cancer Society), global conservation efforts (Greater Los Angeles Zoo Association), and affordable housing and access to the arts (Art Share LA). Brian is a proud alumnus of the University of Cincinnati, College Conservatory of Music (BFA) and Brandman University (MBA), and currently resides in Los Angeles.

programs.name: The Imprint
programs.description: The Imprint is a national nonprofit online news outlet covering child welfare and youth justice. Produced by a diverse group of staff reporters and freelance writers, The Imprint's daily news stories, expert columns and op-eds provide in-depth coverage of the people, policies and practices that land children in foster care and criminal courts — systems affecting families and communities that are too often overlooked in our society.

programs.name: Youth Voices Rising
programs.description: Youth Voices Rising (YVR) is a media and journalism training program for those impacted by the child welfare system with juvenile justice and/or homelessness experience. YVR seeks to bridge the gap between impacted youth, providing young people safe spaces to amplify their voices and strengthen conversations for system change. Fostering Media Connections launched the program in 2016 to help youth gain the skills and confidence they need to articulate the policy and practice changes needed to improve the system, because they are the experts on what solutions might work. All participants are paid for their work.

programs.name: Fostering Families Today
programs.description: An award-winning bi-monthly print and online magazine that is distributed to almost 30,000 readers all resource families and kin caregivers across the country. This magazine ensures caregivers are educated about the latest developments in trauma-informed care, and provides them with an opportunity to earn continuing education credits through reading comprehension.

programs.name: SafeCamp Audio
programs.description: SafeCamp Audio, a podcast network producing and promoting quality audio content on child welfare, youth justice and youth homelessness.

leader.name: John Kelly
leader.profile: John Kelly is co-executive director of Fostering Media Connections and the senior editor of its daily website, The Imprint. Kelly is the founding editor of The Imprint and has been reporting and editing coverage of youth services since 2001, and is passionate about connecting these fields to quality, independent journalism. He writes Youth Services Insider, a regular column that focuses on national issues and federal policy, and produces The Imprint Weekly Podcast.

co_leader.name: Christie Renick
co_leader.profile: Christie Renick (she/her/hers) is co-executive director overseeing programs and operations for FMC. Christie’s background is in nonprofit management, marketing, writing and communications. She holds an MPA from the University of Southern California and an MFA in Creative Nonfiction from the University of Idaho. She completed her undergraduate studies in sociology and writing at Northland College, an environmental liberal arts college located on the shores of Lake Superior. Christie became interested in child welfare, and particularly in the experiences of transition-age youth in foster care, because of her mother’s experience as a foster youth aging out of the system in the 1970s. Christie joined the FMC team in 2013, serving as a reporter, then managing editor and later vice president overseeing FMC’s operations.

name: Coalition for Responsible Community Development
mission: Our mission is to support local business growth, promote economic development, and foster sustainable opportunities that benefit both new and legacy businesses. CRCD's mission is to better sustain, coordinate, and improve local planning, development, and community services addressing the needs of low-income residents and small businesses in South Los Angeles.

programs.name: South Los Angeles All In (SLAAI)
programs.description: SLAAI is a cross-sector, data-driven, anti-poverty initiative aiming to: (1) ensure a just and equitable recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic, recognizing South LA’s unique vulnerabilities and the disproportionate impact of the crisis; and (2) empower residents and local businesses to benefit from the influx of investment and development destined for Los Angeles in preparation for the 2028 Olympics. CRCD launched SLAAI in 2023 and works in collaboration with diverse public, private, and South LA community-based partners. Priorities include: 1. Good Jobs 2. Homelessness 3. Affordable Housing 4. Access to Capital 5. Education 6. Social Infrastructure

programs.name: Youth Development
programs.description: CRCD believes that education and workforce development go hand-in-hand. CRCD provides comprehensive workforce development, leadership/life skills, mentoring, job training, and educational programs to local youth ages 16-24 through CRCD Academy (an accredited alternative high school), a City of LA-funded YouthSource Center, a US DOL-contracted YouthBuild program, an alternative sentencing / restorative justice program, and more. Youth in CRCD programs attend Los Angeles Trade-Technical College to earn industry-recognized credentials (Home Builders Institute, Multi-Craft Core Curriculum) in construction classes and participate in hands-on training by building affordable housing and completing other construction/beautification projects in the neighborhood. Our access to paid work experience and training, education, and personal development support youth in their successful transition to meaningful careers, college, advanced training, career pathways, and alternative sentencing.

programs.name: Education
programs.description: CRCD believes that education and workforce development go hand-in-hand. Our youth programs focus on out-of-school youth, ages 16-24, who are out of work and out of school while facing challenges that traditional institutions cannot accommodate. We provide access to high school education at CRCD Academy (an accredited high school), with co-enrollment and career-path training at partner Los Angeles Trade-Technical College to help young people ages 16-24 reduce barriers to employment and build careers. CRCD also operates the VCN YouthSource Center to provide youth and young people with access to paid work experience and training, education, and personal development to successfully transition to meaningful careers, college, advanced training, career pathways, and alternative sentencing.

programs.name: Workforce Development - Adults
programs.description: CRCD operates a variety of workforce programs for adults over the age of 18, through our hub, the Vernon-Central/LATTC WorkSource Center (an America Job Center) located on the campus of Los Angeles Trade-Technical College. We connect out-of-work residents, dislocated workers, veterans, and the formerly incarcerated with wraparound employment, training, financial education, and coaching services. CRCD endeavors to identify employment pathways and provide individuals with opportunities to succeed in a career with family-sustaining wages. We assist with resume building, workshops, interview preparation, host employment job fairs, and one-on-one financial coaching. The Multi-Craft Core Curriculum (MC3) provides paid training to individuals interested in pursuing a career in construction and connects them with union apprenticeship pathways upon completion.

programs.name: Housing and Support Services
programs.description: CRCD develops and operates permanent supportive housing for youth and young adults, families, seniors, individuals with special needs, and other low-income households. We provide on-site support services to residents of its permanent supportive housing complexes to promote economic self-sufficiency, housing stability, and overall well-being. CRCD serves as the Regional Coordinator in the County of LA Coordinated Entry System (CES) for Youth in South LA, which aims to address the homeless epidemic in Los Angeles. We focus on finding housing resources that best fit each individual’s needs while providing wrap-around case management services including transportation support, life-skills training, and basic needs provisions. We also operate Ruth’s Place, a drop-in center for young people ages 18-24 experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity, where we can address basic needs and provide assistance with housing and access to services.

programs.name: Real Estate Development - CRCD Partners
programs.description: CRCD's direct response to the needs of our service area is the development of permanent supportive & affordable housing for vulnerable populations, including youth (ages 18-24), seniors, veterans, and low-income families. In 2007, CRCD began collaborating with partners to develop affordable and permanent supportive housing, we currently own and operate 9 developments with 463 units of affordable and permanent supportive housing, representing a combined investment of $350 million in South LA housing, a commercial space for our social enterprise, and a drop-in center for homeless youth, Ruth’s Place. CRCD has another $711 million in pre-development, accounting for an additional 996 units of permanent and supportive housing, with a quarter of those set aside specifically for transition-age youth and families experiencing homelessness in addition to on-site case management services and program facilities.

programs.name: CRCD Enterprises
programs.description: CRCD created a social enterprise out of its Neighborhood & Community Beautification Department in 2012 to create jobs for youth in South LA. CRCD Enterprises provides workforce development and on-the-job training for individuals who have barriers to employment, including lack of high school diploma, involvement in the justice and/or foster care systems, homelessness and/or unstable housing, and other challenges. The Enterprise provides the community and LA County with graffiti abatement, commercial & residential painting, bulky item pick and hauling, facilities maintenance, & logistics services, built upon the strengths of CRCD’s experience with neighborhood beautification & workforce development. In 2022, CRCD Enterprises is now a licensed general contractor who also provides commercial/residential painting and facilities management, including graffiti abatement, business district maintenance, office maintenance, unit turnover services, and related services.

programs.name: Economic Development - Small Business Support
programs.description: CRCD operates the Southeast LA BusinessSource Center and the Business Empowerment Center, which provide free and cost-effective tools and support for resident entrepreneurs and small business owners in the South LA community. We aid in one-on-one consulting, business education courses, and programs such as the Entrepreneur Training Program, tax incentives and credits, and small business loan financing. We are committed to helping residents build and grow their businesses and remain competitive within the City of Los Angeles. CRCD assists small businesses to get and stay competitive in our changing neighborhood; over the next 5-10 years, more than $1B in planned development endangers the legacy small business and family/immigrant population (90% Hispanic, 10% Black) with a typical pattern of displacement. CRCD's economic development services are designed to help local businesses to grow.

leader.name: Mark Wilson
leader.profile:
Mark Anthony Wilson, Jr. co-founded CRCD in 2005 along with Ruth M. Teague, Noemi Soto, Fernando Miranda, and Hugo Ortiz. Mark served as CRCD’s Executive Director for a decade and now serves as President & CEO. Raised in South LA, Mark previously served as the Director of the Youth Empowerment Project with the Southern Christian Leadership Conference/Martin Luther King Legacy Association, and the Director of Community Development with the Dunbar Economic Development Corporation.

Today, Mark directs CRCD’s comprehensive community development services in housing, education, and jobs for primarily Latino and African American youth ages 16–24 in the Vernon-Central Los Angeles community. He provides leadership on local and national levels to improve the policies, systems, and long-standing neighborhood conditions that impact young people’s lives.

She recently joined the Los Angeles Fire Department Foundation as the new president and is excited to apply her skills to benefit the public safety arena. Prior to this position, Lin was employed by Center Theatre Group (Ahmanson Theatre, Mark Taper Forum, Kirk Douglas Theatre) for 15 years and oversaw corporate philanthropy, donor communications, and was part of a senior development team responsible for board recruitment and major gifts acquisition. For over nine years, Lin worked for the American Heart Association and served in various capacities including overseeing regional communications, implementing cause-related campaigns, and managing national corporate accounts. In her spare time, Lin enjoys traveling, reading, and spending time with friends, family, and animals.

name: LAST CHANCE FOR ANIMALS
mission: Last Chance for Animals (LCA) is an international, non-profit organization dedicated to eliminating animal exploitation through education, investigations, legislation, and media attention.  LCA believes that animals are highly sentient creatures who exist for their own reasons independent of their service to humans; they should not be made to suffer for the latter.  LCA opposes the use of animals in food and clothing production, scientific experimentation, and entertainment and promotes a cruelty-free lifestyle and the ascription of rights to non-human beings.
ntee_code: D20 - Animal Protection and Welfare (includes Humane Societies and SPCAs)

programs.name: Campaigns & Investigations
programs.description: LCA strives to educate the public about animal cruelty through websites, brochures, email alerts & mailings. These tools are valuable resources for the public as they contain information on a variety of animal rights issues, encourage readers to take action and provide an opportunity to update members about LCA activities. LCAs website, www.LCAnimal.org, receives over 700,000 hits per month.LCAs e-mail action alerts contain "Calls to Action about issues needing urgent attention. LCA, often referred to as the "FBI of Animal Rights, is known for its Special Investigation Unit (SIU) that conducts in-depth investigations to expose horrible cruelty of animals.  The SIU team focuses on validating information, exposing illegal activities and reporting them to authorities for prosecution.  The information obtained is used to develop campaigns, provide education and outreach to the public, and to help in drafting or enforcing legislation that brings lasting changes for animals.

programs.name: Investigations
programs.description: LCA, often referred to as the "FBI of Animal Right,, is widely known for its Sam Simon Special Investigation Unit (SIU) that conducts in-depth investigations to expose horrible cruelty and misuse of animals.  The SIU team focuses on validating information, detecting suspect activity, exposing illegal or unethical activities and reporting them to local, state and federal authorities for prosecution.  The information obtained in LCAs investigations is used to develop campaigns, provide grassroots education and outreach to the public, and to help in drafting legislation that will bring lasting changes for the animals.  The scope of LCAs investigations includes, but is not limited to: pet theft, class "B animal dealers, puppy mills, pound seizure, circus cruelty, elephants in captivity, vivisection and the dog meat trade in South Korea.

leader.name: Chris DeRose
leader.profile:
For over three decades, Chris has been a leader in the animal rights movement, and an inspiration and consultant to countless other individuals and groups dedicated to the animal cause.  In 1984, he founded LCA, an international, nonprofit animal advocacy organization focused on investigating, exposing, and ending animal exploitation.

Inspired by Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King, Jr., Chris has fought all of his battles non-violently and has spent time in jail for his peaceful actions.  One tactic that rocked the foundation of animal experimentation was a daring daytime break-in at UCLA's Brain Research Institute, documented by a film crew to show the shocking truth of animal research.  The 1988 UCLA break-in footage aired around the world.

In 1997, Chris released his autobiography, In Your Face, reporting on his life and his values on compassion. The book was the final achievement that earned him the prestigious Courage of Conscience International Peace Award.
