name: OPERATION HOPE, INC.
mission: Operation HOPE (HOPE) is the leading global provider of financial dignity education and economic empowerment programs for low- or moderate-income youth, individuals and families in underserved communities. HOPE serves three core constituencies as articulated in our five-year Strategic Plan: Youth in underserved schools; low-income adults in underserved communities; and families who have been affected by either natural or man-made disasters. Our Mission is to expand economic opportunity in underserved communities through financial education and career empowerment by offering programs that create financial stakeholders. Our overarching vision is financial inclusion and financial literacy leading to long-term financial dignity for all.
contact_title: Sr. Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer

programs.name: Banking on Our Future
programs.description: The mission of the Banking on Our Future (BOOF) program is to execute a global delivery system for financial education for youth ages 9-18 at no cost to school districts, with a focus on urban, under-served communities. The program consists of five modules, I. Basics of Banking and Financial Services, II. Checking & Savings Accounts, III. The Power of Credit, IV. Basic Investments, and V. Dignity that are taught by volunteer HOPE Corp members who are trained to break down their knowledge of banking and credit into terms that youth can understand and utilize immediately. In addition to financial education, the students are left with a message of empowerment, a message of responsibility, and most important, a message of HOPE.

programs.name: HOPE Inside
programs.description: We currently have a national network of 27 HOPE Insides in key metro markets in the U.S. (expected to grow to 40 by the end of 2015). Some, but not all, HOPE Insides provide Small Business and Entrepreneurship Training, targeting aspiring entrepreneurs, minority- and women-owned small businesses with 1-15 employees. We identify low-income communities and outreach to individuals earning less than $50,000 a year. Participants are encouraged to enroll in Credit and Money Management, Credit Counseling, and Small Business Technical Assistance to ensure they are equipped to handle the financial challenges of operating a small business. Like many other financial literacy nonprofits, the mission of HOPE is to educate and empower. The difference is that HOPE connects that empowerment and education directly to the personal banker-- directly to that new bank account, to that loan officer, and to the start of a relationship with a financial institution that could potentially last a lifetime.

programs.name: HOPE Coalition America
programs.description: HOPE Coalition America’s (HCA) disaster recover services prepares communities, businesses, families and individuals before disasters strike, helps individuals and communities navigate through disasters, and offer guidance and encouragement to recover financially as soon as possible after disasters. HCA focuses on building community resiliency, one resident and one business at a time. As individuals return to productive financial lives, communities are restored. HCA collaborates with local Long Term Recovery Groups and Committees (LTRC), City, County and State Emergency Preparedness agencies, Federal agencies, Volunteer Organizations Active in Disaster (VOAD), faith-and community-based organizations, and national response groups. Working hand-in-hand with these organizations we support individual communities by identifying the unmet needs of their residents and creating appropriate solutions for recovery. Additionally, we work with local businesses and community-based organizations to coordinate outreach and educational events, combine resources, and share best practices. Our staff conducts training seminars on financial recovery and pre-disaster preparation to build sustainable capacity and resilience within these organizations. HCA's partnership with FEMA allows HCA volunteers and employees access to Federal Disaster Recovery Centers, thus enabling them to directly reach out to recovering individuals and provide support services when and where they are most needed. FEMA refers registered individuals requiring assistance to HCA. Through our long-standing relationship with the American Red Cross, HCA also reaches out to survivors at Red Cross shelters and other emergency locations. Whereas FEMA only deals with Presidentially declared disasters the Red Cross responds to disasters of all sizes. HCA has experience responding to both large and small disaster events, serving a range of financial recovery needs.

programs.name: HOPE Business in a Box Academies
programs.description: HBIABA are small learning communities organized around an entrepreneurial/ financial/career theme. The program is designed to provide financial education, technical and academic skills while enhancing engagement and performance in school. Overall, participants who understand the consequences of their early financial decisions tend to make a successful transition to secondary and postsecondary education and, later, a career, or start their own businesses. The program operates on a school level, with a specific structure and curriculum, and on a community level, through business role models and job opportunities with local employers. Phase I. Financial Inclusion: youth participate in the Banking on Our Future program. This program focuses on the development of the following skills: personal finance, creating a budget, banking products, responsible borrowing, credit and investments. Phase II: Entrepreneurial Education: youth participate in HBIABA entrepreneurship course that educates them on various aspects of business including how to write a business plan and manage a budget. In the entrepreneurial course students participate in a business pitch event during which they have 120 seconds to pitch the business ideas developed during the course. Criteria for winning the business pitch include the following: commitment, clarity of vision, work ethic, business plan, and viability of business. Next, students that win the pitch events are then partnered with a Business Role Model from their community. The students spend 10 weeks working with their Business Role Model developing their business plan. At the end of the 10-week business mentoring period, students present their final business plans to HOPE staff. HOPE then rewards students a Business Start-Up Grant of up to $500 dollars to get their enterprise going and are given the opportunity to post their business on the HOPE NYSE Crowdfunding site for additional start-up funding.

programs.name: HOPE Fellows, Interns and Loaned Executives (FILE)
programs.description: The mission of the Operation HOPE Fellows, Interns and Loaned Executives (FILE) program is to educate and empower the next generation of silver rights leaders, while supporting HOPE departments as they work to increase financial inclusion. Recognizing talent and passion, FILE challenges students and recent graduates to grow both personally and professionally and to build on their leadership potential. Through hands-on projects and various development activities, HOPE Fellows and Interns are provided the opportunity to learn and to become effective leaders in their communities.

leader.name: John Bryant
leader.profile: Mr. Bryant is founder, chairman and CEO of Operation HOPE, and the Bryant Group Companies, Inc. He is author of the new bestseller, How the Poor Can Save Capitalism, ranked on Amazon’s and Apple iTunes Top 10 List.  Endorsed by former President Bill Clinton, with a foreword by legendary civil rights leader Andrew Young, the book offers a free enterprise approach to solving the problem of poverty.

co_leader.name: Brian Betts

Prior to joining Operation HOPE, Brian worked specifically in the nonprofit industry for over 10 years, specializing in developing accounting systems and implementing processes to streamline accounting functions while adhering to federal and state requirements. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Tennessee and earned a Master’s degree in Business Administration at the University of Memphis. He has active CPA licenses in both Tennessee and Georgia.  Brian Betts joined the organization in 2018.

name: Environment California Research & Policy Center
mission: Environment California Research & Policy Center is dedicated to protecting California's air, water and open spaces. We investigate problems, craft solutions, educate the public and decision makers, and help Californians make their voices heard in local, state and national debates over the quality of our environment and our lives.
ntee_code: C05 - Research Institutes and/or Public Policy Analysis

programs.name: 100% Renewable Energy
programs.description:
Burning oil, gas and coal has not only polluted our air, water and land for decades; now it’s changing our climate even faster than scientists predicted it would. We can have healthier communities and a livable future for kids growing up today, but to get there, we first need to transform the way we produce and consume energy.

That's why, alongside our national network, we’re calling on communities, colleges and universities, corporations and other businesses, and our state governments to commit to 100% renewable energy. 

It’s a big, bold goal, one that would make America a world leader in the race toward a cleaner, healthier future — and it’s a goal that’s 100% possible.

programs.name: Conservation
programs.description:
We live in a world of incredible material abundance, but we’re running short on nature. We want more places where we can hike, bike and jog among trees and wildflowers. We want more mountaintops where we can see nothing but forest below, more rivers that flow wild and free, more shoreline where all we can hear are waves. We want more wildlife in our world, from the grizzly on the ridgeline to the bee in our garden, from the wolf in the forest to the butterfly in our backyard. We want and need more, to paraphrase Emerson, of a world so beautiful that we “can hardly believe it exists.”

That’s why Environment America Research & Policy Center is running campaigns for more open spaces, more wild places and more wildlife, including protecting pollinators and moving away from single-use plastic.

programs.name: Protecting Our Coast and Ocean
programs.description: Our coast is incredible. Whether taking in the sandstone cliffs of La Jolla Cove, taking a weekend camping trip to Big Sur or watching whales swim along Point Reyes, every inch of our shoreline offers something special. That is why we worked hard to expand California’s federally protected coastal landscape, the California Coastal National Monument, to include the 1,600 acres of the Stornetta Public Lands on the north coast. Now, we're working to stop offshore drilling and other dangerous industrial developments off our coast and ocean.

leader.name: Ms. Laura Deehan
leader.profile: Laura directs our work to tackle global warming, protect the ocean and fight for clean air, clean water and open spaces. Most recently, she directed the public health program for CALPIRG, another organization in The Public Interest Network, where she led campaigns to get lead out of school drinking water and toxic chemicals out of cosmetics. Laura ran Environment California citizen outreach offices across the state and as the Environment California Field Director, led campaigns to get California to go solar, ban single use plastic grocery bags and go 100% renewable. Laura lives with her family in Richmond, California where she enjoys hiking, yoga and baking.

name: CONSUMER WATCHDOG
mission:
Consumer Watchdog is a nonprofit organization dedicated to providing an effective voice for taxpayers and consumers in an era when special interests dominate public discourse, government and politics. We deploy an in-house team of public interest lawyers, policy experts, strategists, and grassroots activists to expose, confront, and change corporate and political injustice every day, saving Americans billions of dollars and improving countless lives. For decades, Consumer Watchdog has been the nation's most aggressive 
consumer advocate, taking on politicians of both parties and the special interests that fund them.
ntee_code: R99 - Civil Rights, Social Action, and Advocacy N.E.C.

programs.name: Healthcare Reform and Patient Protection
programs.description: Consumer Watchdog fights to protect patients, improve health care quality and create universal care. We believe the health of patients should come before the financial wealth of HMOs, drug companies and other health care corporations. We work toward a safer, affordable health care system by eliminating waste, fraud and profiteering.

programs.name: Insurance Reform (Property & Casualty)
programs.description: For more than 20 years, Consumer Watchdog has been the nation's leading property and casualty insurance reform organization. We have saved consumers tens of billions of dollars on auto and home insurance, developed innovative consumer programs, such as the California Low Cost Auto Insurance Program, and reversed some of the most anti-consumer insurance policies in the industry.

programs.name: Consumer Privacy
programs.description: Consumer Watchdog works to increase consumer privacy online .

programs.name: Cleaner, Cheaper Energy Project
programs.description: To keep our society running, we need to fight for affordable electricity and gasoline. To keep our planet running, we need to aggressively pursue alternative fuels. Cleaner, cheaper energy is an essential victory for American consumers. Consumer Watchdog monitors the power and oil companies that too often stand in the way.

programs.name: Keeping Politicians Honest
programs.description: Consumer Watchdog fights to make your voice heard by exposing the influence of the special interests and the politicians that do the bidding of those interests. From Sacramento to Washington D.C., we follow the money trail from big donors to policymakers and track bad public policy back from politicians to those donors.

name: DEFINE AMERICAN
mission: Define American empowers diverse and nuanced storytelling about immigrant experiences across mediums, sectors, and industries.

programs.name: Amplifying Immigrant Storytellers and Stories About Immigrant Experiences
programs.description: Amplify and lead a platform for storytellers and stories that serves as the pre-eminent public voice for storytelling about immigrant experiences. By emphasizing the voices of immigrant storytellers and stories about immigrants, we will diversify and enrich the dialogue around immigration and activate the resource hub.

programs.name: StoryLab
programs.description: Build and curate an accessible resource hub that activates storytelling across mediums, sectors, and industries. This Program aims to simplify the overwhelming landscape of information, offering tailored support from self-service resources to technical assistance partnerships, accessible to a diverse audience spanning Hollywood, publishing, theater, and beyond.

programs.name: Research
programs.description:
At the core of our organization is a transformative research program
that combines innovative insights with real-world applications, all
while ensuring that our research is high-quality, useful, and original.
Our research collaborations help ensure that our projects resonate
with community needs, embodying our ethos of "building with" rather
than "building for." We also ensure our research is not duplicative of
past insights, but rather actively works to fill knowledge gaps in our
field through innovative approaches.

leader.name: Jose Antonio Vargas
leader.profile: Jose Antonio Vargas is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, Emmy-nominated filmmaker, and Tony-nominated producer. He is a leading voice for the human rights of immigrants and the Founder of Define American. His best-selling memoir, Dear America: Notes of an Undocumented Citizen, was published by HarperCollins in 2018. Most recently, he co-produced Heidi Schreck’s acclaimed Broadway play What the Constitution Means to Me, which was nominated for two 2019 Tony awards, including “Best Play.”

name: Team Rubicon
mission: Team Rubicon is a veteran-led humanitarian organization that serves global communities before, during, and after disasters and crises.
ntee_code: M20 - Disaster Preparedness and Relief Services

programs.name: Long-Term Recovery Services (Rebuild)
programs.description: Team Rubicon’s Houston Rebuild Program concluded in 2024, after successfully helping 129 local families return home in the years following Hurricane Harvey in 2017. Team Rubicon has also conducted rebuild operations throughout seven additional disaster-impacted communities in the U.S. and Puerto Rico, assisting a total of more than 794 families rebuild their homes and repair their roofs. Team Rubicon’s Rebuild Program continues today at sites in Southeast Louisiana and Western Kentucky. The program aims to serve additional communities in need of rebuild and repair services following future disasters throughout the U.S.

programs.name: Volunteer Training and Engagement
programs.description: Team Rubicon provides year-round, online and in-person trainings and engagements to support our veteran community and improve our disaster operations. Our 180,000+ volunteers train to serve local communities in need and connect with other volunteers. Trainings range from “Flood Prevention and Sand Bagging Techniques” to “Site Survey” which teaches volunteers how to assess a home/property for damage or risk. These opportunities decentralize and expand the resources available to residents most at risk of disasters, ensuring they can live resiliently through future challenges.

programs.name: Disaster Operations
programs.description: Team Rubicon’s volunteers deploy to serve communities impacted by disasters like tornadoes, hurricanes, and other events. The following are services included in the disaster operations program: site surveys, expedient home repair (roof tarping and boarding windows), mucking and gutting out flooded homes, route clearance and debris management/removal (chainsaw and heavy equipment services).

programs.name: Veteran Reintegration
programs.description: Utilizing veterans' unique skills and experience increases the efficacy of our disaster response efforts while providing veterans the opportunity to rediscover their sense of purpose, community, and identity they need to transition successfully to civilian life.

programs.name: Medical Care (International)
programs.description: Medical volunteers serve with Team Rubicon’s Emergency Medical Team (EMT) Type 1-Mobile to provide primary and emergency medical services to international communities impacted by disasters and humanitarian crises. Teams can deliver emergency medical/trauma care and stabilization, provide inter-agency and emergency management coordination, and assist with the creation and organization of patient transport systems management. In addition to Emergency Medicine, TR medical teams can re-establish primary healthcare for chronic conditions and preventable diseases and coordination care for complex medical conditions.

name: Painted Brain
mission: Painted Brain creates lasting community-based solutions to mental health challenges and the impact of social injustice through arts, advocacy, and enterprise.

programs.name: Painted Brain Community Mental Health & Wellness Programs
programs.description: Painted Brain’s primary mission in regards to the mental health system is to introduce community back into the community mental health system. We do this via art groups. Our groups integrate art activities to get people talking, interacting and having fun with each other. We bring art groups to agencies and communities in need of communal activity and shared purpose. We are tackling one of the most pervasive challenging people living with mental illness in our society, isolation. Art is a conduit to interaction, and art groups help us relearn that we want to be social, we want to interact, we can enjoy being with other people. Humans are fundamentally social creatures, and art facilitates safe socializing.

leader.name: Rayshell Chambers
leader.profile: Rayshell Chambers was born to serve! With a Bachelor’s Degree in Sociology and Master’s Degree in Public Administration, she has devoted her personal and professional life to acquiring knowledge and skills necessary to address the most complex public policy issues affecting the human condition.

name: Small Acts for Good
mission: Opportunity is Power. UpWorks for Good’s mission is to connect, engage and empower networks of civic-minded volunteers to design and create extraordinary good in local communities, everywhere.

programs.name: Volunteering
programs.description:
At UpWorks for Good we encourage and promote volunteerism. We believe the act of volunteering, no matter how small, can bring positive change to communities, everywhere.

UpWorks offers a wide range of custom curated volunteer experiences supporting at-risk communities with much needed resources. We can also partner with other nonprofits to support their volunteer needs.

programs.name: Volunteer Ambassador Program
programs.description: An UpWorks for Good seasoned, “pro” volunteer person ready to take that next step and new challenges can become an UpWorks for Good Volunteer Ambassador. A "pro" volunteer can partner with UpWorks for Good to develop an impactful and engaging UpWorks Volunteer Event. An event that generate funds, raises awareness and creates real opportunity.  We are here to guide, mentor and help create success.

programs.name: Nonprofit Partnership Opportunities
programs.description: UpWorks for Good partners with local, ambitious, likeminded community groups and organizations in an effort to provide the best in volunteer services and maximize impact.

programs.name: Corporate Team Volunteering Events
programs.description: Corporations can be such a force for good! We work with strong, socially conscious corporations to produce impactful volunteer events.

programs.name: Event Management Services
programs.description: Galas and events are among the strategic lifeforce of successful nonprofit organizations. We help nonprofits bring their events - live or virtual - to life!

name: A. Milton Miller Memorial Fund, Inc. dba Disability Rights Legal Center
mission: To champion the rights of people with disabilities through education, advocacy and litigation.

programs.name: Cancer Justice Program
programs.description: DRLC’s Cancer Justice program answers legal questions for people with cancer—because cancer patients and their families deserve to have clear, accessible, and exceptional legal resources. Founded in 1997 as the Cancer Legal Resource Center, Cancer Justice empowers people to navigate legal challenges with confidence. Through our direct services model, Cancer Justice educates and supports cancer patients, their families, healthcare professionals and advocates on matters like maintaining employment through treatment, accessing healthcare and government benefits, taking medical leave and estate planning.

programs.name: Disability Rights Litigation Program
programs.description: The Disability Rights Litigation Program litigates impact discrimination cases that address the civil rights of people with all types of disabilities, physical, sensory, learning, mental and intellectual. This includes class action and individual cases involving cutting-edge legal issues in the area of disability rights. Our cases challenge discriminatory practices by government agencies, businesses, and educational institutions. Examples include: inaccessible newly constructed or altered buildings, refusal to provide sign language interpreters or alternative format materials, inaccessible government programs, discriminatory insurance and health care systems, inaccessible transportation services, and policies that exclude people with disabilities.

name: Greater Los Angeles Zoo Association
mission: Through the passion of our team, the Los Angeles Zoo is leading the way in saving wildlife and connecting Angelenos to the natural world by providing exemplary animal care, delivering distinctive and diverse learning opportunities, and creating unforgettable experiences. Saving Wildlife. Enriching Our Communities. Creating Connections to Nature.
ntee_code: A56 - Natural History, Natural Science Museums

programs.name: Special Needs Outreach
programs.description: The Special Needs Outreach Program is specifically created to reach out to individuals who cannot easily visit the Los Angeles Zoo and Botanical Gardens. Our trained docents will bring small, live animals and other touchable items to your facility. This program is specially designed for an audience located at schools having classrooms for children with disabilities, hospitals, daycare centers (adult and children), and nursing homes. Using the outreach vehicle, our docents will come to your location. This program is about 30 minutes long and is tailored to the abilities of the audience. Audience members will meet some wild creatures and discover how they adapt and thrive within a complex habitat. The docents will explain the unique aspects of the animal’s adaptations, behavior, diet, and abilities. The discussions are designed to be participatory and tactile. These visits are subject to availability and completely free to your organization.

programs.name: ZooCamp
programs.description: Summer Zoo Camp is for children entering pre-kindergarten (age 4) up to those children entering grade 6. Zoo Camp is for children independent of their parents. Zoo Camp provides a safe and fun social setting where children can focus on making both child and animal friends.

programs.name: Field Trips and Children's Classes
programs.description: Onsite Field Trips Field trips are available during the regular academic school year, Monday through Friday from September through June. Zoo School Webinars Live-streamed Zoo School Webinars. Our Learning & Engagement instructors broadcast LIVE from the Zoo to create this unique experience. Each month we will explore a new topic with weekly programs especially curated for K-2nd, 3-5th, or 6th-8th grade students. Programs will include a variety of live activities such as animal observations, story time, career spotlights, and so much more. Docent-Led Virtual Field Trips Our docent guides will join a virtual classroom to facilitate one of our existing programs to foster students skills as scientists with the people and animals that can only be found at the L.A. Zoo. Family Nature Club Participants will spend the morning enjoying loosely structured outdoor play exploring nature through art and building, observation and imagination.

programs.name: Betty White's ZooPals
programs.description: Zoo Pals is a special grant-funded program that provides qualified schools and groups with free admission and free transportation to the Los Angeles Zoo for either a self-directed or docent-guided tour.

programs.name: Zoo World Patch Program
programs.description: Lead by a knowledgeable Zoo docent, the Zoo World Patch Program is a four-hour class for Boy and Girl Scout troops which focuses on the workings of the Zoo and its animal collection. Through digital presentations, hands-on activities, and adventures throughout Zoo grounds, the program takes scouts on an investigative exploration of the Zoo’s plant and animal collection. Children learn about the daily operations of a zoo, as well as zoo careers, animal exhibit development, animal diets, and much more! Each scout receives a special patch after the completion of the program.

programs.name: Adult Education
programs.description: Observing Animals: Behavioral Studies in Zoos (UCLA Extension), Los Angeles Zoo and Botanical Gardens Docent training (UCLA Extension), student veterinary training

programs.name: Conservation Field Study Program
programs.description: Scholarship program to allow high school students and Zoo/GLAZA mentors to go on an Earthwatch Field Study program each year.

programs.name: Conservation Strategic Plan
programs.description: In 2021, the Los Angeles Zoo launched a Conservation Strategic Plan (CSP) that outlines and expands our efforts to protect species and the habitats we share by focusing on six key areas - social and environmental justice, California conservation, illegal wildlife trade, conservation translocations, human-wildlife co-existence, and evidence-based conservation - strengthening our partnerships, and engaging our diverse communities.

name: Liberty Hill Foundation
mission: Liberty Hill Foundation is a laboratory for social change philanthropy. We leverage the power of community organizers, donor activists, and allies to advance social justice through strategic investment in grants, leadership training, and campaigns. For over 45 years, Liberty Hill has been supporting organizations led by those most impacted by systemic oppression. Liberty Hill’s guiding principle is that those who are closest to the issues are the ones who best understand those issues, and are the best equipped to build and implement solutions. In addition to grantmaking, we work with staff and boards of nonprofits to provide assessment, evaluation, and support of their operations, programs, fundraising, and capacity. To help provide this support, Liberty Hill has developed a network of non

programs.name: Fund for Change
programs.description: This program works to make systemic change through community organizing in Los Angeles County to advance economic justice, LGBTQ Justice and environmental justice. Grants will range from $10,000 to $50,000, paid for one year, and can be applied in one of four areas: capacity building, general support, project-specific support, and seed funding. Eligible applicants must have 501(c)(3) status, or be the fiscal sponsor of a nonprofit organization

programs.name: Liberty Hill Foundation Programs
programs.description: In addition to our issue-agnostic Fund for Change program, we make grants, provide capacity-building support, and convene stakeholders to pursue three overarching goals: 1) Build a youth development system and end youth incarceration; 2) Build green infrastructure and end oil drilling; 3) Build community-controlled housing and protect tenants. In pursuit of these goals, a partial list of our programs includes Ready to Rise, a partnership with LA County to fortify a coordinated landscape of youth development organizations; Liberation Fund, a network of organizations ending incarceration of girls and gender-expansive youth; EJ Ready, a coordinated effort to help environmental justice organizations take advantage of local, regional and federal government funding for EJ projects; STAND-LA, a coalition of organizations working to end oil drilling in Los Angeles; and Stay Housed LA, a public-private partnership that is helping tenants exercise and protect their rights.

leader.name: Shane Murphy Goldsmith
leader.profile:
Shane Murphy Goldsmith is the President and CEO of Liberty Hill Foundation, one of the nation’s most admired social change foundations. Ms. Goldsmith served previously as Liberty Hill’s Vice President and Director of Programs. She was responsible for the day-to-day oversight of Liberty Hill’s programs including our training, grantmaking and campaigns as well as Liberty Hill’s operations and finance departments.

Prior to joining Liberty Hill, Ms. Goldsmith was the Executive Director of PATH Ventures, an affordable housing development agency. Prior to that, she served as a senior advisor to then-City Council President Eric Garcetti for four years, overseeing a variety of field and legislative projects, including housing, economic development, the city budget, public safety, and LGBTQ issues. In addition, Ms. Goldsmith ran the Council District 13 Leadership Institute.

name: Legacy LA Youth Development Corporation
mission: Our mission is to make positive interventions in the lives of young people by offering alternatives to gangs and violence. Our programs build youth's capacity to reach their full potential, and equips them with the tools to transform their lives and community.

programs.name: Live Your Legacy
programs.description: Live Your Legacy provides employment, career, and vocational development opportunities for older youth (ages 18-24)

programs.name: Dream Big Youth Leadership Program
programs.description: Legacy LA’s flagship leadership development program engages youth in three years of training using a social justice model to increase knowledge of community issues, civics, and community organizing, and to increase capacity to respond to community needs. This program builds youth power to transform their neighborhood and improve public policies and systems that affect their lives.Youth develop community advocacy campaigns focused on creating access to healthy food, environmental justice, criminalization of youth, and drug and alcohol abuse. This commitment to grassroots leadership extends beyond youth, empowering community members of all ages to take active roles in creating change.Mujeres Poderosas is a women’s leadership skill-building group that empowers women of Ramona Gardens; it was launched after Company of Angels worked with the women on a theater project. Comunidad Unida is a group of trained leaders (adults) improving the community.

programs.name: Arts & Culture
programs.description: Legacy LA provides visual arts, comedy and improvisation, spoken word, poetry, theater, storytelling, graffiti art, murals, hip hop music, book club. Company of Angels, whose performance home is Legacy LA’s black box theater, uses the space to provide arts & culture in collaboration with Legacy LA and to develop emerging artists and produce theater that reflects the richness, diversity, and complexity of LA.

programs.name: Mindfulness and Wellness
programs.description: Legacy LA provides culturally relevant, on-site therapy, indigenous healing practices, mindfulness courses (to reduce stress), life skills sessions, parent groups, a father’s group, and Rainbow Alliance for LGBTQ youth and allies.

programs.name: Gang Reduction and Youth Development
programs.description: Legacy LA provides evidence-based gang prevention services with an emphasis on family case management.

programs.name: Family Source Center Services
programs.description: As a subcontractor for the local City-funded FamilySource Center, Legacy LA provides family services to increase academic achievement for youth and increase income for parents/guardians.

programs.name: Student Success Program
programs.description: The Student Success Program provides after-school mentoring and academic support to youth from middle school through college completion (ages 10-24) to promote educational attainment as a pathway out of poverty and an alternative to gangs.

leader.name: Lucy Herrera
leader.profile: Ms. Herrera is a Legacy LA youth program alumna and grew up in the Ramona Gardens community. She was the first ever youth to join Legacy LA’s Youth Council, where she gained skills to develop an intersectional social justice lens. She later earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science/law and society from UC Riverside and returned to the community after earning her degree. She has held increasingly responsible positions over ten years with Legacy LA including director and manager of youth leadership programming. Ms. Herrera serves on the AltaMed Health Services Board of Directors.

name: SOCIAL JUSTICE PARTNERS LOS ANGELES
aka: SVP, Social Venture Partners Los Angeles, SVP Los Angeles, SVPLA
mission: Social Justice Partners Los Angeles (SJP) invests in, expands, and connects communities advancing racial and social justice. We support the creation of systems and structures of care for the well-being and liberation of all people. We advance racial and social justice by providing grants, training, peer learning, and healing spaces.

programs.name: Engaged Grantmaking
programs.description:
We support emerging nonprofit leaders, early-stage initiatives & community change agents through programs that bolster their skills, confidence, resources and networks to create powerful impact in the world. 

Check out our programs and join this growing community of change makers!

programs.name: Fast Pitch
programs.description:
Over nine months, we create space for Los Angeles's social justice leaders to build community and learn from one another as they hone their systems change strategy, explore liberatory team culture practices, hone their messaging, and expand their relationships and resources. SJPLA's signature Fast Pitch training is a core part of this program.

Through the Fast Pitch training, nonprofit leaders prepare to share their stories and connect with our SJP coaches who support them along the way. The training culminates here, where participants bring their stories to the Fast Pitch virtual stage.

programs.name: Philanthropy Development
programs.description: We work with individuals on their philanthropic journeys in service of creating a thriving, equitable, and healthy Los Angeles. We create powerful relationships amongst our Partners and nonprofits, providing learning opportunities, and resources to grow their impact.

programs.name: Systems Change Acceleartor
programs.description:
The SJPLA Systems Change Accelerator bolsters the growth and impact of initiatives tackling the root causes of Los Angeles’ most pressing social problems.

Over nine months, the cohort model supports nonprofit leaders with lived experience as they hone their systems change strategy, explore liberatory team culture practices, amplify messaging, and expand their relationships and resources. SJPLA has found that supporting these foundational elements accelerates an organization’s ability to create systemic community impact.

programs.name: Consulting and Facilitation
programs.description:
We each have a role to play in creating more just communities. We’re here to support you in finding yours. 

SJPLA offers trainings for individuals and groups to further their understanding of harmful systems and practices, and to deepen their work as champions of racial and social justice. 

Anti-Racist Learning
Liberatory Workplaces
Healing Justice & Wellbeing

leader.name: Ms. Christine Margiotta
leader.profile:
Christine is passionate about channeling our collective power to create enduring justice and community. As Executive Director of SJPLA, she brings together nonprofit, community, and foundation leaders to fuel systemic transformation, facilitating mutual learning, deep connection, and synergistic collaboration. Christine launched SJPLA’s Systems Change Accelerator to bolster early-stage social justice initiatives and Anti-Racism for White People, a year-long learning journey for 170+ community leaders.

For nearly 20 years, Christine has leveraged a blend of community organizing, grantmaking, and policy change to create progress on racial and economic justice, homelessness, and LGBTQ rights. Prior to SJPLA, Christine was the Vice President of Community Impact at United Way of Greater LA, where she designed and led Home For Good, the region’s initiative to end homelessness. name: Los Angeles Section, National Council of Jewish Women
mission: NCJW|LA is committed to advancing economic justice and equity for working women and their families through direct cash assistance. In addition, we support the passage of laws and policies that ensure economic security, promote dignity in the workplace, and expand the safety net for families who are struggling.

programs.name: The Council Shops
programs.description: Recycle. Re-Love. Reinvest. NCJW|LA’s The Council Shop is a catalyst to make our work possible. When our donors recycle gently loved items, they are rediscovered by our shoppers at one of our seven locations throughout Los Angeles. NCJW|LA uses the profits to reinvest in programs that build financial resilience for hundreds of women in Los Angeles each year. Our combination of earned revenue and traditionally raised funds enables NCJW|LA to dedicate resources to innovation, research, and progressive ideas. NCJW|LA Council Shops is able to give away more than 70,000 items to 5,000 needy individuals each year through the 20 social services agencies that partner with us. NCJW|LA provides these same agencies, as well as its own clients, with free clothing vouchers that can be used by individuals for everyday use, who may be returning to the workforce, or who need school clothing for their children.

programs.name: The Health Equity Guaranteed Income Program
programs.description: This program supports working female heads of household, who receive care from MLK Community Healthcare or Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, who have diabetes and who earn between 30% and 80% of the Area Median Income. By specifically targeting working women with diabetes who are household heads, this program will establish a framework for future policies to incorporate Guaranteed Income as an essential component of treating chronic illnesses within low-income families. Program Goals are to minimize the substantial economic challenges associated with managing diabetes for pilot participants. Enhance fairness in social, economic, and health outcomes within a racially diverse, lower-income group of working mothers. Broaden the research scope regarding the influence of GI, encompassing chronic illnesses within marginalized communities. This approach aims to isolate and understand the direct contribution of income to health outcomes.

programs.name: Advocacy
programs.description: We create and support progressive policies that ensure economic justice and equity for women in Los Angeles. We confront systemic barriers that erode financial stability, advocating for fair economy, tax reforms, and robust work protections. Our dedication extends to enhancing the social safety net, rooted in dignity and actively championing the implementation and funding of guaranteed income policies. We prioritize comprehensive reforms across local to national platforms to tackle wage disparities, housing inequities, childcare accessibility, healthcare access, and reproductive justice. Through our advocacy for inclusive financial systems and progressive taxation, we tirelessly work towards fostering a more just society where all women can thrive economically, socially, and emotionally.

programs.name: Moms Wellness Network
programs.description: The Moms Wellness Network (MWN) offers support for mothers with shared interests and responsibilities, focusing on marginalized groups. Participants are provided tools to improve their well-being and balance their various responsibilities. The program includes exercises, activities, and conversations to aid personal development and promote positive change in financial planning and resilience practices. Be part of our empowering community designed for moms and caretakers. Our expert facilitator will skillfully guide you in developing mindfulness and self-care strategies. You will receive personalized support for your financial well-being and enjoy perks designed to accelerate your sense of accomplishment. Let us inspire and empower you to reach your financial goals.

programs.name: Rental Assistance Program
programs.description: The Los Angeles Women’s Rental Assistance Program offers financial assistance to female heads of households with dependents living with them. This assistance helps cover the cost of partial monthly rent for those financially impacted by layoffs, reduction in hours, reduced salary, illness, or other unexpected emergencies within the last 90 days. Many Americans today are living paycheck to paycheck with little to no savings available in the event of an emergency. Many people in the workforce are only one missed paycheck or one unexpected expense away from possible homelessness. Established in 2014, the Rental Assistance program offers emergency assistance, (up to $1000 per month for up to four months) to low-income women and families in Los Angeles County. To date, this program has helped thousands of families to stay in their homes.

programs.name: Clothing Assistance
programs.description: We offer several ways for people in need to obtain fresh, clean and many-times, brand-new clothing at no cost. Our Clothing Assistance Program supports individuals and families living under or near the poverty line by providing gift cards that can be redeemed for clothing, shoes, and accessories. Gift cards can be used at any of our seven Council Shops. Cards are distributed by NCJW|LA monthly. We directly issue 50 cards each month. Once the cards are gone, clients may still apply and will be added to the waitlist for the following month. Each eligible family member can receive a single gift card each year. Children under the age of eight receive a $30.00 card. All other family members are eligible for $50.00 cards. You may only solicit gift cards for individuals living at the same address, with a limit of six (6) cards per address.

programs.name: P.A.I.D. Guaranteed Income Program
programs.description: We know there is an economic burden pregnant people with restricted income face. Financial stresses during pregnancy can create challenging conditions affecting birth outcomes. Guaranteed Income can help relieve some of these strains and stressors. The program is designed to start early in pregnancy to impact as much of the pregnancy as possible. Pregnancy Assistance Income with Dignity (P.A.I.D.) aims to develop a plan for change and conduct a study to show how maternal health and poverty are connected. Reduce the economic burden, improve social, economic and health outcomes, and improve health and developmental outcomes of babies born into low-income households.

programs.name: Career MOMentum
programs.description: Career MOMentum supports women who are the primary caretakers and sole earners in their homes, by equipping them with the skills, tools, and resources for long-term success. Employment is a key focus, where we provide individualized support. This hybrid program expands beyond job training alone and provides you with a supportive environment where you are safe and have a welcoming space. Learn in-demand, transferable skills that intersect multiple sectors including retail, nonprofit, and event management, and potential living-wage employment opportunities. Including hands-on experience in The Council Shops and collaboration to plan and execute a community-building event. Build a foundation for financial security with integrated, practical financial education. Explore the connection between your mental health, physical well-being, and career success. Foster connections and cultivate friendships through a stronger community.

programs.name: Cash for Learning
programs.description: Our commitment in addressing the social and economic realities facing women and their families, NCJW|LA has awarded financial assistance to Los Angeles County residents for more than 20 years. Since its inception, providing more than $250,000 in grants focusing on improving the quality of life through responsive social service programs distinguished by a vigorous commitment to self-sufficiency, education, and social responsibility. Since 1987, this committee distributes funds to heads of household women who are courageous in facing life’s obstacles. Also making a commitment to higher education to achieve a better future for themselves and their families. It simplifies spiritual processes and practices by merging the persuasions of the Logical Mind with the Spiritual so that there is full harmony within. programs.name: Growing the Empowered Child
programs.description: An empowered child is the one who is happy, responsible, creative, and confident, with a drive for excellence. The Growing the Empowered Child is a program that teaches through game modules how to be Free from Fear and Anger; and to learn how to discover and celebrate their own uniqueness and that of others. There are 16 age specific modules targeted for children ages 5 to 17. Each module has a series of games or activities that allow the child to identify and reinforce in themselves, confidence, empowerment, and other positive qualities that they have or desire to embody. These games can help a child on a day-to–day basis rise above the trials and tribulations that youth experience in their journey to adulthood.

programs.name: The Way Forward
programs.description: Nature’s Principles and Practices for Empowered Living. A practical, radical, and innovative new way of thinking, living, and being, in total harmony with oneself and all of life. The Way Forward has outlined 18 powerful principles that take you on a journey into your soul and the cradle of life. It nourishes you with wisdom, which empowers you to master your life.

programs.name: Essential Life Education

Highlights of the Course include: Understanding the primary Life Drives, which are Spiritual, Social, Psychological, Physical and Financial Quests. Everyone is driven by one or a combination of these forces. Understanding the Forces of Life, which are Time, Energy, Space, and Circumstance (TESC), and how they influence you and your relationships. name: The House Institute Foundation
mission: Building on our strong foundation, we continue to innovate in hearing health through research, education, global hearing health, and pediatric care, "so all may hear".

programs.name: Research
programs.description: Our team of faculty and research scientists focus their research on the causes and treatment of both sudden and progressive hearing loss due to associated genetic disorders and sensorineural hearing loss. Current research directions include, but are not limited to, natural history of neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2), tinnitus treatment, balance disorders, and cochlear implantation.

programs.name: Education
programs.description: Our education programs aim to support medical professionals as well as the general public through our extensive library of surgical technique videos, our visiting physicians program for international medical providers, our ACGME-approved clinical fellowship program, our temporal bone dissection courses, and our temporal bone surgical dissection manual. We also offer a weekly presentation series from experts around the world, and an annual symposium for audiologists. We continue to develop print and web content to help educate the public about various hearing conditions and how to prevent hearing loss.

programs.name: Global Hearing Health
programs.description: Our global hearing health efforts aim to support physicians worldwide, as well as provide hearing solutions and interventions for undeserved populations at home and abroad.

programs.name: Pediatric Care
programs.description: House Children's Hearing Center (HCHC), a dedicated pediatric clinic, was opened in Los Angeles in 2022 to treat the full spectrum of hearing conditions in children from birth to 21 years of age. From hearing aids and cochlear implants to family services and support groups, our bilingual clinic is designed to offer the highest quality care to families of all socioeconomic backgrounds and uniquely support children and their families on their hearing health journeys.

name: Homeless Not Toothless
mission: Homeless Not Toothless is a 501C(3) nonprofit dedicated to providing free and quality dental care to the homeless, foster youth, and low-income persons in Los Angeles, bringing back one smile at a time. The organization also aims to empower the homeless and underserved by providing access to becoming part of the mainstream workforce again.

programs.name: Free Dental Care for Veterans
programs.description:
Our goal is to provide free dental care to as many homeless veterans as possible. 

Homeless Not Toothless intends to treat Veterans with preventative care such as dental screenings, cleanings, x-rays, fillings, and health education.  As needed, more invasive dental procedures such as root canals, fillings and extractions will be performed. 

For many Veterans, this will be the first time that they receive dental care since they were active duty.  Many are living below the poverty level, are uninsured/underinsured and cannot afford “out of pocket” dental costs. It is our goal to ensure that dental care, from brushing and flossing twice a day to remembering to have a semi-annual check-up, becomes a regular lifelong practice.  

Our facilities have been donated by practicing dentist offices, this also allows us to have over 96% of our funding go directly to patient care.

Our program serves to improve the quality of life and while also addressing a critical challenge among veterans. Our efforts also result in building a safe, prosperous and vibrant community by reducing the number of homeless people in the community and also restoring their pride in their community.

programs.name: Free Dental Care for Foster Youth
programs.description: We provide free dental care to foster youth as well as former children of the foster program who have aged out but are currently attending college.

programs.name: Free Dental Care for Survivors of Domestic Violence
programs.description: We provide free dental care to survivors of domestic violence.

leader.name: Dr Jay Grossman
leader.profile:
Founded by Dr. Jay Grossman in 1992, Homeless Not Toothless is a 501(c)(3) organization dedicated to providing free dental care to the homeless and underserved. Since its inception, the organization has provided over $7.7 million in services to over 100,000 patents.

Homeless Not Toothless has hundreds of dentists who donate some of the dental lab work.

Dentists volunteer their time and either pay for their own laboratory expenses or work with labs who donate their dental work.

Most of the patients are referred by the local clinics and shelters, where their dental needs and the necessity for treatment are assessed. They include a number of military Veterans, as well as young people who have aged out of the foster system.

The dentists and staff who work with the homeless patients do so without financial compensation and with only the kindest and most generous hearts. They all have one thing in common: A belief in the power of a great smile.

name: ST JOHNS COMMUNITY HEALTH
mission: The mission of St. John's Community Health is to improve community health and reduce health disparities by delivering high quality, comprehensive services and impacting health and social policy.

programs.name: Community Health Center
programs.description: St. John's Community Health (SJCH) is one of the largest Federally Qualified Health Centers in Los Angeles, operating a network of 22 clinics. SJCH provides medical, dental, mental health, and substance use services to 100,000+ patients annually regardless of their income level or insurance status. SJCH also provides case management, supportive services, and outreach. Its specialized programs include: Homeless Health Services, PRIME (serving people with or at risk for HIV, AIDs, and Hepatitis C), Transgender Health Program, RISE re-entry program (for people exiting incarceration), CalAIM care management, Domestic Violence, Harm Reduction, Healthy Homes (housing environmental health), and outreach, advocacy, and education on a range of health issues.

leader.name: James Mangia
leader.profile: James Mangia, President and Chief Executive Officer, has held his position at SJWCFC since 1993.  Under his leadership the organization has grown from a small volunteer-run pediatric clinic to a key safety net provider in L.A. County, with a network of 25 community and school-based clinics and four mobile clinics providing a full range of medical, dental, mental health, and supportive services to children, adolescents and adults of all ages.  The annual operating budget has increased from $65,000 to more than $200 million.  Mr. Mangia has built sustainable partnerships with dozens of community based organizations, resulting in increased access to healthcare and social services to tens of thousands of low-income residents of L.A. County, primarily Latino and African American. Mr. Mangia has a Masters in Public Health (MPH) from UCLA, and a B.A. in Political Science and History from City University of New York.

name: Elysian Valley Arts Collective
mission: Preserving and promoting an inclusive community along the Los Angeles River for creative production by artists, designers and artisans; in order to cultivate a sense of place, a vibrant local economy and arts education for youth.

programs.name: Program 1
programs.description: IMPACT REPORT2023 was a another big year for us. lluminate the Night came back for the second time and was a great success. We asked you to "bring the light" to the LA River and you did! We presented numerous events at our headquarters at The Blake Lofts and participated in many off-site events with our Creation Station; a mobile art studio and gallery. Download our project and impact report below to learn all about our year in 2023. 2023 Impact ReportPROGRAMMINGOVERVIEWFestivalsThe Frogtown Artwalk is our signature event since 2006 and is offered biennially on even-numbered years. The 13 year old festival was created to bridge the divide between artists and residents in the mixed use neighborhood of Elysian Valley, affectionately known as "Frogtown, and to provide support for the group of artists occupying the former manufacturer buildings along the Los Angeles River. Illuminate the Night, also running biennially in odd-numbered years, is a more recent festival that celebrates the performing arts, light installations and invites participants to "bring the light" to the LA River.ClassesSince 2009, the EVAC has offered free or low-cost art classes to the youth of the area. Class offerings have included drawing, ceramics, photography, woodworking, mosaic and video film-making. Juried Art ShowsFrom time to time, the EVAC sponsors a juried art show in conjunction with the Frogtown Artwalk. Shows are typically open to youth from ages 5-18, and is juried by working artists in the Frogtown neighborhood. Click here to learn about past juried art shows.FilmsAs part of its mission, the EVAC is interested in supporting young filmmakers by sponsoring documentary film projects that use oral history techniques and family photos to capture stories of the history of Frogtown. Some films include Our River (2016) and Mapping Frogtown Stories (2011).

leader.name: Ms. Wendy Butts
leader.profile: A 16-year veteran of the LA Conservation Corps, Wendy Butts has been leading the organization as CEO since July 2014. Wendy’s interest in the environment and its impact on communities started in 1994 when she worked as a United States Peace Corps Volunteer in Ecuador. She planned community recycling projects, created an environmental club and educated middle school students in conservation-related studies in a rural coastal town. She began her career at the LA Conservation Corps in 1998 working directly with Corpsmembers, and training them in natural and urban environmental studies. She has served as Development Director and Program Development Director, procuring private and government funding for the Corps which led to a 15% growth in the annual budget in four years. Most recently, Wendy served as the Corps’ Contract Compliance Officer developing new systems for monitoring program quality and compliance with contracts. She developed best practices and trained corps across the nation.

name: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
mission: Through key partnerships with local health organizations, Cedars-Sinai strives to reduce health disparities by improving access to care, the quality of that care and the promotion of the overall health and wellbeing of the most vulnerable members of the community through a series of programs and initiatives.

programs.name: Civic Engagement
programs.description: The Civic Engagement funding priority aims to increase the capacity of organizations to address issues of public concern in partnership with local community efforts that align with Cedars-Sinai institutional priorities and geography.

programs.name: Social Determinants of Health
programs.description: The Social Determinants of Health funding priority aims to increase the capacity of organizations to promote healthy environments in which people are born, grow, live, work, and age.

programs.name: Patient Care
programs.description: Cedars-Sinai is widely known for its national leadership in transforming healthcare for the benefit of patients. Cedars-Sinai includes more than 50 medical offices throughout Southern California, as well as Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, one of the largest nonprofit academic medical centers in the U.S. with 886 licensed beds, 2,100 physicians, 3,000 nurses and thousands of other healthcare professionals and staff. Clinical programs range from primary care for preventing, diagnosing and treating common conditions to specialized treatments for rare, complex and advanced illnesses. In addition, Cedars-Sinai serves the community through its Medical Network, which includes the highly rated Cedars-Sinai Medical Group and Cedars-Sinai Health Associates.

programs.name: Medical Research
programs.description: Discovery is central to Cedars-Sinai’s mission. The institution’s scientists and physician-scientists generate ideas, therapies, devices and systems that contribute to biomedical progress around the world. More than 1,500 research projects currently underway explore the genetic underpinnings of disease, exploit the potential of stem cells, leverage nanotechnology, parse big data, and assess how gender and metabolism impact health. Cedars-Sinai’s investigators push the frontiers of biomedicine with studies in cardiac care, cancer, digestive health, the neurosciences, women’s health and more. Cedars-Sinai has earned its position as a research leader through an ever-expanding effort to promote health, reduce suffering and improve human life.

programs.name: Education
programs.description: Cedars-Sinai educates the medical professionals of tomorrow with more than 80 residencies and fellowships in specialty and subspecialty areas, and several graduate programs, as well as major educational programs for nurses and other health care professionals. The Graduate Program in Biomedical Sciences and Translational Medicine focuses on transforming innovative concepts into impactful treatments. Cedars-Sinai’s nurse training programs teach specialized skills and encourage leadership. The institution also provides training for allied health professionals and postdoctoral scientists. Education at Cedars-Sinai combines rigorous academic curricula with mentorship from globally recognized faculty.

programs.name: Community Benefit
programs.description: As an integral part of the Los Angeles community, Cedars-Sinai's work goes beyond the walls of our facilities. We’re providing care to the uninsured and underinsured every day through programs in and with schools, clinics, homeless shelters and community centers to elevate the health of the region. Cedars-Sinai fulfills its vital mission of community service by investing in programs and services dedicated to improving community health, working closely with schools, local government, senior centers, health and human service programs, and other agencies to better meet community needs, and to expand the capacity of other organizations to serve those who are most vulnerable, maximizing the impact of joint efforts to improve lives.

programs.name: Community Response
programs.description: Cedars‑Sinai's Community Response grantmaking portfolio is designed to increase the capacity of local and regional partners whose missions closely align with our institutional priorities, and to build a strong network of area nonprofits capable of responding to issues of public concern. We do this through grants made to civic partners and in alignment with our triennial Community Health Needs Assessment, ignition grants-a cluster of grants intended to spark change in response to unmet or emerging public health needs, and rapid response grants to address emergencies.

programs.name: Access to Care
programs.description: The Access to Care portfolio works to increase the capacity of Los Angeles County’s healthcare safety net to improve access to comprehensive, quality healthcare services for underserved populations. The portfolio includes Cedars‑Sinai's flagship Community Clinic Initiative, which is focused on bolstering leadership and effectiveness within safety net clinics. It also includes a commitment to increasing access to integrated health services and a dedicated focus on Black birth equity.

programs.name: Homelessness and Housing
programs.description: Cedars‑Sinai's Homelessness and Housing portfolio aims to increase the capacity of organizations to promote healthy environments in which people are born, grow, live, work and age. This portfolio focuses on the connections between healthcare and housing systems and works to prevent and end homelessness among older adults, youth and young adults in Los Angeles County.

Each summer the outdoor stages at California Plaza, the program’s architecturally unique venue, come alive with performances, workshops, masterclasses, and audience discussions serving more than 25,000 people annually – an audience recognized as the most demographically diverse in the country. Because all programs are presented free to the public, entire families, seniors, school and youth groups, and others are able to enjoy the performing arts regardless of their financial ability. Grand Performances makes every effort to utilize our unique combination of venue and program to serve the community and enliven our public space.

leader.name: Rafael Gonzalez
leader.profile:
Rafael is President & CEO of Grand Performances whose mission is to inspire community, celebrate diversity, and unite Los Angeles through free access to global performing arts.

Rafael is a proven and inclusive leader, manager and advocate driven by his core values of justice, collaboration, accountability, balance, respect, trust and innovation. Over the years, he has worked and organized in the nonprofit, government, service and philanthropic fields. This multisector experience has gifted him the skill to develop and maintain relationships with individuals from diverse disciplines and backgrounds for purposes of realizing common objectives, social impact, equity and community/systems change. 

 Rafael integrates the people’s social, political, cultural and economic context into Grand Performances’ presentations and audience experience. This framework serves as the narrative that weaves together expression, struggle and aspirations in the form of music, theatre, poetry and dance.

name: SAVING INNOCENCE INC
mission: We support and empower children and adults impacted by human trafficking by disrupting cycles of abuse and confronting exploitation through strategic partnerships and trauma-responsive education, advocacy, and systems of care.

programs.name: Case Management & Advocacy
programs.description: Case Management and Advocacy provide one-on-one mentorship, emotional support, independent living development, and access to resources and referrals to partner organizations that provide for a client's identified needs. Saving Innocence Case Managers and Advocates are experts in Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children and all forms of Human Trafficking and provide trauma-informed, responsive-care to ensure clients are treated with care, compassion, and thoroughness. Saving Innocence prioritizes accessibility and cultural competency by partnering with culturally specific services to provide comprehensive care and translating materials into Spanish, Mandarin, and Korean. Services are offered in Spanish by bilingual Case Managers and interpreter services are available free of charge.

programs.name: Crisis Response
programs.description: Saving Innocence provides Crisis Response to human trafficking victims recovered by Law Enforcement within 90 minutes of contact 24/7 to an identified staging area (station, hospital, etc.). Community Crisis Response through the Saving Innocence Crisis Hotline provides emergency crisis coordination and possible in-person response based on needs and safety. Crisis Response services can include: Case Management and Advocacy, short-term housing via hotel, shelter and transitional housing coordination, short-term food assistance, basic needs (hygiene, clothing, etc.), transportation assistance to return home, etc. All Crisis Response clients are offered Case Management and Advocacy services.

programs.name: Workshops
programs.description: Saving Innocence provides trauma responsive workshops and classes that support the specific needs of Saving Innocence clients. Workshops include: life skills, emotional group support, and other specialized groups for individuals impacted by exploitation and trafficking. Clients can learn a variety of coping, life, and social skills when fully engaged and participating.

programs.name: Foster Family Agency (FFA)
programs.description: Recruiting, training, and supporting Foster Families who have enough room in their homes and hearts to join one of the children that Saving Innocence cares for with their family. These families provide support, connection, love, and protection to invest in the future of our children.

leader.name: Alan Smyth
leader.profile: Alan Smyth currently serves as our Executive Director with over 30 years of nonprofit management and experience. Alan is responsible for all business operations, direct services, our Foster Family agency and all development efforts including donor acquisition, budget creation and management. Prior to his time with Saving Innocence, he spent 25 years with Young Life, a globally known nonprofit focused on kids around the world. His time with Young Life was primarily focused in Greater Los Angeles. Alan got his Bachelor of Communication Studies from San Jose State University.

name: Mental Health Advocacy Services, Inc.
mission:
The mission of Mental Health Advocacy Services (MHAS) is to protect and advance the legal rights of low-income adults and children with mental health disabilities and empower them to assert those rights in order to maximize their autonomy, achieve equity, and secure the resources they need to thrive.

MHAS accomplishes its mission by providing direct legal assistance to individuals, as well as training and technical assistance to attorneys, mental health professionals, consumer and family member groups, and other advocates.
ntee_code: R20 - Civil Rights, Advocacy for Specific Groups

programs.name: Special Education Outreach Project
programs.description: MHAS conducts community training sessions to teach parents and caregivers how to obtain special education services for their children.  For families needing additional assistance, MHAS provides individual advocacy.

programs.name: Government Benefits
programs.description: MHAS assists clients with issues related to Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and other Social Security benefits. This assistance includes preventing clients from losing their SSI benefits by assisting them with post-eligibility issues such as benefit terminations, overpayments and disability reviews. MHAS also helps individuals with issues related to Medi-Cal insurance coverage and access to appropriate mental health services. MHAS collaborates with other local organizations to develop strategies for increasing access to benefits and services for low-income individuals.

programs.name: Project New Start
programs.description: In partnership with the organization Painted Brain, MHAS recently launched “Project New Start”, a comprehensive job placement, mental health, and legal services program for formerly incarcerated individuals that reside in South Los Angeles. Project New Start was established to combat employment barriers for individuals who are or who have been in the criminal justice system and are experiencing mental health challenges. Painted Brain and MHAS staff collaborate to provide individualized employment service plans for formerly incarcerated program participants to successfully obtain employment. Additionally, MHAS helps clients overcome barriers to reentry by providing legal services and advocacy in the areas of expungement, employment, housing, and criminal justice debt.

programs.name: Consumer Advocacy
programs.description: Consumer law and credit reparation is a common area of service across MHAS’ programs serving low-income clients with mental health disabilities. Credit reporting errors, when reported by credit bureaus or tenant screening services, can prevent clients from obtaining work or securing housing. MHAS partners with our clients to end or reduce debt collection, enforce fair debt collection laws, resolve credit reporting errors, prevent negative consumer reporting, and resolve financial disputes with landlords, businesses and public agencies. MHAS also helps clients combat financial exploitation by unscrupulous individuals and corporations and enforces mental health consumer rights.  Finally, MHAS conducts a broad range of know-your-rights trainings on specific financial topics including how to monitor your credit, how to establish credit when you have no credit history or a poor credit history, how to identify credit repair scams, and how to respond to debt collectors.

programs.name: Fair Housing
programs.description: MHAS fights housing discrimination against individuals with mental health disabilities through legal representation, fair housing training, and community education. MHAS currently has an ongoing fair housing education and outreach project, funded by the U.S. Department of Housing & Urban Development Fair Housing Initiatives Program, to educate mental health consumers and service providers about fair housing rights and responsibilities. In addition to conducting fair housing workshops, the project distributes “Fair Housing Tip of the Month” e-mail messages in in English, Korean, and Spanish to over 3,000 people.

programs.name: Homelessness Prevention
programs.description: In 2020, MHAS launched a new behavioral health legal partnership in which legal services intervention specifically targeting low-income tenants with mental health disabilities at risk of homelessness is holistically integrated in partnership with three of the largest mental health services providers in Los Angeles. Clients are provided with eviction defense and other tenant defense assistance in landlord-tenant rental disputes, including pre-eviction and eviction legal services, counseling, advice and consultation, mediation, training, renter education and representation, and legal services to improve habitability and to ensure receipt of eligible income or benefits to improve housing stability.

programs.name: Whole Person Care Medical Legal Community Partnership
programs.description: MHAS is a key partner in LA County's Medical-Legal Community Partnership ("MLCP"), a project administered by the Department of Health Services, and part of the county's Whole Person Care ("WPC") initiative. Through the MLCP, MHAS assists participants with legal issues to ensure that they have the resources and support needed to achieve better health outcomes and overall well-being. Since the project began in early 2018, MHAS has helped hundreds of participants on legal matters in the areas of housing, public benefits, and discrimination; provided a series of trainings on legal issues pertinent to care management staff; and guided hundreds of clinical staff with legal technical assistance.

programs.name: Mental Health Court Clinic
programs.description: In 2022, Mental Health Advocacy Services is launching a new Clinic in partnership with the Hollywood Mental Health Courthouse targeting individuals with mental health disabilities. The Clinic will provide Court-approved information and resources about Mental Health Court proceedings to litigants and other members of the public who are not currently in custody.  The Clinic will also offer information and brief services on a range of ancillary civil legal issues with a goal of helping litigants achieve greater overall stability, thus allowing them to move through their proceedings at Mental Health Court with greater efficiency and success, and with less likelihood of returning. This will include helping litigants secure and maintain housing, helping litigants access SSI or other benefits to which they may be legally entitled, and assisting litigants with obtaining - or having reinstated - their Driver's License or California ID, among other civil, legal needs.

programs.name: Stay Housed L.A.
programs.description: In 2022, Mental Health Advocacy Services joined the Stay Housed L.A. coalition, a partnership between the County of Los Angeles, the City of Los Angeles, and local community and legal service providers that provides tenants with the information and support needed to exercise their rights so that they can remain safely in their homes. Through its participation in this partnership, MHAS provides individualized advice and counsel on fair housing and tenancy rights to clients with mental health disabilities, as well as direct representation on behalf of these clients in conflicts with landlords, housing authorities, and non-profit housing and service providers. MHAS also provides technical assistance and training to other members of the Stay Housed LA Coalition on the rights and responsibilities of individuals with mental health disabilities.

leader.name: Ms. Jenny Farrell
leader.profile:
On January 2, 2019, Jenny Farrell became the Executive Director of Mental Health Advocacy Services. As Executive Director, Jenny is responsible for overseeing the administration, programs, and strategic plan of the organization. She also manages development and fundraising, marketing, and community outreach for the organization. She has several years of senior nonprofit management experience and a strong, personal commitment to protecting the rights of people with mental health disabilities.

Jenny previously served as Director of External Relations of the Los Angeles Center for Law and Justice, a nonprofit legal aid agency that provides free legal services to survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault.  

Jenny received her Bachelor’s degree from Smith College and her J.D. from the University of Southern California Gould School of Law. When she's not at work, Jenny and her partner John enjoy wrangling their two very-adorable-but-very-stubborn boys, Robby and Micah.
