name: Community Nature Connection
mission: TO INCREASE ACCESS TO THE OUTDOORS FOR COMMUNITIES IMPACTED BY RACIAL, SOCIO-ECONOMIC, AND DISABILITY INJUSTICES BY ELIMINATING EXISTING BARRIERS THROUGH ADVOCACY, COMMUNITY CENTERED PROGRAMMING, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT.

programs.name: Akuutet Learning Nursery at Elyria Canyon
programs.description: Akuutet Learning Nursery at Elyria Canyon offers a hybrid learning course for high school youth and young adults who are interested in learning about native plants, the role of a nursery, the process around habitat restoration, interpretation of outdoor experiences, the role of fire in an ecosystem, how to create wildfire resilient communities through habitat restoration, and leadership development. This 13-week hybrid course introduces participants to the life cycle of plant propagation, as well as discuss the outdoor access issues that limit urban communities from wildland. Participants will learn tools on project management, inclusivity in the field and interpretation for and from diverse perspectives. This course will be a combination of online virtual meetings and in-person outdoor field trips. The programming runs during the school year, with internships happening during the summer months after completing the program. Participants gain outdoor skills for career readiness.

programs.name: Outdoor and Coastal Access Leadership Institute
programs.description: Outdoor & Coastal Access Leadership Institute (OCALI) engages a cohort of 12-15 youth community leaders through a 10-week extended leadership program focused on 'access to nature' issues affecting low-income communities and communities of color, and the advocacy efforts working to address these issues. Participants of the programs visit park and coastal lands throughout the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area, engage in speaker series about environmental issues, learn outdoor skill-sets, and organize 'access to nature' projects. In addition, these youth community leaders are able to take the skills developed in this program and use them to become volunteers, interns, and part-time staff with CNC.

programs.name: Transit to Trails
programs.description: Available and affordable transportation are significant barriers to accessing the outdoors. In a county that runs along the beautiful Pacific Ocean and is bursting with parks and natural areas, Angelenos can struggle to find access points or transit to these spots. The Explore the Coast/Transit to Trails program provides free bus trips for community groups and communities from various County Supervisorial districts to these outdoor beach and park locations so that everyone has the opportunity to get outdoors and fall in love with nature. Each trip is led by a seasoned naturalist, who provides interpretive programming specific to the destination.

programs.name: Sensing Nature
programs.description: CNC’s ‘Sensing Nature’ program is a new elementary school program that primarily works with Title One elementary schools, specifically at the 4th and 5th grade level, in our programmatic focus areas of Westlake and Northeast Los Angeles. This school program consists of 3-4 engagements with a classroom, which includes a pre-field trip visit, a field trip, a post-field trip visit, and an optional school event. The program is designed to facilitate experiential learning about nature and outdoor spaces using curiosity, play, and wellness. In particular, the program uses examples of flora, fauna, and natural systems to shed light on how youth can use their different senses to experience the world around them. This program highlights wellness and the interconnectedness of our wellbeing to being in natural spaces or outdoors. We engage in activities that give space and time to practices of healing, reflection, rest, creativity, and curiosity that comes from communing with nature.

programs.name: Emerging Naturalist
programs.description: The Emerging Naturalist offers two youth-centered programs that focus on cultivating connection to nature and gaining exposure to careers in the outdoors. The purpose of this program is to create meaningful outdoor experiences for youth in the community. Our Emerging Naturalist 1.0 is a six- week introductory program designed for middle school and high school youth (ages 11-14) to support and develop naturalist skills of observation and journaling and outdoor and camping skills. The Emerging Naturalist 2.0 program is a school year-long effort focused on high school youth (ages 14-18) focused on a deeper dive into outdoor issues and connections, with civic engagement and advocacy elements interwoven into field and camping trips, with participants also learning about careers in the outdoors and urban ecology. This program will be a combination of in-person outdoor field trips and one camping trip.

name: Baby Warm, Inc.
mission: Baby Warm provides incubators to wildlife rehabbers who care for orphaned baby animals. Without a mom to keep them warm, the tiniest fragile babies have the best chance of survival in an incubator and yet it's life saving equipment most wildlife rehabbers cannot afford. In every community across the country, wildlife rehabbers devote their lives to saving orphaned wild babies. Baby Warm will make sure there's a warm bed for every baby.

programs.name: Incubator Fundraising
programs.description: We fundraise for incubators for wildlife rehabbers who care for orphaned baby animals.

leader.name: Kim Barker
leader.profile: I’m Kim Barker, a Canadian writer, and while living in California, my passion was animal rescue photography. I spent the six years meeting wildlife rehabbers all over the country and was amazed by their willingness to do whatever it takes to help animals. The wildlife rehabber is the one up at dawn feeding a baby squirrel who lost his mom, or comforting a lonely baby river otter, or shedding tears over the baby hummingbird who didn’t make it. I don’t have what it takes to be a wildlife rehabber myself, but what I can do is help make sure they have the best equipment possible. I started Baby Warm in 2014 to do just that.

name: International Medical Corps
mission: International Medical Corps' mission is to improve quality of life through health interventions and related activities that strengthen underserved communities worldwide. With the flexibility to respond rapidly to emergencies, International Medical Corps offers health services and training to people at the highest risk, always working to strengthen local healthcare systems and promote self-reliance.

programs.name: Emergency Response and Preparedness
programs.description: Because disaster can strike anywhere and anytime, the ability to respond even in the most remote areas of the world is essential for effective emergency response. With the most acute phase of disaster response spanning just 72 hours—when life-threatening injury and disease can be effectively addressed—deployment speed is critical. Combined with pre-positioned stocks of essential supplies, and ongoing partnerships with both international and local aid groups, we maintain the needed surge capacity to respond to emergencies in the most challenging environments regardless of scale or geographic location. To build self-reliance even in the midst of natural and manmade disasters, we offer training in the areas of greatest need alongside life-saving medical services and relief. https://internationalmedicalcorps.org/program/emergency-response-preparedness/

programs.name: Health Services Support
programs.description: Efficient, well-organized and well-equipped health services can be lifesaving and life-changing when facilities are well equipped with pharmaceuticals and medical supplies, and when providers are well trained in how to use them in a range of critical areas. Training and education, as well as needed tools and resources, are therefore central to our support of health services. We train and mentor health workers, construct and rehabilitate local health facilities, and work hand-in-hand with both national governments and communities to ensure primary and secondary healthcare is available and affordable for all. https://internationalmedicalcorps.org/program/health-services-support/

programs.name: Family and Community Health
programs.description: Family and community health programming needs to target the entire population, including children and adolescents, men and women of all ages, and people with disabilities. Working with families and communities makes it possible for us to ensure a comprehensive approach to providing primary healthcare, which includes reproductive health, mental health and psychosocial support, and disease prevention. International Medical Corps works with local governments and community leaders to engage individuals and households in an interactive process to identify their health priorities, needs and resources. We help mobilize resources, fill identified gaps as appropriate, and pass needed skills into local hands through training. Combined, these efforts prepare communities for healthier futures. https://internationalmedicalcorps.org/program/family-community-health/

programs.name: Women’s and Children’s Health
programs.description: Protecting the well-being of women and children is a high priority in healthcare, and women’s health is vital for healthy communities. We work with communities and local health authorities to improve the health of expectant women by offering a full range of safe motherhood health services. We focus on children's health through programs that include vaccinations, growth monitoring, early childhood development interventions and community-based case management. In times of crisis—when traditional social codes protecting women can easily break down—women, adolescent girls and young children become more vulnerable to abuse, rape or sexual exploitation. We offer culturally appropriate services for gender-based violence and work to reduce forms of violence rooted in gender discrimination. We also implement child-protection programs according to the needs of children, their families and communities across a range of different contexts.

programs.name: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene
programs.description: Providing adequate water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities is a key public health challenge in many remote and low-income areas. At a time when roughly 2.1 billion people lack access to safe, readily available drinking water at home and 3.6 billion do not have safely managed sanitation, roughly half the hospital beds in the developing countries are occupied by people suffering from water- and sanitation-related diseases such as diarrhea, pneumonia, skin infections and cholera. We therefore work to provide these most basic of human needs, especially in disaster-affected contexts. We support community efforts to provide and promote the use of clean water, safe sanitation services and hygiene awareness within communities and their health clinics to limit the spread of diarrheal diseases. https://internationalmedicalcorps.org/program/water-sanitation-hygiene/

programs.name: Nutrition and Food Security
programs.description: International Medical Corps helps strengthen nutrition programs at the national, local and community levels in some of the world’s most challenging environments. Malnutrition, both chronic and acute, contributes to more than 3 million deaths of children under five each year—nearly 50% of all child deaths worldwide. It also carries enormous social and economic costs, leaving almost 200 million children with stunted growth, compromised cognitive development and/or poor physical health. We work with families to prevent malnutrition, screen and treat children under five and pregnant and nursing women for acute malnutrition, and focus on educating the mothers and caregivers of young children on the importance of breastfeeding and of providing a diverse diet using locally available foods. Our food security and livelihood programs help these vulnerable groups grow nutrient-rich foods and diversify their diets. https://internationalmedicalcorps.org/program/nutrition-food-security/

programs.name: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support
programs.description: Mental health conditions are one of the great invisible health burdens for all societies. Every year, around one in ten people experience a mental health or substance abuse condition worldwide, yet nearly two thirds of people with a known mental health condition will never receive help. During emergencies, the percentage of those suffering common mental conditions can double. We are an acknowledged leader in meeting mental health and psychosocial needs during humanitarian crises, and advocate for integrating mental health into primary care. We have implemented mental health programs in more than 20 countries, including in emergency contexts. https://internationalmedicalcorps.org/program/mental-health-psychosocial-support/

leader.name: Nancy Aossey
leader.profile: Nancy Aossey has led International Medical Corps since 1986 and overseen its expansion to include the delivery of more than $4.5 billion of humanitarian assistance, health services, and training to tens of millions of people in over 80 countries. Ms. Aossey helped launch International Medical Corps' early programs in Angola, Somalia, and Rwanda. She has served as Chairman of the Board of InterAction, America's largest coalition of international relief and development organizations, and is a member of the Council on Foreign Relations, the RAND Global and Emerging Risk Board, Her Majesty Queen Rania Al-Abdullah’s Jordan River Foundation/USA, and the UCLA Health System Board. She is also a member of the Chief Executives Organization and the Young Presidents’ Organization.

name: Children of Conservation Inc
mission:
Many iconic African animals will become extinct within our lifetimes. The primary threats are hunting, habitat loss and disease. Chimpanzees and gorillas are hunted as a source of meat. In addition, entire families are killed to satisfy an ever-growing foreign pet trade. Elephants and rhinos are killed for their tusks and horns. Deforestation by foreign investors results in habitat loss for all these animals.

Children of Conservation is dedicated to the conservation and protection of endangered species through education, habitat preservation and wildlife sanctuary and conservation worker support.

programs.name: Scholarships
programs.description:
Our scholarship program has been running since 2009. In that time, we've made it possible for more than 900 children across five African countries to go to school.

The children we support are the kids of wildlife conservation workers. Their parents make a very modest salary and because they live in countries where education is not free, they often can't afford the school fees, uniforms, books and sometimes even boarding costs.

This means that children are growing up without opportunities.

Our scholarship program allows them to attend the best school in their area and there are eleven criteria that help us calculate the amount they receive. Kids can earn bonuses for consistently great grades and taking part in extra-curricular conservation activities.

We work directly with the sanctuaries or local authorities to distribute the funds directly to the schools.

We currently support the children of workers at Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary (Kenya), Limbe Wildlife Center (Cameroon), Ape Action Africa (Cameroon), Chimp Eden (South Africa) and Ngamba Island Chimpanzee Sanctuary (Uganda).

programs.name: Anti-Poaching Programs
programs.description:
KENYA
For the past four years, Children of Conservation has partnered with the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust to spearhead an anti-poaching initiative in villages surrounding the Tsavo National Parks.

In an effort to mitigate human impact on animals and to encourage communities to voluntarily cease the poaching of elephants for ivory, bushmeat or trade, we have been entering into agreements with village leaders. The purpose of this program is to create a buffer-zone around the national park , where the animals are not officially protected, by engaging local communities to participate in conservation.

The communities in and around this large park are primarily supported by pastoralism and other agriculture with few opportunities for new livelihood options. Hunting of elephants for profit is an ongoing and growing threat. It has been found that money from poaching was often used to pay school fees, pay for uniforms, transport and books for their brightest children to attend secondary school.

Children of Conservation is working with on-the-ground-partner, David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, in communities around Tsavo National Park with a history of elephant hunting but who now agree to cease elephant poaching activities in exchange for scholarships, administered carefully by CofC, for their top two students. Children of Conservation’s Anti-Poaching Initiative is designed to eliminate poaching and hunting for bush meat in and around the park. Our scholarships are the consideration given in exchange for a binding agreement with a village chief to ban poaching and promote wildlife conservation.

UGANDA
We are partnering with Uganda Wildlife Authority (UWA) to create a buffer-zone around Kidepo National Park, outside the area where the animals are officially protected, by engaging local communities to participate in conservation.

The volunteer Community Wildlife Scouts of the Kidepo Valley wildlife corridor have been recruited from communities surrounding the park border by Uganda Wildlife Authority community liaison staff and the Community Conservation Warden. In an effort to mitigate the human impact on the environment and for communities to continue to benefit from eco-tourism of visitors brought to the area by the national park, teams of scouts have been established.  They are currently effectively managing human-wildlife conflict and anti-poaching in the large wildlife dispersal area of more than 580 square miles.  However, the scouts, who are not armed, are facing threats from high level poachers who have much better technology and resources than they do.

The Uganda Wildlife Authority supports these scouts and trains them to arrest and detain poachers, collect evidence and then appear in court during proceedings to prosecute ivory traffickers. The scout patrols often spend multiple days away from home while patrolling a vast area of northern Uganda, rich with roaming elephants.

We aim to provide these teams with basic supplies to aid their work and technology to allow them to continue their great work to stop ivory hunters and to improve their ability to report, track and identify poachers.

programs.name: Myende Conservation Community
programs.description:
We are taking on a new incredibly impactful pilot project; transforming a poverty-stricken fishing village in Uganda with no access to formal education or healthcare, no running water or electricity, poor sanitation, limited clean water and no opportunity for skills development into a model conservation community that can be replicated across the continent.

This project is the collective vision of the community’s 22 leaders, the local and national governments, the Uganda Wildlife Authority and our partner sanctuary – Chimpanzee Sanctuary and Wildlife Conservation Trust. Together, we are developing a holistic approach to conservation through community empowerment, a focus on the United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals, alignment with Uganda’s Vision 2040 for Prosperity and a commitment to utilizing methodologies designed to reverse global warming and minimize climate change. This community will serve as a roadmap for Uganda in similar impoverished areas, as a pilot for similar projects throughout Africa, and as a showcase for the world to see opportunities for synergy between people, planet and prosperity.

The community chosen is the Myende fishing village off the coast of Entebbe in Uganda’s Lake Victoria, just minutes away from the Ngamba Island Chimpanzee Sanctuary and home to a biodiverse population of birds, many of which are unique to this area. Like most rural but environmentally important villages, Lake Victoria’s fishing villages are the most under-served communities in the country due to their remoteness and comparatively low population densities. Myende has a direct impact on the neighboring Chimpanzee Sanctuary, and is comparatively accessible. It is also located in an extremely biodiverse country that struggles to balance the immediate benefits of environmentally degrading investments in oil, minerals and agriculture with the long-term potential revenue stream from eco-tourism. For these reasons, it is an ideal pilot and model project.

programs.name: Fallen Wildlife Heroes
programs.description:
We are partnering with the Uganda Wildlife Authority to create the Fund for Fallen Heroes.

This fund will support the families of wildlife rangers killed in the line of duty. In the past five years, more than 20 wildlife workers in Uganda have lost their lives while protecting some of the world's most endangered and threatened animals. These heroes leave behind children and partners that often find themselves destitute without their main breadwinner's income.

Education is not free in Uganda and the children of these fallen fighters will grow up without an education unless we help them. Please give what you can today to help us show some compassion for these families.

Uganda Wildlife Authority employs some of the best respected conservationists in Africa and they deserve our support. Just last year, a UWA ranger was awarded the prestigious Tusk Award, presented by HRH Prince William. He is credited with increasing the lion population in Murchison Falls National Park from 200 to 1600. You can read more about that here: Wildlife Ranger Wins Award

UWA currently employs approximately 1,500 rangers to cover about 71,000 square kilometres of protected area.
World Ranger Day, which is marked on July 31, is held in remembrance of rangers who died in the line of duty.
According to International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), rangers in Uganda, DR Congo and Rwanda have been directly responsible for an increase in the number of mountain gorillas, risking their lives to ensure the survival of this critically endangered species.
In northern Uganda, human impact on the land means that native animals can only be found in national parks such as Kidepo National Park. Here, the conflict between humans and wildlife is a constant battle for park rangers. They often find themselves in dangerous situations as a result of poachers entering the park.

name: HomeMore Project Inc.
mission: Our Mission is to uplift the homeless community in California by building a culture of transparent and genuine relationships while focusing on the centralization of resources and providing realistic yet innovative solutions to an ongoing crisis.

programs.name: Makeshift Traveler
programs.description: At the core of all of our projects lies innovation, creativity, and a passion for bringing people together. We have spent the past year developing our Makeshift Traveler, a backpack specifically tailored toward the needs of an individual experiencing homelessness. With your help and contribution, you are not only providing an individual with a Makeshift Traveler and other short-term aid, but you are allowing our organization to utilize this as a vehicle to make connections with individuals who are interested in our Future Transitional Housing Program.

programs.name: Education Program
programs.description: Our Education Program is a dynamic platform that includes short films, a LearnMore Blog, and even a children's book. Through these mediums, we aimed to raise awareness and foster understanding about the complex issues surrounding homelessness.

leader.name: Zac Clark
leader.profile: Zac Clark is the founder and executive director of The HomeMore Project, a 501c3 nonprofit organization serving California's homeless community of nearly 180,000 people. Zac built the HomeMore Project while studying international business and marketing at the University of San Francisco. Upon his graduation in 2023, he received the Student Leadership Award and the Dean's Service Award for his impact on over 2,000 people experiencing homelessness combined in 2023 and 2024. In 2025, Zac and the HomeMore Project plan to launch a scalable transitional housing model, utilizing tiny homes. Zac is now a master’s in urban planning student concentrating on Economic Development and Housing at UCLA. He seeks to leverage resources and networking opportunities to continue building The HomeMore Project to become a household name in the State of California.

name: Active Cultures
mission: Active Cultures is a public arts nonprofit in Los Angeles that explores the intersection of art, food, and ecologies through artist-led projects and programs.

programs.name: Active Cultures Programming
programs.description: Active Cultures is a public arts organization based in Los Angeles that explores the intersection of art, food, and ecologies through artist-led projects and programs. Our work supports interdisciplinary, community-rooted cultural practices that reflect a wide range of lived experiences and local knowledge systems. All programs are offered free or on a sliding scale, and are designed to lower barriers to participation and engage intergenerational publics across Los Angeles. Our two core program areas are Artist Projects and Public Programs. Artist Projects provide funding, curatorial support, and multi-season engagement for artists whose work aligns with our mission. Projects often include community gatherings, meals, performances, and workshops, and are developed through extended dialogue between artists, staff, and local partners. Public Programs offer accessible points of entry into our artists’ work through performances, talks, walking gatherings, and community meals.

leader.name: Laura Fried
leader.profile: Laura Fried is a Los Angeles-based curator and is a co-founder and Director of Active Cultures, a nonprofit organization that explores the convergence of food and art in contemporary life. Throughout her career, Fried has advocated for artists and institutions while pushing forward new models for engagement and exhibition making, and remains deeply committed to projects that are artist-centered and interdisciplinary. She recently served as founding Artistic Director of the Seattle Art Fair, for which she organized a comprehensive program of large-scale installations, performances, talks, and projects. Fried was previously on the curatorial staff of Massachusetts Museum of Contemporary Art, North Adams, MA, as well as a curator at the Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis, where she organized major exhibitions with artists Spencer Finch, Carey Young, Sean Landers, Stephen Prina, Elad Lassry, Manon de Boer, and Richard Aldrich, among others.

name: Performing Arts Center of Los Angeles County
mission: On behalf of the County of Los Angeles, the Music Center is committed to building civic vitality by strengthening community through the arts. We accomplish this by bringing to life one of the world's premier performing arts centers and by providing distinctive leadership and diverse opportunities for life-long learning and engagement with arts and culture.

programs.name: Education Programs
programs.description: Music Center Education Programs provide comprehensive services for K-12 schools and districts in LA County as well as performances, festivals and events for the general public. These include in-school initiatives, the in-depth Artist Teacher Partnership program, artist training and development, curriculum materials, professional development for educators, advocacy, World City international performance series, the annual Very Special Arts Festival, and the yearly Blue Ribbon Children's Festival.

leader.name: Rachel S. Moore
leader.profile:
Rachel S. Moore is president and CEO of The Music Center, Los Angeles' premier performing arts center. In that capacity, she leads the $65 million company that manages The Music Center campus and operates and programs Grand Park on behalf of the County of Los Angeles. In addition, Moore oversees The Music Center's work as a presenter and curator of programming, including its internationally acclaimed dance series, Glorya Kaufman Presents Dance at The Music Center, as well as a number of innovative programs, events and activities that are introducing new audiences to the performing arts. In addition, she guides The Music Center's multi-faceted arts education initiatives, which reach children and youth all over Southern California.
Moore joined The Music Center from American Ballet Theatre (ABT), one of the world's great dance companies, where she served as CEO since 2011 and as its executive director since 2004.

name: Clockshop
mission: Clockshop works with artists to deepen the connection between communities and public land, in order to build a shared vision of a future based in belonging and care. As a Los Angeles-based arts and culture nonprofit, Clockshop produces free public programming and commissions contemporary artist projects on public land to better connect Angelenos to the land we live on.

programs.name: Community & Unity Peoples' Kite Festival
programs.description: This free, all-ages, family-friendly cultural festival brings together diverse communities in Los Angeles through the art of kites and a day of joyful connection at Los Angeles State Historic Park in Chinatown. Clockshop invites attendees to participate in free arts workshops, enjoy live music, and meet local community organizations to learn about their work in the nearby neighborhoods. The Kite Festival is designed as a celebration to honor the communities surrounding Los Angeles State Historic Park that fought for and steward this public parkland, recognizing their resilience, cultural histories, and aspirations.

programs.name: Sotomayor Youth at the Greenway
programs.description: Clockshop collaborated with Sotomayor High School on a multidisciplinary curriculum centering the nearby Ed P. Reyes River Greenway. Borne out of a desire to reactivate this space, a daylit water filtration site in Lincoln Heights, this curriculum encourages students to explore the future of the Greenway through the lenses of oral histories, math, art, and agriscience. Ed P. Reyes, former member of the Los Angeles City Council and one of our Take Me to Your River participants, has actively participated in this partnership. Throughout the school year, students worked alongside their teachers and with the guidance of experts to develop various proposals for the Greenway. In May 2024, students hosted an open house event at the Greenway to showcase their final proposals for the reactivation of the site. Local residents, stakeholders, and partners listened to students as they shared their visions of the future for the space.

programs.name: Summer Youth Arts & Advocacy Fellowship
programs.description: Clockshop’s Summer Art & Advocacy Youth Fellowship is a 6-week-long, cohort-based summer program for a small group of high school students in Northeast Los Angeles. The program combines outdoor exploration and art-making with public space advocacy training. The fellowship is tuition-free, and fellows directly receive a $2,500 award to be used towards future educational endeavors. Over the course of the summer, fellows learn about the ecology of the Los Angeles River and our local public lands and parks, collaborate with professional artists, explore political strategies for advocating for public space in Los Angeles, grow leadership skills as they imagine and actualize a collaborative final project, and build community with other high schoolers from across Northeast Los Angeles.

programs.name: Take Me To Your River
programs.description: Take Me to Your River: A Cultural Atlas of the LA River, is a three-year collective history and cultural mapping project initiated by the Los Angeles-based arts organization Clockshop. Take Me to Your River aims to celebrate the diverse experiences of those who call Northeast LA home. In specific, neighborhoods that surround the Glendale Narrows section of the Los Angeles River, including Elysian Valley, Atwater Village, Cypress Park, and Glassell Park. The project is a celebration of the communities that make up Northeast LA, and a dynamic reflection on how this area is rapidly and drastically changing. As gentrification displaces local residents, it also erases the complex histories of these neighborhoods.

programs.name: Reading and Listening by Moonrise
programs.description: Listening by Moonrise is a quarterly music series, held at the Los Angeles State Historic Park on the eve of the full moon (or as close to it). Listening by Moonrise features performances and immersive sound experiences with leading multi-disciplinary sound artists. This program offers listeners moments of reflection, connection, and joy while experiencing music and sound collectively within the context of a community-centered green space. Reading by Moonrise is a quarterly reading series, formerly held at the Bowtie Project on the eve of the full moon. Authors, journalists and playwrights were invited to read original and favorite texts along the banks of the LA River. Guests were encouraged to bring picnic items and blankets as they gather around the fire for s’mores and stories.

programs.name: Artist Commissions
programs.description: We partner with artists to produce place-based contemporary art installations on public land in Los Angeles. We believe art can be a portal through which we glimpse a different, brighter future, and a catalyst for an emotional connection to place. Recent artist commissions include The Light of Many Suns by April Banks, What Water Wants by Rosten Woo, and Por El Río by Christopher Suarez with Carlos Agredano, Diana Yesenia Alvarado, and timo fahler.

programs.name: The Future Bowtie State Park
programs.description: Over the past decade, Clockshop has partnered with California State Parks to produce dozens of artist commissions and over 110 public programs at the undeveloped Bowtie parcel along the Glendale Narrows section of the LA River and Los Angeles State Historic Park. Our approach to programming has focused on centering the stories of communities who have been historically marginalized and displaced. At the end of 2022, Clockshop officially became a Cooperating Association with California State Parks, which solidified our decade-long partnership. We continue to work with State Parks staff and The Nature Conservancy (TNC) on planning and programmatic designs for the new Bowtie State Park, including a new permanent artwork with artist Rosten Woo for TNC’s Bowtie Wetland Demonstration Project, a stormwater capture, nature-based water filtration system that will also become a beautiful river-adjacent wetland and provide much-needed habitat for native riparian species.

name: INTERNATIONAL FOUNDATION FOR WORLD FREEDOM
mission: The mission of IFWF is to protect the human rights of refugees, victims of war, and armed conflicts. We stand for safe resettlement of immigrants and their families; protection for those who seek harbor in fear for life and persecution is our focus. IFWF accomplishes its mission by charitable programs in social services and emergency assistance.
ntee_code: R20 - Civil Rights, Advocacy for Specific Groups

programs.name: Products 4 Home
programs.description: IFWF accomplishes its mission by charitable programs in social services and emergency assistance. Over a dozen years have passed since we opened our doors, and the world has changed. Countries have been destroyed; people flee in fear for their life in masses. At IFWF, we hear cries of children. They are suffering through a living hell; tortured, killed, maimed, turned into suicide bombers, imprisoned, and starved to death. Children are paying the highest price in numerous wars around the world today. IFWF has been providing social services for immigrants for the past 14 years. The changing world and the state of armed conflicts today direct our focus to the needs of children. Our mission and capabilities will first serve refugee children, the largest, most indigent, and most vulnerable group.

programs.name: Network for Good
programs.description: Membership driven Network for public charities. Services for members include re-granting of household products, toys, and appliances in bulk for distribution to qualified individuals in need.

programs.name: Immigration for Refugees
programs.description: We provide immigration services by referring refugees to legal consultants and advocating for their human rights.

programs.name: Financial Literacy for Refugees Educational Program
programs.description: It is evident IFWF continues to play a vital role in the lives of low-and no-income immigrants and refugees in providing these essential resources, however, we also acknowledge that in order to achieve our mission we must provide other services outside of our current scope. Therefore, we have decided to introduce a new program which offers essential Financial Literacy to these vulnerable populations. IFWF is developing a new program that will serve the same vulnerable populations. In the United States, it is exceedingly difficult for immigrants to gain knowledge about personal finance, especially considering barriers such as insufficient grasp of the English language or the inability to access online resources. IFWF seeks to bridge this information gap by creating a Financial Literacy course specifically geared towards immigrants and refugees. The course will help newcomers learn the U.S. economic system and will give the tools necessary to budget, save money, and develop good credit.

leader.name: Yuliya Davtyan
leader.profile: Yuliya Davtyan is the Founder and President of the International Foundation for World Freedom (IFWF), a nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering refugees, immigrants, and underserved communities through educational, humanitarian, and cultural programs. With a background in law and nonprofit leadership, Yuliya has led the creation of innovative projects in financial literacy, immigrant support, and cross-cultural education. She is deeply committed to building a diverse and inclusive society and works tirelessly to expand opportunities for individuals and families in need.

name: A Radical Guide
mission: To connect, amplify, and unite liberation movements by preserving their histories, amplifying their present struggles, and fostering transformative spaces for education, dialogue, and collective action. A Radical Guide serves as a resource hub and community builder, supporting grassroots efforts to advance justice, equality, and collective liberation.
contact_title: CEO / President of the Board of Directors

programs.name: Community Engagement
programs.description: A Radical Guide’s Community Engagement efforts are dedicated to fostering a globally connected network of activists while amplifying diverse voices and facilitating collaboration. Through building connections, sharing resources, and creating platforms, we support inclusive participation and collective action. Global Network Building: Strengthens relationships among radical activists and groups worldwide by facilitating collaboration and resource sharing. Amplifies perspectives and experiences from communities resisting oppression, ensuring their voices shape global conversations. Publications: Develops and shares resources like Liberation: Principles and Practices for Social Transformation, offering insights into radical principles, practices, and movements. Highlights the ongoing work and histories of liberation movements to inspire and inform collective action.

programs.name: Educational Programs
programs.description: A Radical Guide's Educational Programs connect and amplify liberation movements by fostering collective knowledge and practical skills. These programs include two key components: Workshops and Seminars and the Interactive Online Repository. Workshops and Seminars: Global virtual workshops and seminars that bridge historical struggles with present-day resistance through practical activism, mutual aid, and community organizing. Events designed to strengthen skills, share movement knowledge, and build solidarity networks across geographies and struggles. Interactive Online Repository: A dynamic archive of liberation movement histories and resistance strategies, including interactive maps, podcasts, guides, and documentation. We also produced print publications such as the Journal of Liberation, Liberation: Principles and Practices for Social Transformation, and Resist Project 2025: A Radical Guide to Countering Authoritarianism in the U.S. (first and second editions).

programs.name: Mutual Aid Programs
programs.description: Mutual Aid Program The Mutual Aid Program at A Radical Guide (ARG) embodies our commitment to fostering resistance and solidarity within communities working for liberation. This program includes two key components: Mutual Aid Fund: A collective resource pool providing sustained monthly support to grassroots organizations. Directly supports communities resisting oppression and building collective power. Movement Support Fund: Solidarity funding for radical groups and collectives advancing liberation projects. Supports efforts to preserve movement histories, connect struggles, and create systemic change.

programs.name: Farmworker Rental Assistance Program
programs.description: A Radical Guide and Center for Farmworker Families are partnering to prevent homelessness and housing instability for farmworker families facing unemployment or underemployment. This program provides direct rental support—no bureaucracies, no delays—just real solidarity with those who put food on our tables while struggling to keep a roof over their own. Together, we can raise $1,000 a month for each family and build a model rooted in dignity.

leader.name: Jason Bayless
leader.profile: Jason Bayless is a prominent social justice activist who has dedicated over two decades to promoting animal rights, advocating for farmworker families, and fighting for a more just and equitable society. He co-created PETA2, PETA's youth division, and served as President of the Board for the Center for Farmworker Families. As a National Board member for Move to Amend and a member of the Democracy Unlimited Board, he campaigns to end corporate personhood and promote democratic principles. In 2018, Bayless founded A Radical Guide, a platform highlighting radical history and fostering community-building initiatives. His leadership has built an extensive network of activists, enhancing resource sharing and inspiring collective action for social transformation. Bayless’s deep commitment to social justice has earned him widespread respect in the activist community.

name: The Prem Rawat Foundation
mission: The mission of The Prem Rawat Foundation (TPRF) is to advance dignity, peace and prosperity by addressing the fundamental human needs of food, water and peace. Through a variety of programs and initiatives, TPRF is dedicated to building a world at peace, one person at a time.

programs.name: Food for People
programs.description: Food for People (FFP) takes an innovative approach to helping people emerge from poverty by providing nutritious meals, clean water and educational opportunities to disadvantaged communities in India, Nepal and Ghana. By the end of 2023, the FFP program had provided clean water and over 5.6 million meals to children and ailing adults, as well as classes on computer skills, sewing, agriculture, physical education and more. The program has resulted in improved health, higher school enrollment and achievement and economic growth.

programs.name: Peace Education Program
programs.description:
The Peace Education Program is an innovative series of video-based workshops that help people discover their own inner strength and personal peace. The program gives participants the opportunity to focus and reflect on their own humanity, and their inner resources such as choice, hope and dignity. Rather than describing or defining personal peace, the program empowers individuals to reach their own understanding. Everyone can benefit. The program has proven effective in a variety of settings including community centers, high schools and universities, adult education programs,  healthcare settings, senior centers, homeless shelters, drug rehabilitation facilities and correctional facilities. 

Over 400,000 people in more than 80 countries have participated in the program, and impact studies have found a wide range of benefits, including reducing anxiety, increasing self-awareness and personal growth, and enhancing hope and appreciation for life.

programs.name: Public Events and Forums
programs.description: TPRF has sponsored more than 45 live events and forums with Prem Rawat and other leaders to build awareness that personal peace is the strongest foundation for world peace, including at prominent institutions such as the United Nations and European Parliament. TPRF has reached hundreds of millions of people on social media and other online platforms with inspiring messages that encourage positive and peaceful living.

programs.name: Disaster Relief
programs.description: TPRF regularly provides disaster relief in partnership with other nonprofit organizations, especially addressing underserved areas. In addition, TPRF sponsors eye clinics in disadvantaged rural areas of India and Nepal to provide eye exams, eye infection medications and corrective lenses at no charge to people who could not otherwise afford them. TPRF has given over 175 grants totaling over $6.3 million to a variety of NGO partners in 40 countries to provide food, water, medical care and other aid.

leader.name: Linda Pascotto
leader.profile:
Born in San Mateo, California, Mrs. Pascotto attended Girls' Collegiate High School in Claremont, California, where she graduated with honors. She continued her education at the University of Denver, where she received a degree in political science.

Mrs. Pascotto has had a lifelong interest in philanthropy and supports directly and through her private foundation many charitable organizations that promote specific cultural, social, and educational work.

Married with two grown sons, Mrs. Pascotto lives in Zephyr Cove, Lake Tahoe, Nevada and has taken an active interest in several organizations in that area including Barton Memorial Hospital, Lake Tahoe Community College, and both the Reno public broadcasting station and the Reno public radio station.

Mrs. Pascotto travels throughout the world in pursuit of her primary passion of supporting and participating in activities involving Prem Rawat and TPRF.

name: Still Bisexual
mission: Our mission is to foster public acceptance, awareness and understanding of bisexual, pansexual, fluid, and queer identities and the challenges they face; to develop and promote self-acceptance, personal empowerment and visibility among bisexual, pansexual, fluid, and queer people; and to foster inclusivity and acceptance for bisexual, pansexual, fluid and queer people among the larger LGBTQIA+ community.

programs.name: Sacred Space
programs.description: Virtual wellness events for the Black LGBTQ+ community.

programs.name: Bi+ Affirming Mentorship and Storytelling Lab
programs.description: Program funded by the Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health that will launch in 2024 and bridge the inter-generational gap between elder bi+ people and bi+ youth with a common lived experience.

programs.name: Still Bisexual videos and Still Bisexual education programs and curriculum
programs.description: Our Flagship program educating the public and bisexuals about bisexuality as an identity and reality using short, engaging videos made by Bi+ folks.

programs.name: Bi+ Mental Health Justice Coalition with #Out4MentalHealth
programs.description: Advocating for mental health equity for bi+ people across Los Angeles County. Funded by the #Out4MentalHealth program via the Health Access Foundation

name: My Serenity Sanctuary
mission: Our mission is to address the unique challenges primarily Black women and girls face and to create inclusive spaces that foster healing, self-discovery, and personal growth. Through a combination of therapeutic programs, workshops, events, supportive resources, and our fabulous online community, we strive to empower women and girls of color to prioritize their mental, emotional, and physical health. We also advocate for policies and initiatives that support the health and wellness needs of our target population. By fostering a sense of community, celebrating cultural identity, and promoting holistic self-care practices, My Serenity Sanctuary aims to uplift and positively impact the lives of the 1.2 million Black women in girls in California.

programs.name: EmpowerHer Self-Care & Wellness Program
programs.description: An 8-week self-care and wellness education workshop series for women in underserved communities. We offer this program to other nonprofits, community partners, and other organizations that serve our population.

programs.name: Girls2Great
programs.description: The Girls2Great program takes a programmatic approach to supporting the self-care and well-being of young women between the ages 13-17. The programming includes self-care and wellness workshops, health & fitness classes, listening circles and other activities that are unique to young ladies and can help them, build their confidence, self-esteem and relationships. The goal is to create a safe space for our young Black girls to find their voice and learn to protect the emotional, physical and mental health.

programs.name: My Serenity Sanctuary's Self-Care Summit
programs.description: Serenity Sanctuary's Self-Care Summit is an annual event dedicated to promoting self-care and well-being for Black women and girls. This transformative gathering brings together a community of individuals who are passionate about prioritizing their mental, emotional, and physical health. The summit is designed to provide a safe and inclusive space where attendees can engage in various empowering activities, workshops, and discussions centered around self-care practices. The goal is to equip participants with the tools, knowledge, and resources to cultivate a sustainable self-care routine supporting their overall well-being. During the Self-Care Summit, renowned experts and speakers specializing in various fields, such as mental health, mindfulness, fitness, nutrition, and personal development, share their insights and guidance. They lead interactive workshops, facilitate engaging discussions, and provide practical tips and strategies for incorporating self-care into everyday life.

programs.name: MySS Online Community
programs.description: My Serenity Sanctuary's Online Community is a virtual space that fosters connection, support, and empowerment for individuals seeking to prioritize self-care and well-being. This inclusive community brings together a diverse group of individuals, particularly Black women and girls, who share the goal of nurturing their mental, emotional, and physical health. The Online Community serves as a membership platform where members can engage in meaningful discussions, share experiences, seek advice, and offer support to one another. It provides a safe and non-judgmental space where individuals can express themselves authentically and find solace in knowing they are not alone on their self-care journey.

leader.name: Dr. Gena Yuvette Davis
leader.profile:
My Serenity Sanctuary holds a profound significance for me, not only as the founder and board chair but also as a passionate advocate for social change and equality. In a world where disparities in access to wellness resources are all too common, especially for Black women and girls, My Serenity Sanctuary serves as a vital lifeline. It is more than just an organization; it is a movement dedicated to empowering those who have historically been marginalized and overlooked.

The urgency of our work is underscored by the systemic barriers that often prevent Black women and girls from accessing the resources they deserve. Through fundraising, innovative programming, and interactive community building, we strive to dismantle these barriers and ensure that wellness is not a privilege but a right. My Serenity Sanctuary is committed to making self-care accessible and inclusive, advocating for holistic health that encompasses the mind, body, and spirit.

name: Social Justice Legal Foundation
mission: Advancing social justice by focusing on groundbreaking trial work and innovative collaboration across private, public and academic sectors. Our trial lawyers, veterans of historic cases, work closely with the next generation of leaders in the law to prevail in the nations most impactful, precedent-setting cases.

name: WalkGood LA
mission: WalkGood LA is a family-led wellness 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization providing equitable healing spaces for underrepresented communities and individuals.

programs.name: BreatheGood
programs.description:
BreatheGood is WalkGood LA's large-scale community yoga class, occurring once a month on Sundays, often located at Kenneth Hahn State Park in Baldwin Hills, California. Each class averages about 250, sometimes up to 400 individuals. As with all community experiences, BreatheGood is a free, donation-based experience, and friendly for families, all ages, all walks of life, and all levels. The value that yoga is for everyone is holds true here at BreatheGood.  

BreatheGood programming includes an hour long or more of guided breath work, meditation, and yoga. 
To elevate the experience, BreatheGood also features live DJ's, a wellness-based vendor market, food trucks, partner collaborations, giveaways and more. 

Follow us on socials and sign up for our newsletter via walkgoodla.org to join the community.

programs.name: HikeGood
programs.description: HikeGood is WalkGood LA's quarterly community hike.  We trek through trails all across LA county and outside of county lines with groups that often reach numbers of 50 or more. As with all experiences, HikeGood is an inclusive experience meant for anyone that wants to enjoy the outdoors in nature experience with a supportive group. Most hikes are family friendly.

programs.name: RunGood
programs.description: RunGood is WalkGood LA's weekly 5K community run. And when we say community run, we really mean it. No one is left behind during a RunGood experience. Runners encourage one another and help each other reach the finish line. The energy is high and contagious as we aim to make running not just fun but something that anyone can feel like they can do on a consistent basis. All levels are welcome. WalkGood LA also offers a concurrent walking group for those that want to get in their miles, but don't want to run just yet.  Supervised children are welcome.

programs.name: YouGood? A Black Men's Healing Circle
programs.description:
YouGood? is WalkGood LA's monthly Black Men's Healing Circle; however, we stand with open arms and welcome all men-identifying individuals of all ages, creeds, and backgrounds. It is open to anyone that wants to join. Vulnerability is encouraged during every circle. Experiences are shared openly and without judgment. 

Programming for YouGood? includes guided meditation, yoga, a sound bath, and closes with a section dedicated to prompted journaling followed by group breakout discussions and open mic opportunities. Each experience lasts approximately 2 hours and is held at The WalkGood Yard, WalkGood LA's creative wellness study located in Arlington Heights, Los Angeles. 

Supervised children are welcome. This experience is free, donation-based.

programs.name: YouGood Gyal? A Black Women's Healing Circle
programs.description:
YouGood Gyal? is WalkGood LA's quarterly Black women's healing circle.  The term "gyal" is an homage to the Jamaican heritage of WalkGood LA.  

YouGood Gyal?  brings all female-identifying individuals from all walks of life together through meditation, breath work, journaling, yoga, and intentional group conversation & community-building exercises.  Each experience offers a safe space that aims to  foster sisterhood through dialogue, movement, and breath.  Yougood Gyal? reminds women of their worth and empowers them to heal and thrive in the face of challenges. Each experience lasts approximately 2 hours and is held at The WalkGood Yard, WalkGood LA's creative wellness study located in Arlington Heights, Los Angeles. Supervised children as welcome. This experience is free, donation-based.

programs.name: FilmGood
programs.description:
FILMGOOD is the first ever film & wellness festival, bringing together community while pushing the needle forward through the power of storytelling. Held in the heart of Los Angeles, FilmGood is an annual 2-3 day festival that includes the following programming:  screening block of short films, informative industry panels, constant networking opportunities, and multiple wellness experiences for a robust community of Black & Brown filmmakers and creatives. 

Accessible spaces are created to explore the intersection of wellness & storytelling. FilmGood is a platform for everyone in attendance to tell share their stories,  and has created a forum that continues to find ways to normalize mental health in the entertainment industry.  The inaugural FilmGood was held in March 2023 and looks to expand each year.

programs.name: SoulGood
programs.description:
SoulGood: Healing Through Music is an initiative that takes place annually during Grammy Weekend, bringing to the community a weekend of wellness, sound, discourse, and change-making.  As the only wellness and community-centered initiative during Grammy weekend in 2023, the first SoulGood was a big step forward in normalizing the conversations and struggles of mental health in the music industry while providing resources and healing spaces. The theme of Healing Through Music was felt throughout our activations as we served as an accessible bridge for those not only continuing their mental health journeys, but those starting out.

Programming includes: guided yoga, meditation, breath work, panels, mixers, and live music. SoulGood 2023 was in partnership with Soulection, On, and Backline Care.

programs.name: The WalkGood Yard
programs.description:
The WalkGood Yard is WalkGood LA's creative wellness studio located in Arlington Heights, Los Angeles. 
It is a multi-purpose space that functions as a yoga/wellness studio throughout the week, but is also open to rentals for a diverse range of classes, workshops, and events, from live performances to film screenings. The WalkGood Yard will have its grand opening in February 2024. We hope to have a significant positive impact on the community with the opening of this space in providing more accessible and safe wellness resources and opportunities. 


The WalkGood Yard was made possible with the help of Propel Fitness Water and Michael B. Jordan. 
Address: 4019 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90019

name: Advot
mission: Advot uses the power of artistic exploration to empower young people to find their voice and grow into courageous and effective self-advocates.
ntee_code: I70 - Protection Against and Prevention of Neglect, Abuse, Exploitation

programs.name: Listen-Act-Change
programs.description:
Our core program, Listen-Act-Change (“LAC”), engages teens and young adults in introspection and reflection on how even the smallest choices made in a split-second can have a lasting impact on their future. We teach that every individual has the power to make better choices. As they participate in expressive theater, visual art, music, dance, and writing exercises, LAC participants build skills to become their own best advocates and reach their full potential.

LAC workshops each explore healthy communication skills that fall within five communication streams. These are:
1. Intentional listening,
2. Authentic stories,
3. Start with “I” (Accountability),
4. Speaking your truth, and
5. Recognizing perspective.

For over a decade, LAC has been offered at youth-serving sites across Southern CA, with a primary focus on LA County juvenile detention facilities to support youth who are most in need of help learning to express themselves, apply critical thinking, and navigate their world.

leader.name: Ms. Naomi Ackerman
leader.profile:
Since the late 1990s, The Advot Project’s Executive Director and Founder Naomi Ackerman has been performing and facilitating workshops globally that focus on the dynamics of abuse and domestic violence. Centered on her acclaimed one woman show, Flowers Aren’t Enough, these workshops inspired and informed the development of Relationships 101, a drama-based curriculum that teaches healthy relationship skills to teens and young adults. 

Ms. Ackerman founded The Advot Project (“Advot”) in 2011, with the mission to prepare youth for success in life. Ms. Ackerman was awarded an UpStart Labs Fellowship in 2019, and today, she continues to fight for the rights of detained youth and incarcerated young adults, and spends her time in lock-up facilities, group homes, and re-entry programs  teaching relationship skills through the arts.

name: theatre dybbuk
mission: theatre dybbuk creates provocative performances and innovative educational encounters that explore Jewish thought to illuminate universal human experience. We envision a world where people challenge themselves to revel in the complexity of our shared humanity.

name: WESTCOAST SPORTS ASSOCIATES INC
mission: Westcoast Sports Associates' (WSA) purpose is to provide economically disadvantaged children an opportunity to participate in high quality sports programs. The organization has funded community programs and activities at numerous city recreation facilities and nonprofit organizations administering youth sports and character education programs in under-served neighborhoods located in Southern California. WSA has allocated $3.5 million over the years to programs throughout Southern California to achieve its mission of Making Youth Sports Possible. Young people need safe, healthy activities to build their confidence and help develop social skills. WSA's network of administrators make youth sports accessible to over 10,000 young people every year.
ntee_code: N12 - Fund Raising and/or Fund Distribution

programs.name: Annual Youth Sports Grant Funding
programs.description: The primary goal of Westcoast Sports Associates is to help economically disadvantaged children play sports. Youth sports programs provide safe environments for children outside of school and the home to develop healthy habits and build character. The mentorship and role modeling facilitated by coaches and volunteers have a lasting impact on the next generation!

name: Woodcraft Rangers
mission: Guiding young people as they explore pathways to purposeful lives.

programs.name: Expanded Learning
programs.description: PHILOSOPHY Through the Fourfold Woodcraft Way, a precursor to the modern whole child educational model, a young person develops an authentic and holistic sense of self through play the cultivation of body, mind, spirit and service. Believing that maturity, not scholarship, is the first aim of education, the Woodcraft Way builds character and equips youth with strength and resiliency, new skills, deeper understanding of their place in the world, and greater commitment to their community. The Woodcraft Way encourages individuals to find, test, and explore their strengths, in the company of friends and committed guides, who provide a sense of belonging and support so that they may grow confidently in many directions. Woodcraft harnesses personal power that gives each participant the tools needed to be reflective and the inspiration to set and then strive towards personal goals. From Woodcraft’s inception, the central fire has served as its unifying symbol and has illustrated our commitment, for nearly a century, to cultivating an inclusive environment that has always welcomed and honored diverse participants and perspectives. Finally, nature is a critical element in this journey of self-discovery for Woodcrafters as it brings physical and mental restoration from our modern existence. Woodcrafters are eager to learn, inspired by vision, and willing to lead. OUR WORK Woodcraft Rangers programs are anchored in a holistic educational framework that encompasses all areas of a young person’s development. With student interests at the center of our program design, Woodcraft Rangers offers opportunities for youth to explore and develop themselves through various pathways, including Sports, Arts & Media, STEM, Dual Language Enrichment, Health & Wellness, and Youth Leadership. Our longstanding delivery of service has enabled us to impact the lives of hundreds of thousands of young people over the years, ranging in age from 5 to 18 years. Our longevity is evidence that we have always been responsive to the changing needs of our communities and we continue to build and adapt around the current issues facing our youth. Our cumulative demographics mirror the rich diversity of Woodcraft Rangers communities within the Greater Los Angeles area. This encompasses South Los Angeles, San Gabriel Valley, Vernon, Huntington Park, South Gate, and San Fernando Valley. Woodcraft participants identify as Hispanic (80%), African-American (10%), Asian/Pacific Islander (7%), and Caucasian (3%). They are 51% male and 49% female. SIGNATURE PROGRAMS By providing youth with a safe space and a variety of options to test and learn, coupled with active mentorship and the encouragement to try and win or fail, Woodcraft Rangers affords young people with the opportunity to grow. Our experience has shown that when youth are given agency to choose the subjects and activities that inspire and motivate them, not only can learning be fun, it can be transformational. AFTERSCHOOL ENRICHMENT PROGRAMS In 2020, our programs will serve approximately 15,000 students, equating to 7.5 million hours of learning and mentorship for LA’s youth in communities showing the greatest need. All aftershool opportunities are offered either outside of normal school hours or during holidays, enabling parents to maintain employment during out-of-school hours knowing their children are safe. Unique to Woodcraft’s program, students have access to over 100 different enrichment clubs, providing participants with the ability to explore their own interests and develop new skills. Clubs are organized into 6 main learning pathways: Arts & Media, Dual Language Enrichment, Egalitarian Sports, Health & Wellness, STEM, and Youth Leadership. Woodcraft Rangers Club Leaders and Site Coordinators curate activities to meet the specific needs of the students at each site and dovetail with the unique dynamics of each neighborhood and community. Social and emotional learning and trauma informed practices a

programs.name: Camp Woodcraft
programs.description: Our Residential Summer Camp, comprised of one week stays in Big Bear, California, is the heart of Woodcraft Rangers. We believe that children learn through play and should have the opportunity to take developmentally appropriate risks that build resiliency and independence. This sense of autonomy is nurtured through mentoring by trained instructors and counselors who are equipped to support the social, emotional, and physical development of every child. In each week-long session, over 100 young people engage in nature-based activities designed to build and enhance confidence, conflict resolution skills, communication, teamwork, and perhaps most importantly, connectedness to one another and to nature. Nature is a critical element in this journey of self-discovery for Woodcrafters as it brings physical and mental restoration and a respite from our modern existence. Research also shows that this immersive nature experience helps young people to recalibrate in a world of digital overload. Woodcraft Rangers has stayed true to the founding principles of access and inclusion, and our intentionally diverse camps create a unique opportunity as a laboratory for social cohesion.

leader.name: Julee Brooks
leader.profile: Julee Brooks is an experienced nonprofit strategist and changemaker with a solid track record of leading family and youth-focused organizations through periods of dynamic growth in program delivery, earned revenue and fundraising. Julee's areas of expertise include strategic planning, improving organizational efficiency, board development, and access and inclusion. Julee brings direct experience in arts and culture, youth development and human services including roles as Executive Director of the Los Angeles Ronald McDonald House, Museum Director of the Zimmer Children’s Museum (Los Angeles) and as Director of Education at Nashville Children’s Theatre. Julee holds an MFA in Theatre for Youth from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro, and a BA from Centre College. She lives with her husband Ross and two sons, Ryder and Duncan, in La Crescenta.

name: Youth Mentoring Connection
mission: YMC's mission is to transform the lives of at-risk youth by caring for their wounds and shining a light on their gifts, through participation within an asynchronous mentoring community, creative expression, and life-changing experiences; thus inspiring them to become thriving adults. The organization's vision is to influence safe communities worldwide using our Gifts Centered Approach to bring vital connection, love and healing into the lives of opportunity youth, so they may live fully into their passion and purpose.

programs.name: YMC Youth Advisory Council
programs.description: YMC’s Youth Advisory Council was developed to assist YMC in identifying programs and other needs to best serve young people. The up to 10-member council identifies projects then plans and executes them. YMC staff and other experts provide information and tools to assist them and are available for guidance if needed. This year’s project is focused on conducting a Youth Program Needs survey. The information gathered from this project will be used to develop new programs at YMC. Youth Advisory Council members gain valuable skills in leadership, collaborative project planning and execution, team work, and many other skills.

programs.name: Urban Oasis Youth Center
programs.description: YMC’s Urban Oasis Youth Center (UOYC) provides youth with a connection to YMC’s core mentoring, youth support, and positive youth development activities. It’s also a place where YMC partners can provide youth services and classes—including our long-time partners Street Poets to provide creative expression through poetry and Rhythm Alliance to teach African Drumming circles and dance. There are computer stations for schoolwork and job searches; a space for on-site counselling; space for creative expression such as dance, music, and film; recreational activities; dedicated on site staff; workshops and programs to prepare young people for adulthood; and so much more. YMC also contracts with a therapist to provide on-site counselling. YMC’s trademarked Gift Centered approach which is based on the premise that our gifts lie next to our wounds and to fully live into our authentic selves, these need to be uncovered, is woven through all youth programs and activities.

programs.name: Mentoring for underserved Los Angeles Youth
programs.description: Since 2001, Youth mentoring Connection (YMC has positively impacted over 8,000 vulnerable youth through dedicated and caring adult mentors who provide long-term consistent support and guide them toward developing positive characters, good decision-making skills, enhanced self-esteem, and bringing their gift into the world.

programs.name: Community-Based Mentoring Programs
programs.description: Community-based mentoring programs match at-risk high school and middle school students with caring adult volunteers for highly structured and supported mentoring programs. • Children’s Hospital, as part of the Mayor’s Gang Reduction Youth Initiative • California Community Foundation (CCF), as part of PAT (Preparing Achievers for Tomorrow) increasing youth participation in organized sports, music and recreation in Los Angeles which includes our Surf Program • L.A. County Probation Department, to identify and recruit young black males and redirect them through employment and education opportunities through the CCF BLOOM (Building a Lifetime of Options and Opportunities for Men) initiative.

programs.name: Youth Support
programs.description: Intensive staff support for youth in mentoring programs who are in crisis. Support includes: counseling, transportation, housing referrals, and intensive mentoring and guidance by YMC Youth Support Workers, known as the "street team."

programs.name: Mentee Initiation Retreat
programs.description: This flagship YMC program offers an intense, 4-day experience which prepares youth to enter their mentoring relationships. 100 high school-aged mentors and mentees travel with staff and mentors to Big Bear each fall to participate as a community in vital rites of passage missing from our society. Specific Retreat Program activities include: Ice breaker (get to know each other) activities, Drumming, Reading, Poetry Writing, Mask and Gift Making, Horseback Riding, Conquering a Ropes Course and a Rock Wall, Nighttime Campfire Story Telling, Nature Hiking, Singing, and Tolerance, Conflict Resolution, and Violence Prevention Workshops.

programs.name: YMC Surfing Program
programs.description: Due to socio-economic conditions in urban communities, youth are increasingly becoming disconnected from positive and healthy pursuits. Too often they turn to the influences of drugs, alcohol, violence or gangs. The surfing community that we create connects with at-risk youth through the exhilaration of surfing in order to broaden their life experiences with positive, healthy, non-competitive activities that may have a significant impact on their self-image and self-confidence. Youth involved in our surfing programs learn the sport in a fun, supportive environment under the supervision of experienced surfers who share the positive impact that surfing has had on their lives. The program runs 6 Sundays a summer for 60-70 youth. YMC provides transportation; insurance; and staff members to coordinate the transportation, releases, equipment set-up, surf boards, rash guards, water & food, canopies, and volunteers on the day of the event. To date, over 1,000 youth have participated in this transformative surfing program. For many of our youth, this means seeing the beach for the first time in their lives and others, who did not know how to swim, learning to be comfortable in the water. Our youth face enormous obstacles and live in high crime areas where they are constantly exposed to gangs, drugs, and violence. Surfing is a retreat from the daily environment they face, and many use the sea to heal their wounds.

leader.name: Tony LoRe
leader.profile:
Tony LoRe is founder and President of Youth Mentoring Connection, an organization specializing in creating opportunities for kids to be mentored by business people, both at the work site and school site.  As of January 2010, programs created or facilitated by Tony have been responsible for thousands of youth receiving quality mentoring experiences.    He has also been a featured speaker and seminar leader at each of the California Mentor Summits, and at many symposiums throughout the state.  In addition, Tony is the author of the nationally recognized "2 Minute Mentor Tips", an e-mail campaign which gives over 2000 mentors on-going (twice monthly) mentoring assistance/training. 

With a Masters Degree in Psychology, in addition to his work in mentoring, Tony has written Life Skills and Business Skills curriculum for youth and has facilitated at the Universal Youth Entrepreneur Academy and the Center for Entrepreneurism at Manual Arts High School.
