name: California 211 Providers Network
mission: California 211 Providers Network (211 California) is a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization that serves as a gateway for transforming how all Californians equitably connect to health, human, and disaster services in order to build healthy, resilient communities.
ntee_code: M99 - Other Public Safety, Disaster Preparedness, and Relief N.E.C.

programs.name: Information & Referrals
programs.description: 211 is a vital service leveraged by millions of people across North America. Every day, clients contact 211 to access free and confidential crisis and emergency counseling, disaster assistance, food, health care and insurance assistance, stable housing and utilities payment assistance, employment services, veteran services and childcare and family services.

leader.name: Alana Hitchcock
leader.profile:
Alana Hitchcock, appointed Executive Director and CEO of 211 California in January 2023, is a skilled cross-sector leader with expertise in 211 systems and statewide policy. During her career at 211 LA, Alana launched programs, expanded online services to assist over 1 million people in 2022, and developed public data tools.

Alana’s experience includes running a UN Women-recognized social enterprise in Thailand, sustainable planning work with Caltrans, and serving as a Capital Fellow. A USC graduate in Public Administration, she applies her expertise to address California's complex social challenges.

name: San Diego County Animal Support Foundation, Inc.
mission:
The San Diego Animal Support Foundation assists more than 35 underfunded local shelters and rescue agencies. Unlike any other organization, the foundation promotes the adoption of animals from ALL the rescues and shelters who need us...many of whom cannot afford the luxury of a publicity department or PR person. This is done at NO EXPENSE to the local organizations.  We use daily television segments, weekly radio spots, and our relationship with the media to promote adoption, events, proper pet care, and seasonal issues.  The SDASF organizes four massive annual adoption events: BIG DOGS ROCK,  Cupids & Canines, Santa Paws, & Dog Days of Summer, which bring the local agencies together for adoption events featuring 150-200+ adoptable dogs and dozens of legitimate agencies in one place! Due to the lack of available spay/neuter services, the foundation also has a FREE spay/neuter program for individuals who can't afford to have their pets altered. We also provide a platform for owners to raise money for medical care without having fees taken out of the balance. 
In the Wildfires of October 2007, the Foundation brought thousands and thousands of people together from across the nation to help save animals and livestock affected by the fires. For 5 days, a 24-hour line was maintained bringing together fire victims in need, transportation volunteers, & people who were willing to provide boarding.  In 2009, the Foundation answered the cry of deployed San Diego based Marines to bring back multiple dogs from Afghanistan that would have been killed if left behind.  A separate fund for this mission was maintained, and 100% of the donations were spent on bringing the dogs home.
We embrace and support well thought out ideas for programs that ultimately increase adoptions from legitimate organizations, prevent unwanted litters from being born, and bring the Southern California community one step closer to zero euthanasia.
ntee_code: D20 - Animal Protection and Welfare (includes Humane Societies and SPCAs)

programs.name: Pet Adoption Program
programs.description: 1)  Pet Adoption Program:  Promotes the adoption of animals from more than 30 legitimate local shelters and rescue organizations.  At zero cost to the local shelters and rescues, we take adoptable pets on television.  During these segments, we are able to promote adoption, and educate the public about general animal welfare while promoting the non-profits and adoption events.

programs.name: Spay/Neuter Program (no cost)
programs.description:
2)  Spay/Neuter Program:  We fund a free spay/neuter program with the partnership of local vets who provide these services to us at an extremely low cost.  Our target audience is otherwise responsible pet owners who have put off spaying or neutering their pets due to cost, or people who simply will not spay/neuter unless they get it for free.  
We have recently acquired the help of an experienced volunteer to expand the numbers of vets with whom we work, and expand this resource to more locations within the County.

programs.name: Mega Community Adoption Events
programs.description: The SDASF organizes four one-day mega adoption events featuring between 250 - 300 adoptable dogs & cats from approximately 25-30 legitimate local rescues and shelters.  This involves negotiating location, bringing together all the organizations, mapping, gathering 50+ extra volunteers, and massive publicity!  The very successful events bring adoptable pets to adopters in one convenient place, but also brings out new volunteers and foster homes to benefit the participating non-profits.  It is a completely altruistic endeavor, and therefore we do not accept fees from participating rescues/shelters, nor do we charge admission from the public. To date, these events have been put together on a zero budget, but future success will depend on funds for promotion and advertising reaching out to the community.  A budget of $5,000 would allow us to take out one giant, highly visible ad in the newspaper for each event and help to cover the cost of required permits and liability insurance.

programs.name: Emergency Veterinary Medical Fund
programs.description: 3)  Emergency Medical Fund:  We work with owners to help raise donations to pay for necessary medical care. The families who ask for our services are required to help us raise donations to specifically cover these expenses, as well as pick up a portion of the initial fees, as a show of good faith.  Any unspecified money donated to the medical fund is used to contribute toward medical care for those who may not have the time to raise money for their pet.

name: Prism Reports, Inc
mission: Through in-depth and thought-provoking journalism, Prism reflects the lived experiences of people most impacted by injustice. As an independent and nonprofit newsroom led by journalists of color, we tell stories from the ground up: to disrupt harmful narratives, and to inform movements for justice.
ntee_code: R20 - Civil Rights, Advocacy for Specific Groups

programs.name: Intersectional and nuanced journalism
programs.description: At Prism, we produce journalism that examines the intersections of multiple social injustices, our readers’ lived experiences and identities, and movements to reshape our society for the better. Our readers turn to Prism to see and hear their communities because, like the issues that affect us, we are not just one-sided. We uncover new perspectives, pathways, and frames that make people think about issues and solutions in new ways. Our coverage is grassroots and grounded in reporters’ own local communities, where they’ve built deep roots, networks, and trust with sources. Reporting from their home bases, our staff and contributors bring to their work a nuanced understanding both of local and regional issues, and of how they fit into a national context.

programs.name: Reflective Journalism Project (RJP)
programs.description: The Reflective Journalism Project (RJP) by Prism trains aspiring writers, community leaders, and frontline social justice thinkers and organizers on the editorial process from soup to nuts. Our goal is to build a deep bench of content creators and grow the network of BIPOC writers telling their stories, sharing their experiences, and reporting on issues mainstream media often overlooks. RJP aims to ensure the white-dominated news media industry no longer uses the excuse “there are no writers of color” to perpetuate homogeneous coverage of what’s happening in our democracy.

programs.name: Right to Write (R2W)
programs.description: Right to Write (R2W) is rooted in the legacy of BIPOC revolutionaries, writers, and reporters whose work from prison drew greater attention to what was happening behind bars and across the nation. As a journalism nonprofit dedicated to collective liberation and justice, it is important for Prism to keep piercing through the walls of oppression and uplifting the voices, narratives, and experiences of incarcerated people. Acting as a partner-publisher and destination for incarcerated reporters, writers, and the organizations and initiatives with whom they work, Prism’s R2W ensures that their voices are a consistent part of our editorial goals and coverage.

programs.name: Events
programs.description: Prism’s virtual events connect our community of readers to movement leaders, organizers, advocates, and experts working at the frontlines of a more just society. By putting our readers in conversation with each other, and the people behind Prism’s stories, we foster deeper connections and reach a wider audience by providing a new medium for engagement.

name: Animal Samaritans
mission: Animal Samaritans is dedicated to improving the lives of animals and people.
ntee_code: D20 - Animal Protection and Welfare (includes Humane Societies and SPCAs)

programs.name: Spay and Neuter Program
programs.description: The overarching goal of Animal Samaritans' spay and neuter program is to make low and no-cost spay and neuter services of companion animals available to a wide range of in need pet owners. By creating community centered efforts, Animal Samaritans facilitates spay/neuter services throughout the Coachella Valley and end the complications associated with pet overpopulation. Also included under this umbrella is a feral cat program wherein concerned citizens trap feral cats. They are then brought to Animal Samaritans for their sterilization procedure and they are returned to their feral colony 12 hours later. Trap, Neuter Release (TNR) programs like ours are considered in animal welfare circles to be the gold standard for managing feral cat colonies.

programs.name: No Kill Shelter and Adoption Center
programs.description: Animal Samaritans maintains a licensed animal shelter that houses adoptable animals until a responsible home can be found. Animal Samaritans houses cats and dogs . On average, each year about 250 homeless animals are adopted from our shelter. All cats and dogs are spayed or neutered before they are adopted. Additionally, they are provided necessary medical attention, testing, evaluation and vaccinations. This service provides a humane safety net for our community's animals.

programs.name: Humane Education
programs.description: In a world that seems at times increasingly hostile, Animal Samaritans understands that kindness to living things is often taught. Our Humane Education program is based on a philosophy dedicated to the principle of creating kinder communities through kindness to animals. Every year we educate more than 12,000 children in schools. We also provide summer camps for other children who might not otherwise have opportunities to bond with animals. Our unique programs effective curricula are helping to create a new generation of citizens who understand both how and why to treat other living beings with respect.

programs.name: Affordable veterinary services
programs.description: At Animal Samaritans, we know there is nothing scarier than when one of our furry family members is sick, especially if you don't have enough money to pay for their care. In addition to our already lower-priced primary veterinary options, Animal Samaritans offers financial aid options to help those in need.

programs.name: Adoption Alliance Animal Rescue Program
programs.description: The Adoption Alliance, in conjunction with the Riverside County Shelter and over 200 fosters and rescues throughout North America, save adoptable at risk animals at risk of euthanasia. Since the start of this program in 2011, we have saved the lives of over 16,000 at-risk adoptable animals!

name: Nature for All
mission:
Our mission is to build a diverse base of support to ensure that everyone in the Los Angeles area has equitable access to the wide range of benefits which nature provides. We’re committed to building support to protect, create access to our forests, rivers, and parks, and developing a new diverse generation of environmental leaders and stewards who connect to and care for our public lands.

Nature For All advocates for policies and programs that will:

-- Protect the mountains and rivers in our area, to conserve resources and be more climate-resilient.
-- Create more natural spaces such as parks and bike paths in our historically underserved neighborhoods.
-- Connect people and public lands through more trails and other outdoor recreational opportunities, to improve public health.
ntee_code: C30 - Natural Resource Conservation and Protection

programs.name: Protecting Our Public Lands
programs.description:
Nature for All is working to protect and expand the San Gabriel National Monument and other public lands around Los Angeles, so we may safeguard our natural resources and provide access to nature for our diverse, urban population.
--Advocating for a successful House vote of the San Gabriel Mountains Foothills Rivers Protection Act (Act), reintroduced by Representative Chu in February 2021 (Update: Success in the House!)
Introduction of a bill/bill package by Senator Padilla, followed by successful hearings and vote in 2021
--Continuing efforts to implement the SGM National Monument Management Plan with an emphasis on access and visitor services
Providing input to the anticipated Visitor Services Plan to be initiated by the Forest Service
--Continuing engagement with community/stakeholders at large on protections and improvements to the SGM

name: CALIFORNIA STATE PARKS FOUNDATION
mission: California State Parks Foundation is an independent, member-supported nonprofit dedicated to protecting and preserving the California state park system, for the benefit of all.
ntee_code: C30 - Natural Resource Conservation and Protection

programs.name: Access and Experiences
programs.description: While California state parks are public spaces, many people cannot experience them. Barriers to park access include lack of transportation, cost of visiting, lack of awareness of parks or activities, and more. Though we are working to reduce these barriers, this is just the beginning of the effort to ensure that every Californian feels welcome and included in state parks. A sense of belonging is fostered by positive park experiences: welcoming signage and staffing, relevant programming, and amenities that are inclusive and well-maintained. We work to address these issues in localized areas with communities that face greater systemic barriers, such as Candlestick Point State Recreation Area and Los Angeles State Historic Park. This allows us to identify scalable solutions, educate and activate Californians and the Legislature, and ultimately influence policy and legislation to create state level programs such as the California State Library Parks Pass and California State Parks Week.

programs.name: Climate Resilience
programs.description: California’s 280 state parks are increasingly threatened by climate change, and building climate resilience is essential. Climate resilience is the ability to prepare for, adapt to, and recover from the effects of climate change, which have already drastically altered California landscapes. California state parks face numerous climate threats — from devastating wildfires to increased flooding. To address these challenges, California State Parks Foundation has created climate resilience initiatives to prepare parks for more frequent and severe wildfires, accelerating sea level rise, biodiversity loss, extreme weather events, and more. We are using the best available research to learn about climate threats and potential solutions, educate Californians and the Legislature, inspire people to take action, and ultimately influence policy and legislation that prioritizes marginalized communities most impacted by climate change.

programs.name: Volunteerism
programs.description: California State Parks Foundations year-round volunteer park stewardship program organizes workdays to protect and preserve state parks across California by addressing climate change and demands on natural resources. In partnership with the Department of Parks and Recreation, California State Parks Foundation generates high-quality workday service projects to attend to unmet needs and engage Californians with their local parks, including signature Earth Day Climate Action events in April. Our volunteers provide consistent, sustainable support for park staff and help with critical projects such as planting native plants, removing invasive species, trail repair, trash clean-up, post-wildfire restoration, and clearing brush to reduce wildfire risk.

programs.name: Park Excellence
programs.description: Effective staffing, funding, and protection policies are critical to ensuring a thriving state park system. With sufficient staffing, parks can offer high-quality visitor services and maintain facilities and trails to a high standard. Proper funding is equally vital to ensure that parks have the resources they need. Parks are also vulnerable to a variety of threats, including development pressures from adjacent lands, roads, powerlines, and other non-mission use. To address these challenges, it is crucial to have strong policies and regulations in place, such as those that restrict commercial activities within park boundaries, prohibit encroachment, and protect sensitive habitats. In addition to promoting key policy solutions, California State Parks Foundation ensures park excellence by supporting California state parks in creating thriving partnership programs so that they can benefit from all the work of nonprofit partners.

leader.name: Rachel Norton
leader.profile: Rachel Norton joined California State Parks Foundation as Executive Director in May 2017. Born and raised in Northern California, Rachel grew up camping and hiking in California's beautiful national and state parks with her family. She began her career as a journalist, working for Reuters and The New York Times before returning to California to start a family. A former elected school board member, Rachel is passionate about getting kids into nature. She has two daughters and lives in San Francisco.

name: San Dieguito River Valley Land Conservancy
mission:
The San Dieguito River Valley Conservancy preserves, protects, and shares the natural and cultural resources of the San Dieguito River Valley through collaborative efforts to acquire lands, complete trails, restore habitats, establish educational programs, create interpretive centers, encourage recreation, and mobilize public support.

We partner with other organizations to complete the planned 70-mile Coast to Crest Trail from Del Mar to Julian in San Diego County.  48 miles of the Coast to Crest Trail are open to the public today!
ntee_code: C30 - Natural Resource Conservation and Protection

programs.name: Land Acquisition
programs.description:
Assist with the acquisition of land within the 94,000-acre coast to crest San Dieguito River Park planning area. More information is available at http://sdrvc.org/support/directed-giving/land-acquisition/.

In early 2021, SDRVC purchased 117 acres  in the Del Dios area of the San Dieguito River watershed previously slated for development to preserve as open space in perpetuity.   Funding includes $276K from the Conservancy, over $2M from the US Fish & Wildlife Service and almost $554K from the California Wildlife Conservation Board.

programs.name: Coast to Crest Trail
programs.description:
Assist the San Dieguito River Park to accelerate the completion of the 70-mile Coast-to-Crest Trail, which spans from the beach in Del Mar to the crest of Volcan Mountain in Julian.

During 2021, SDRVC provided $144,100 as the required match for a State of California Propsition 68 grant to the San Dieguito River Park JPA to build a one-mile segment of the Coast to Crest Trail in Osuna Valley.

programs.name: Conservation
programs.description: Assist with programs that rehabilitate, maintain and protect the natural resources (habitats, land, rivers, streams, historical etc.) within the San Dieguito River Valley by controlling invasive species and restoring native vegetation. The Conservancy engages over 400 volunteers annually in stewardship projects.  Information about current stewardship projects is available at http://sdrvc.org/current/invasives-management.

programs.name: Environmental Education
programs.description:
Support outdoor education programs for both youth and adults within the diverse San Dieguito River Valley landscape. Programs include: in-the-field seminars on the biology, geology, hydrology and cultural history of the San Dieguito River Valley; expert-led hikes; and lectures.   More information is available at: http://sdrvc.org/current/esp/ and http://sdrvc.org/support/directed-giving/environmental-education/.     Conservancy staff also particpate in school-based environmental programs and student projects.

We are busy translating our field visits to virtual educational events.  Already we have received funding from SDGE and Genentech for our new Through the Lens educational program which includes photos of wildlife from our motion activated cameras placed strategically in our preserves.

programs.name: Operations
programs.description: The San Dieguito River Valley Conservancy protects and restores the San Dieguito River Valley and assists in the implemention of the 94,000-acre planned San Dieguito River Park. In addition the Conservancy educates the public about the natural, recreational and historical resources the River Park provides. Our donors are the heart of  the San Dieguito River Valley Conservancy.  Donor support makes up 70% of our basic operations with each dollar donated to the Conservancy being leveraged 15 times through public, private and corporate grants.

programs.name: Citizen Science Monitoring Program
programs.description:
Citizen science takes advantage of the fact that visitors to the River Park are constantly observing their surroundings as they hike, bike or ride their horse on our trails. This program offers residents, volunteers, trail users and other outdoor enthusiasts a way to actively contribute to the betterment of their local outdoor spaces; they can be a field scientist for a day. It also offers students, when combined with school and university programs, a great way to get hands-on learning opportunities.

in 2021 we will gather our Citizen Scientists to conduct baseline biological surveys on our newly acquired 117-acre Del Dios Preserve.

programs.name: River Path Del Mar
programs.description:
The River Path Del Mar provides a scenic overlook of the San Dieguito Lagoon and River, complete with interpretive signage of the flora and fauna of the River and Lagoon. The existing trail goes from Jimmy Durante Blvd westwards to the coast and parallels the south edge of the River, providing beautiful water views and information regarding this important wetland and natural resource. Parking is currently provided for trail access at a lot immediately east of the City's Public Works yard.  In May 2016, the River Path was extended from Jimmy Durante Boulevard to the Old Grande Avenue Overlook.  

The City of Del Mar and Conservancy are working to complete Phase 3 of the River Path extension from the Overlook to the Crest Canyon Preserve trailhead, estimated to be completed in 2024.

programs.name: Watershed Explorers Program
programs.description: The purpose of the Watershed Explorers Program is to provide an opportunity for students to get outdoors and learn what a watershed is and why its health is important for preserving wildlife and plants, supplying water and keeping water clean. As they experience the outdoors, traveling from Volcan Mountain 55 miles west to the San Dieguito Lagoon, students develop a "sense of place" and appreciation for the environment - recognizing they play a role in keeping the natural community a thriving ecosystem.

leader.name: Ms. Trish Boaz
leader.profile: Hired in 2013, Trish brings over 25 years of experience in conservation and environmental protection, as well as established positive relationships with many of the Conservancy’s partners. She has previously worked for the County of San Diego Department of Parks and Recreation, where she oversaw the implementation of the Multiple Species Conservation Program and managed the award-winning County Trails Program. She coordinated the County’s acquisition of over 7,100 acres of open space lands. Trish also volunteers as a crisis interventionist with the City of San Diego Police Department.

name: Laguna Canyon Foundation
mission: Laguna Canyon Foundation is dedicated to the conservation and ongoing protection of the South Coast Wilderness. We envision a thriving coastal ecosystem that serves as a source ​of inspiration, connection, and refuge for all.
ntee_code: C30 - Natural Resource Conservation and Protection

programs.name: Habitat Restoration Program
programs.description: Laguna Canyon Foundation is dedicated to restoring and preserving healthy, functional native ecosystems and wildlife habitats that encourage biodiversity. We restore habitats by removing invasive species and planting and tending native vegetation in and around the South Coast Wilderness. We also oversee local resource management projects to ensure that impacts to sensitive habitat are minimized. Restoration also improves viewsheds and recreation opportunities, building a connection between residents and the local environment.

programs.name: Education Program
programs.description: The South Coast Wilderness Education Program brings over 4,500 students per year from urban Title 1 schools into Orange County's Laguna Coast and Aliso and Wood Canyons Wilderness Parks. Our Next Generation Science Standards-based field trips foster a sense of environmental stewardship, connect the children to the land, and inspire the next generation of conservationists. To make the program affordable for all students, we cover the complete cost of the program, including busing costs, lesson materials, field instructors, snacks and supplies. We partner with twelve schools, bringing the children into the parks each year from second to fifth grade. Our General Education Program provides Next Generation Science Standards-based field trips to Laguna Beach schools. Private schools, scout troops, and home school groups are also welcome, though we charge a nominal fee to cover our costs. Topics can vary depending on teacher interest, and are often tailored to the specific class.

programs.name: Volunteer and Outreach Program
programs.description: Laguna Canyon Foundation reaches out to all users and potential users of the wilderness. As the bridge between the open space and the surrounding communities, we are the leading organization for education, public outreach, habitat restoration, and trail work in the canyons. Our goal is to develop conservationists who love the land, who will protect it, and who will recreate responsibly. Our objective is to engage visitors in public programs that speak to their interests through unique hiking, riding, and stewardship opportunities. As participants enjoy their time on the trails during our hosted events, they often express interest in becoming long-term volunteers to preserve this land, and thus, our community of conservationists grows. We offer diverse opportunities to give back to the community – everything from hands-on habitat restoration to leading interpretive hikes to to assisting visitors at the Nix Nature Center.

programs.name: Trail Program
programs.description: The trail systems in these parks are a tremendous resource to the communities surrounding them, allowing people to get out and enjoy nature in a variety of ways. Trail usage in Laguna Coast and Aliso & Wood Canyons Wilderness Parks has increased exponentially in the past few years, threatening the viability of important habitat. Laguna Canyon Foundation and Orange County Parks staff work together to minimize human impacts, protect habitat, and foster community investment in the trails and harmony between different trail user groups (i.e. hikers, mountain bikers, and equestrian users). LCF staff and volunteers work with OC Parks staff to maintain and improve the trails. We take a holistic view of our authorized trail system and prioritize the most urgent trail projects. We look at surrounding habitat and impacts to wildlife, make the trails more sustainable by keeping people on the trail and getting water off the trail, and design trails so they're fun and safe for everyone.

programs.name: Fuel Modification Program
programs.description: In partnership with the Laguna Beach Fire Department, we are managing the vegetation in the canyons and slopes adjacent to neighborhoods and businesses to reduce fire behavior potential in these regions. Our fuel modification work showcases an environmentally sustainable way to achieve fire safety objectives. More traditional fuel modification methods, such as creating wide-open fuel breaks or clearing an area using goats, impact native plants, cause erosion, and spread invasive plant species. In our methodology, specially-trained and closely-supervised hand crews remove ladder fuels and non-native, dead, or dying vegetation, and thin remaining vegetation where necessary in order to reduce potential fire behavior. This allows us to maintain native vegetative cover, protect rare plant species, and reduce the potential for erosion or weed problems. These methods protect wildlife habitat and aesthetic values to the greatest extent possible, while providing an additional measure of safety to at-risk neighborhoods and to firefighters in case of wildfire. Laguna Canyon Foundation coordinates pre-project planning and neighbor outreach, educates contractor crews, directs contractor work in the field, conducts photo monitoring and sensitive species protection measures, and ensures that the work is completed to the necessary standards. We also oversee ongoing maintenance work once initial treatment is complete.

leader.name: Scott Thomas
leader.profile: As Executive Director, Scott oversees conservation, education and outreach, fundraising, and administration for Laguna Canyon Foundation. Scott has been involved in land conservation and protection in Orange County for over 35 years. Prior to coming to LCF, Scott was the chief landscape architect at OC Parks, responsible for master planning and park improvement projects across the 60,000 acre regional park system. He was one of the first certified volunteer naturalists for Laguna Coast Wilderness Park, and later ran the volunteer stewardship program prior to LCF taking on that role in 2007.  In his free time Scott enjoys spending time with his family,  gardening, surfing, camping and traveling. He also enjoys long-distance backpacking, hiking from Mexico to Canada on the Pacific Crest Trail, as well as the Vermont Long Trail.

mission: Promoting and establishing animal welfare in the country of Romania, through providing free or subsidized veterinary services for homeless dogs and cats and the animals of the poor, including spay/neuter and treatments, veterinary training, education, and shelter food.

leader.name: Nancy Janes
leader.profile:
Founded Romania Animal Rescue  following a hiking tour of Romania from the USA in 2003.  In 2015 we launched Homeless Animals Hospital Program. In 2016 we started building the Center of Hope Hospital that opened its doors in 2017.  Center of Hope provides free and subsidized veterinary treatment for strays and animals of extremely impoverished  owners and rescuers via our Homeless Animals Hospital Program.  
As of end of 2024, Romania Animal Rescue has spayed and neutered 135,000 dogs and cats.   Through surgeries at Center of Hope, Family Vet, and mobile campaigns.  
Center of Hope hospital trains  vets from around the world on minimally invasive surgical techniques, with scholarships for Romanian vets provided by Romania Animal Rescue.  We also work out of Family Vet hospital in Craiova.  RAR provides food for a shelter of over 300 dogs and cats.  Center of Hope and Family Vet run field trips for local schools.

co_leader.name: Aurelian Stefan

name: Pinnacles National Park Foundation
mission:
Ensuring excellence in education, resource stewardship, and visitor experiences at Pinnacles National Park.

The Pinnacles National Park Foundation is the official nonprofit partner of Pinnacles National Park.
ntee_code: T12 - Fund Raising and/or Fund Distribution

programs.name: Pinnacles Condor Fund
programs.description: Supports the California Condor Recovery Program at Pinnacles National Park with volunteer support and funding, including cost sharing GPS tag download fees for the Pinnacles flock of California condors.

programs.name: Camp Pinnacles
programs.description: Camp Pinnacles is an overnight Science Camp that serves 4th and 5th grade students from the surrounding area. Hands on resource immersion activities are planned out for students to have fun while learning about the natural and cultural history of the region. Curriculum based activities get the students engaged in active learning and problem solving.  Camp Pinnacles is made possible through collaboration between PINN Education and PNPF.  Camp Pinnacles strives to put students on a pathway to becoming good stewards of the land we all share.

programs.name: San Benito Working Landscapes Group
programs.description: The San Benito Working Landscapes Group is a group of agencies, non-governmental organizations, ranchers, and farmers partnering to find common ground for protecting and enhancing the open, working landscapes of San Benito County and adjacent lands.  The Working Landscapes Group was conceived in 2010 as an effort to encourage dialogue and increase mutual understanding among agencies, organizations, and the local ranching community, to support the long-term viability of San Benito County rangelands, while upholding habitat connectivity and making habitat improvements.

programs.name: Trails Forever
programs.description: The Trails Forever Program provides for rehabilitation, restoration, and improvements to trails and climber access routes at Pinnacles National Park.

name: Sentient
mission: Sentient is a nonprofit news organization that publishes stories and solutions to explain factory farms and their effect on climate, animals, public health, politics and more. Founded in 2018, Sentient's content is fact-checked and science-driven, with reporting that serves readers who are interested in the impacts of what they eat on animals, climate, water, conditions for workers and so much more. Our content is available free of charge, without a paywall or advertisers. Our donors and board have no editorial influence on content.
ntee_code: D05 - Research Institutes and/or Public Policy Analysis

programs.name: Food & Farming Journalism Network
programs.description: The Food and Farming Journalism Network (FFJN) is an online community of journalists covering the industrial food system and its impacts on climate, health, economics, workers and animal welfare. It’s a members-only space for journalists (and editors) at all stages of their careers, working as freelancers or staff writers. Members have access to a moderated Slack channel, a twice-monthly email alert with the latest reporting, fellowship and other career and learning opportunities, access to monthly Zoom gatherings for networking and learning, early registration for FFJN’s webinar series, Food System Forensics, and other resources.

name: Environmental Health Coalition
mission: Environmental Health Coalition is dedicated to environmental and social justice. We believe that justice is achieved when empowered communities act together to make social change. We organize and advocate to protect public health and the environment threatened by toxic pollution. EHC supports efforts that create a just society and foster a healthy and sustainable quality of life.

programs.name: Toxic-Free Neighborhoods Campaign
programs.description: Toxic Free Neighborhoods Campaign organizes in communities of color to advocate for the prevention of toxic pollution from industrial and mobile sources. Our efforts are focused in the communities of Logan in San Diego and Westside National City. These communities both suffer from years of inadequate zoning that has created an unhealthful mix of toxic industries, homes, and schools. Both communities receive additional pollution from port-related activities at nearby terminals. EHC and community leaders are actively involved in developing new visions for their neighborhoods through participation in the Barrio Logan Community Plan and Old Town National City Specific Plan stakeholder groups and the Clean Ports Plan. EHC works with an alliance of five other environmental justice organization to promote policy changes at the statewide level.

programs.name: Healthy Homes Campaign
programs.description: Through partnerships with the San Diego Housing Commission and the City of National City, EHC) has made over 1,000 homes safer by eliminating lead, mold, and other health and safety hazards. EHC’s organizing and advocacy efforts led to ordinances in both San Diego and National City requiring the inspection and remediation of lead hazards in rental properties. To further improve environmental health conditions in homes, EHC now integrates innovative solutions to protect residents from indoor air pollution through the Portside Air Improvement and Relief (PAIR) program. PAIR distributes air purifiers and monitors to families in portside communities, empowering them with tools to improve their indoor air quality. Additionally, EHC connects residents to partner organizations offering electric appliance upgrades, replacing polluting gas appliances with cleaner, more efficient alternatives.

programs.name: Border Environmental Justice Campaign
programs.description: Border Environmental Justice Campaign works to reduce toxic pollution caused by Maquiladora industries in Tijuana and promote fair trade. In January 2009 EHC and residents of Colonia Chilpancingo celebrated the completion of the long-awaited cleanup of the Metales y Derivados battery recycling plant. After more than ten years, EHC and our Tijuana affiliate, the Colectivo Chilpancingo Pro Justicia Ambiental, negotiated an unprecedented binational agreement to address the problem. The Colectivo’s youth group created a comic book that tells the story of Metales y Derivados from their family’s perspective. After the completion of this toxic cleanup, the Colectivo turned its attention to diesel pollution from trucks and buses use Chilpancingo’s residential streets as a short cut to the maquiladoras, passing in front of the local elementary school and kindergarten.

programs.name: Voter Empowerment
programs.description: Our nonpartisan civic engagement work is central to movement-building and is integrated into all our organizing efforts. We work closely with our local target communities and the regional coalitions Engage San Diego and Leadership Development Project (LDP) to strengthen the culture of voting in underrepresented communities and to build a leadership pipeline to advance leaders to positions of influence.

programs.name: Climate and Transportation Justice
programs.description: Through our Climate and Transportation Justice program, we lead local and statewide environmental justice efforts to address climate change, air pollution and build sustainable communities with improved public transit, renewable energy, and access to well-paid, green sector jobs.

programs.name: Clean Ports Campaign
programs.description: The Port of San Diego plays a significant role in creating the pollution burden for National City and Logan. Residents in these communities are plagued with the air pollution that comes with living near an industrial and goods movement port. EHC created the Clean Ports campaign over 30 years ago to advocate and organize for pollution reduction in the freight, shipyards and military industrial activities on the waterfront. Through this ongoing campaign, the EHC staff and community leaders monitor Port activities and advocate for local, regional and state policies to improve and protect the health of fenceline community residents.

leader.name: Mr. Jose Franco Garcia
leader.profile: José Franco García, Executive Director, joined EHC in 2010. Previously, he directed the Community Building program at the Coalition of Neighborhood Councils in San Diego and worked with the United Domestic Workers of America and SEIU 2028. At EHC, García launched a Community Action Team in City Heights and in 2011 organized residents and members of allied organizations to participate in the Built Environment Team, a collaborative of social and environmental justice organizations in City Heights that created the first Community Development Action Plan for the neighborhood. García has a B.A. in political science and public law from the University of California San Diego. In 2011 he was a member of the Latino Redistricting Committee and joined the New Leaders Council as a board member. García leads EHC’s Organizers Team and our voter engagement efforts.

name: Mission Trails Regional Park Foundation Inc
mission: In partnership with the City of San Diego, preserve and protect the natural environment of Mission Trails Regional Park and provide and promote educational and recreational opportunities.
ntee_code: B90 - Educational Services and Schools - Other

programs.name: Youth Environmental Education
programs.description: Pre-K children and students in grades K-12, living primarily in socioeconomically challenged areas of San Diego County, visit Mission Trails Regional Park (MTRP) as an enhancement to their classroom experience. The MTRP Foundation provides free educational opportunities to more than 3,000 youth each year, from offering the pre-K Trail Tykes program eight times monthly, to the twice a week free field trips for elementary youth to Eco Ambassadors, a free program for teens interested in working in environmental fields. Through the programs, youth learn about the park’s Kumeyaay history, native plants and wildlife found at the park, natural history and geology. Programs are presented by our trained outdoor educators for children throughout San Diego County, at the park and in the classroom. A unique aspect of our program is that we fund the cost of field trip bus transportation to ensure the MTRP experiences is available to all children in the community, especially at Title I schools.

leader.name: Jennifer Morrissey
leader.profile: Jennifer Morrissey joined the Mission Trails Regional Park (MTRP) Foundation as Executive Director in March 2018, bringing more than 20 years experience at San Diego County nonprofit organizations. Her background in public relations, marketing, and fundraising contributed greatly to the growth and impact of her past employers including the Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, Timken Museum of Art, and Voices for Children. During her tenures in marketing at the University of San Diego and her alma mater, UC San Diego, Jennifer conceived and executed marketing campaigns that brought significant attention and funding to the institutions. At Mission Trails Regional Park, Ms. Morrissey leverages her expertise and leadership ability to further the MTRP Foundation and increase engagement with the park by San Diego County residents and visitors.

name: THE GREENLINING INSTITUTE
mission: The Greenlining Institute works toward a future where communities of color can build wealth, live in healthy places filled with economic opportunity, and are ready to meet the challenges posed by climate change.
ntee_code: R05 - Research Institutes and/or Public Policy Analysis

programs.name: Leadership Academy
programs.description: The Greenlining Academy works to empower and develop the next generation of multi-ethnic leaders to advance racial and economic equity and create positive social change. The Academy offers advocacy training and hands on public policy experience to students and young people seeking to acquire these skills and build vital social networks that will enhance their ability to be effective advocates. Through its programs, the Academy has trained, supported and empowered over 1000 young leaders.

leader.name: Olga Talamante
leader.profile: Olga Talamante was appointed to serve as The Greenlining Institute’s Interim President and CEO in 2025. She is also Executive Director Emerita of the Chicana Latina Foundation (CLF). She became the first Executive Director of CLF in January 2003 serving in that position until March of 2018. CLF’s mission is the Empowerment of Chicanas/Latinas through their Personal, Educational, and Professional Advancement. In her position she oversaw the granting of thousands of dollars to Latina college students and founded the organization’s pioneering Leadership Institute that has graduated over 700 Latina social justice leaders. Prior to those fifteen years with CLF, she also held various positions, including Regional Vice President, from 1986-2002 at INROADS, a national career and leadership organization for students of color. She is widely respected for her community activism and leadership. During the mid-seventies, she became well known for her experience as a political prisoner in Argentina.

name: Burundi Friends International
mission: BFI unites and educates youth, women, and men, creates economic empowerment, and builds self-sustaining communities in Burundi, East Africa.

programs.name: Women Empowered Project: Gitega Expansion II
programs.description: The Women Empowered (WE) project is in thanks to a partnership with Project Concern International (PCI), A Global Communities Partner. The WE project provides a way for rural Burundian women to overcome roadblocks to economic growth. Project facilitators assemble beneficiaries in small saving and loan groups, provide financial literacy training, and enhance women’s decision-making skills to solve community issues. The project will include business entrepreneurship tools that show women how to create income-generating activities, enabling them to effectively reach economic resilience and integrate into the business sector. To accelerate economic resilience and enable women to get fully involved in their business, the project will also incorporate a positive masculinity approach to empower men in the beneficiary communities to get involved in household and reproductive tasks in order for women to gain more time to follow up businesses.

leader.name: Julie Marner
leader.profile: Julie studied Music Education at St. Ambrose University in Iowa, has a B.A. in Psychology from the University of Colorado and a M.A. in Practical Theology from the University of San Diego. As BFI’s Executive Director, Julie focuses on partner development, fundraising, and oversight of projects in Burundi, East Africa. Her love for Burundi began with her first visit to the country in 2010, then a subsequent trip in 2011 to teach English Communication at Light University. Since that time, Julie's  trips to Burundi have expanded beyond efforts in education to the fields of economic empowerment and the performing arts.

co_leader.name: Odette Habonimana
co_leader.profile:
Odette earned her B.A. in English Language and Literature from the University of Burundi in 2013 and a M.A. in Organizational Leadership from the International Leadership University in Burundi. Her work experience includes serving as Project Coordinator for the U.S. Embassy’s American Corner in Gitega, Burundi, and as Gender Program Associate for the U.N. Development Program in Burundi. Odette has worked closely with BFI since 2015. 
In 2020, Odette was named BFI Country Director and was selected as one of the ten finalists for the US Institute of Peace’s (USIP) inaugural Women Building Peace Award.

name: San Bruno Mountain Watch
mission: The mission of San Bruno Mountain Watch is to care for San Bruno Mountain through conservation, ecological restoration, education, and advocacy in partnership with local communities.
ntee_code: C30 - Natural Resource Conservation and Protection

programs.name: Ecological Restoration
programs.description: San Bruno Mountain Watch organizes community-based ecological restoration programs for the benefit of rare and endangered species in a variety of habitats on San Bruno Mountain. We collaborate with agencies including local cities, San Mateo County Parks, California State Parks, and the California Department of Fish and Wildlife.

programs.name: Public Hikes
programs.description: San Bruno Mountain Watch provides free interpretive hikes to the public every month highlighting the cultural and natural history of San Bruno Mountain and the changing environmental conditions of the mountain throughout the seasons.

programs.name: Environmental Education
programs.description: San Bruno Mountain Watch develops curriculum and activities for San Bruno Mountain aligned with Next Generation Science Standards for each K-12 grade level. We provide field trips and service-learning activities for schools, including local community colleges and universities.

programs.name: Mission Blue Nursery
programs.description:
Mission Blue Nursery grows plants entirely from seeds and cuttings collected on San Bruno Mountain and provides these for ecosystem restoration projects on the mountain.

The nursery also supplies plants for landscaping projects in local cities including school gardens, backyards, and sustainable streetscapes.

Mission Blue Nursery helps raise awareness about the San Bruno Mountain and its extraordinary and unique flora, promotes drought tolerant and locally adapted landscaping, and contributes extensively to the restoration of habitat for the mountain's endangered species. Plants are grown with the help of community volunteers, engaged in weekly programs.

leader.name: Ariel Cherbowsky Corkidi
leader.profile: As the executive director for San Bruno Mountain Watch, Ariel oversees the planning, funding, and operation of our restoration, education, and nursery programs, carries out the administration of our non-profit, and implements our strategic plan. Ariel believes deeply in the democratic potential of community-based ecological restoration and in the power of place-based environmental education. He is a graduate of UC Berkeley’s College of Natural Resources. Before joining San Bruno Mountain Watch in 2015, Ariel worked with the Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy’s Park Stewardship Program.

name: Out for Equality
mission: Out For Equality ensures the human rights of LGBTQ+ people by providing strategy and support to grassroots LGBTQ+ organizations and activists around the world.
ntee_code: R12 - Fund Raising and/or Fund Distribution

programs.name: Astitva
programs.description:
Empowering the transgender community through livelihood support, health support and advocacy for legal rights.

​The transgender community in India (also known as hijras), which is estimated to be over 500,000 is among the most vulnerable, most abused and the least understood populations in that country. Started by Sarita Shukla and operating with Pahal - Nurturing Lives, Astitva works to uplift this community through entrepreneurship development, livelihood exchange, insuring access to public health facilities, and working to help the transgender community achieve legal rights and social acceptance.

programs.name: Gays & Lesbians Accepted in Society (GLAS)
programs.description: Bringing forth a positive change to the lives of the lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender people in Bulgaria and eastern Europe, guaranteeing them full equality and protection from all forms of discrimination. The organization’s goal is the complete inclusion of LGBTQIA+ people in all aspects of life and society. The main focus is on working with parents of LGBTQIA+ people, creating an integrated work environment and campaigning against homophobic hate crimes, as well as promoting tolerance.

programs.name: Lakshya Trust
programs.description: Working to improve the lives of Gay, Bisexual, Transgender/Hijra and Koti minority groups and communities. With a main focus on cultural, social, spiritual, physical and mental health of all sexual minority groups, the organization works on various issues addressing and advocating the social, economic, legal, psychological, spiritual and health aspects of sexual minorities.

programs.name: QueerInk
programs.description:
Telling queer stories by queer Indians. It is estimated that at least 90 million Indians may be LGBTHQIA+. 90 million persons, a large percentage unaware who they are nor do they have the means to empower themselves to live their true selves openly. Each of the 90 million have family who need to be empowered with information to support them. 

The QueerInk project records the lived experiences of LGBTHQIA+ Indians through oral histories and digital reproductions of significant artifacts. Queer Ink places queer histories as part of Indian history.

programs.name: HIV/AIDS Testing & Prevention
programs.description: Supporting quality health education, as well as combating the stereotypes and prejudices that surround the HIV virus amongst not only Bulgarian society at large, but the group of men, who have sex with men – the group that is most vulnerable towards infections. Through a series of focused campaigns and organized support groups, the foundation seeks to stimulate regular HIV/AIDS testing, as well as to provide information concerning the latest methods used to prevent and fight the virus with the help and collaboration of partners and health organizations.

programs.name: Support of LGBTQIA+ people in Uganda
programs.description:
The current situation for LBGTQIA+ people in Uganda is dire. The Anti-Homosexuality Act 2023 signed by the Ugandan President has criminalized any form of housing, expression, association, or support for LGBT+ people, putting their lives and rights at risk. Penalties from this law expand to impose draconian penalties on allies. For example, Landlords who knowingly rent premises to gay people risk going to prison for seven years. This is creating widespread violence against people suspected of being gay and trans, and many suspected of being gay are being evicted by their landlords and reported by their neighbors.

Out For Equality is working with partners on the ground in Uganda and around the world to provide immediate assistance to LGBTQIA+ individuals fleeing persecution. We are working with the only LGBTQIA+ Shelter in Kampala, providing individuals with financial assistance for food and immediate needs, and Out for Equality is assisting people to secure documents to legally lea

leader.name: Brian Rusch
leader.profile:
Brian Rusch is a humanitarian, peace leader, and storyteller who regularly consults in the areas of human rights and diversity, equity and inclusion. With a client base made up of nonprofit organizations, governments, corporations and celebrities, Brian helps them strategize how they can best optimize their platforms to be change makers for good. Expanding on his global humanitarian efforts, in 2022, he launched Out For Equality.

Brian has run foundations for Nobel Peace laureates Desmond Tutu and the Dalai Lama. He continues his work with the Nobel Laureates as a strategic consultant for Kailash Satyarthi and a member of the board of Leymah Gbowee’s foundation. Brian is vice-chair of Rotary International’s DEI task force, responsible for putting together a plan to assess the state of DEI in Rotary and iimplementing that plan amongst its 1.4 million members.

name: California Mountain Biking Coalition
mission: Our mission is to expand and enhance sustainable bike-friendly trails throughout California by leveraging a unifying, statewide voice for mountain bikers and trail stewards.
subsection_description: 501(c)(4) Civic Leagues and Social Welfare Organizations

programs.name: Teen Ambassador Program
programs.description: The California Mountain Bike Coalition launched its Teen Ambassador program in 2023, in partnership with NorCal Interscholastic Cycling League and the SoCal High School Cycling League. This initiative provides a cohort-based internship model for junior and senior high school student-athletes who are interested in building their resumes while riding, connecting, and taking meaningful action with other California-based student-athletes. In 2024 the program will be expanding eligibility to include the Golden State South League and the California-based athletes in the Nevada North League. The ambassadorship is rooted in NICA’s Teen Trail Corps’ SPEAK, SERVE, RIDE, and RESPECT principles and the SoCal League’s WRMB Challenge Values, both of which focus on the non-racing aspects of cycling. The program aims to educate student-athletes about the world of cycling advocacy and inspire a culture of service and personal action. Ambassadors will work alongside our advocacy team and trail partners

programs.name: Outdoor Recreation and Trail Advocacy
programs.description: CAMTB is coalition representing and supporting 41 CA trail advocacy organizations CAMTB is organized to provide a unified statewide voice for organizations and individuals with common interests in improving and increasing trail access and other off-road opportunities for cyclists throughout California; to advocate for improved opportunities to steward, care for, create, and experience California's open spaces; to provide leadership in protection and preservation of the environment by advocating for the development of informed public policy and by encouraging the establishment and management of protected land that will increase and improve off-road cycling opportunities and experiences ; to serve as a platform for California organizations to organize and coordinate their efforts to protect and steward public lands and the trails accessing them, and to ensure these lands and trails can be enjoyed in a meaningful and sustainable manner by the diverse people of California
